live.instructions: Drry runs a coach's community: courses, a member feed, events, email, funnel pages, a website, a store and payments. Start with list_communities; every other tool needs the communityId it returns, and a coach may run more than one. Each family tool takes an `act`; read the act list in its description before calling. For "what needs me" or "how are things going", call community_insight/attention first. For a community still getting started, community_insight/next_step says what to build next. For how the business is doing, community_insight/revenue, community_insight/engagement and community_insight/content_performance give the analytics page's numbers. To build the coach's website: manage_site/read first, then a template or pages, the look, the menu, footer and header, search and sharing, manage_page/preview and manage_page/score on each page, publishing, and the home page (manage_site/set_home). New courses, lessons, guides, pages, forms and emails are drafts; publishing is always a separate act, and several acts email members or go public, so confirm those with the coach in the same turn. A draft nobody has seen can be deleted (never anything published, sent or switched on), and so can a page that is unpublished now and is not the home page; a deleted draft or page cannot be brought back, so confirm with the coach first. Posting and replying in the feed (manage_community) and replying in the coach's own direct messages (manage_messages) speak as the coach and reach members at once, so show the coach the words first. Product, offer, discount code, event ticket and membership-tier prices (manage_product, manage_offer, manage_event/set_price_changes, manage_tier) are live the moment they save (or the moment their window opens) and are charged to strangers' cards, so confirm every amount, code and date with the coach first; people who already paid keep what they pay. Refunds, the community's own single membership price, member removal and role changes, rulings on held or reported posts, and starting a new direct message are the coach's to do in the console. When an answer includes a console link, give it to the coach rather than describing where to click.

tools.name: manage_course
tools.title: Read, build and publish courses
tools.description:
A course, its modules, its lessons and the order a member meets them in. Reading costs nothing and is where to start. Anything you CREATE here lands as a DRAFT nobody can see until you publish it.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One course in full, or every course when courseId is omitted. Start here.
- create_course: A new course. Answers with its courseId AND a first moduleId.
- update_course: Retitle a course, change its subtitle, move it with `position`, set its locked-lesson and quiz wording, or aim `coverFocalPoint` at the subject of its cover photo. It does NOT set the cover colour.
- publish_course: Make a course visible. Queues the new-drops email to every member with access.
- create_module: A second section inside a course.
- update_module: Rename a module, or move it with `position`.
- create_lesson: A lesson inside a module. Needs moduleId.
- write_lesson: Replace a lesson's body, rename it, or move it within its module. This is how you write the actual teaching.
- update_lesson: How a lesson unlocks: drip, a date, or after earlier lessons, plus the quiz pass mark. NOT its title or body.
- move_lesson: Move a lesson to another module or another position.
- publish_lesson: Make one lesson visible. Mails members only once its course is published.
- unpublish_lesson: Take a lesson back out of view. Deletes nothing.
- unpublish_course: Take a whole course back out of view, lessons included. Each lesson keeps its own status, so which were live is not lost, but manage_course/publish_course is NOT a clean undo: it also publishes every draft lesson and emails members again. Deletes nothing.
- set_prerequisites: Which COURSES must be finished before this course opens. For lesson order use manage_course/update_lesson.
- set_quiz: The questions on a quiz lesson, and the score needed to pass.
- delete_course: Delete a DRAFT course no member has ever reached, with its modules and lessons. Refused, with the reason, for anything published or used. Cannot be undone.
- delete_module: Delete a module none of whose lessons was ever published or opened, with its lessons. Cannot be undone.
- delete_lesson: Delete a DRAFT lesson nobody has opened, with its sub-lessons. For a published one use manage_course/unpublish_lesson. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

courseId.description: Omit to list every course with its id.

lessonId.description: One lesson in full, body and quiz questions included. Takes precedence over courseId.

title.description: The course title.

subtitle.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

firstModuleTitle.description: Name of the first module. Defaults to "Module 1".

position.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

lockedMessage.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

quizPassMessage.description: What a member reads after passing a quiz in this course. Send an empty string for the default.

quizFailMessage.description: What a member reads after failing a quiz in this course. Send an empty string for the default.

coverFocalPoint.description: Where the subject of the cover photo is, so the places that show it in a different shape crop around that point instead of the middle. A cover is cropped to 16:9 once, but the home banner is much wider and the teasers are square, so a subject near an edge gets cut off. Send null to go back to the center. Omit to leave it alone. Read manage_course/read first for the framing it has now. A course with NO cover photo is REFUSED rather than quietly accepted, because uploading a cover clears the framing, so anything set beforehand would be discarded by that upload; send null on a coverless course and it is allowed, since clearing is already the state.

x.description: Across the photo. 0 is the left edge, 1 the right.

y.description: Down the photo. 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom.

release.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

releaseDays.description: Days to wait. Required for "days_after_joining" (at least 1). For "after_previous_section", 0 means the moment the previous section is finished.

body.description: Lesson text as simple HTML paragraphs.

releaseDate.description: For "on_a_date": the day it opens, as YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO timestamp. A bare date means midnight UTC of that day.

prerequisiteLessonIds.description: Lessons that must be finished before this one unlocks. They must be in the SAME course; anything else is dropped. Send [] to clear them.

quizPassMark.description: Percentage needed to pass, for a quiz lesson. Default 70.

targetModuleId.description: The section it should end up in, from manage_course/read.

prerequisiteCourseIds.description: Courses that must be finished before this one opens. Send [] to clear them. Omit to leave them alone.

requirePreviousCourse.description: Also require the course immediately above this one in the library, whichever that turns out to be.

delayDays.description: Extra days to wait after a member qualifies. 0 means open it the moment they do.

options.description: The answers to choose from, in the order shown.

correctOptions.description: Which options are correct, as zero-based positions in `options`. One entry makes it single-choice; more than one makes it select-all-that-apply.

questions.description: The whole quiz, in the order members answer it.

passMark.description: Percentage needed to pass. Omit to leave the current mark alone.

tools.name: manage_guide
tools.title: Read, write and publish guides
tools.description:
Guides are the standalone written pieces beside your courses: recipes, protocols, checklists. Built step by step, published when you say so.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One guide in full, or every guide and collection when guideId is omitted.
- create: A new draft guide. Members cannot see it until you publish.
- update: Title, summary, collection and the rest of the header.
- write: Replace the guide's steps. This is the writing itself.
- publish: Make it visible to members, or take it back to a draft. Publishing queues the new-drops email, like any other publish.
- reorder: The order guides appear in. Send every id in the collection.
- share: Turn the public share link on or off.
- save_atom: Save one what-you-need line or one step to the coach's drawer, to reuse in a later guide. Keyed on its name, so a repeat REPLACES.
- saved_pieces: Read that drawer. Console-only; no member sees a saved piece.
- delete: Delete a guide that has never been published. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

guideId.description: Omit to list every guide with its id.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

collectionId.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

intro.description: The opening, as simple HTML paragraphs.

kind.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

coverHue.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

meta.description: The fact chips; send [] to clear them.

label.description: e.g. "Prep time".

type.description: What the value MEANS, so a consumer can find it without the label. Omit for a free-form chip.

heading.description: What the list is called, e.g. "Ingredients".

checkable.description: Whether members can tick items off. On by default.

id.description: The itemId from manage_guide/read. Send it back unchanged: it holds members' ticks. Omit only for a new line.

text.description: The thing itself, e.g. "Olive oil".

quantity.description: Free-form amount, e.g. "2 tbsp" or "to taste".

amount.description: Structured magnitude, for a list a member can scale. Omit if not a number.

category.description: For a merged shopping list, e.g. "Produce". Never shown in the guide.

group.description: In-guide section heading, e.g. "For the sauce".

steps.description: In the order you send them.

id.description: The stepId from manage_guide/read. Send it back unchanged: it holds the step's image or video. Omit only for a new step.

body.description: The step, as simple HTML paragraphs.

notes.description: The closing block, e.g. "Tips", as simple HTML.

published.description: true to publish, false to take it back to a draft.

orderedIds.description: Every guideId, in the order members should see them.

visibility.description: public: anyone with the link reads the whole guide. private: members only. Omit to change only the link name.

slug.description: The link name, 2 to 48 characters of lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Omit to keep the one it has, which is minted from the title the first time it goes public.

label.description: What it is called in the drawer. Defaults to its own text or title.

text.description: The line itself, for kind "need".

body.description: The step words as simple HTML, for kind "step".

tools.name: manage_guide_collection
tools.title: Group guides into collections
tools.description:
A collection is the shelf a guide sits on, and what members browse.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new shelf for guides to sit on, which is what members browse.
- update: Rename it or change its description.
- reorder: The order collections appear in. Send every id.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: What members see.

orderedIds.description: Every collectionId, in the order they should appear.

tools.name: manage_page
tools.title: Read and write funnel and website pages
tools.description:
Public pages built from typed sections: funnel pages, and the pages of the coach's website (manage_site owns the site's menu, footer and header). Draft, read back what was stored, refine, then publish.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One page's sections, or every page when pageId is omitted. Read before every edit.
- create: A new draft FUNNEL page nobody can see (at /p/<slug>), from sections or from a template key. A website page is manage_site/create_page.
- update: Replace the page WHOLE. Compose every section from what read just returned. Every section type is writable, on a funnel page or a website page alike (a website page also takes a freeform layout, its elements placed anywhere on a grid and kept by id (editElements changes some by id and keeps the rest), each with its own style if wanted: text size, weight, spacing and case, a fill, border, corners, shadow, turn and opacity, and a photo's focus and shape, how each element moves (how it arrives as it scrolls into view and after what delay, an effect as the page scrolls, what it does under the pointer, and staying in view while its section scrolls past), and a layer name and groupId for the editor's layers list, so elements sharing a groupId select and move together): the copy blocks, forms (by formId), booking sections (by typeSlug), the LIVE sections that show the community's own courses (courseCatalog, every published one or a picked list of course ids), upcoming public events (eventsList), store products (productGrid, every listed one or a picked list of product ids) and one of the website's collections (collection, by collectionId from manage_collection/list, with a layout, an order, a tag to show only and a count; adding one, or a button that opens a popup: Available on the Creator plan, while one a page already holds keeps saving), each read when the page renders and only what a stranger may see, link lists, announcement bars, stats, marquees, social feeds, Latest posts from the blog (the newest, one category's or author's, or picked posts by id), profile headers, video links, image, gallery, logo and before-and-after blocks, pricing tables and the designer's saved layouts the templates are built from. Every photo slot takes a photo from the stock library (manage_page/stock_photos), one the page already holds, or one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos, or a new one from manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link); a photo or video the coach uploaded is kept when its section's id is copied back (a gallery's or logo row's by the photo number read prints), and no other file of theirs (a lesson video, a resource) is ever taken. On a plan with custom code (every plan today) a custom code block is written and edited here too, its name, HTML, CSS, JavaScript and slot values, and whether it runs in its own frame or is drawn into the page (render inline, only with no script: sanitized, read by search, and able to mount a real form or booking picker where a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot sits; otherwise stack a custom block, a form or booking section and another custom block, never a form built in HTML), and any section's own CSS (customCss); the retired email box is edited, never added. Every button's style and destination is part of its section (on a pricing table, of its tier; on a link list, of its button), and so are each section's alignment, spacing (or its own space above and below and its widest, in pixels; on a two-column section the column split and what a phone shows first), background tone, custom colours, colour fade, hidden flag, which screens it shows on (every screen, desktop only or phones only), how it arrives as it scrolls into view (a curated entrance: a quiet rise, none, fade, slide from the left or right, zoom, or its items one after another; never on a hero or a sticky bar), the focal point that keeps each photo's crop on what matters, and its own variants, so they are read and written here too. Also lays a template over a DRAFT page, moves the page to a new address, shows or hides its header, and sets the page's own button style, fonts (headings, body, and a label font for eyebrows, buttons and the header navigation), colours, header button, footer, social links and search title and description, whether search engines may list it, the picture a shared link to it shows (a stock photo or one of the community's uploaded page photos), and who can see a WEBSITE page (pageSettings.audience: everyone, members only, with tierId members on one tier and up, or anyone with the password, set with a write-only pageSettings.password that is never shown back; the home page stays public).
- layouts: The designer's saved layouts a section can use, by category; with a comp key, that design's slots, caps, repeating items and buttons, plus a blank section to fill.
- templates: The finished funnel page templates, by what the page is for, with the key create and update take to start a page from one.
- stock_photos: Drry's own stock photos, the same ones the page editor's Choose from stock offers: the set the templates ship with, then the stock library's page photos this community may pick now. Each with the key a photo slot takes, its shape, mood, the kinds of coach it suits, whether it shows people, its search words and what it shows; narrowed by query, niche and shape, at most limit of them. A profile photo or a testimonial's photo takes none (it stands for a real person). Ends with any photo the coach uploaded in the last hour that no page shows yet.
- upload_photo: Store ONE new photo in the community's storage for its pages, from a public address (url, fetched by Drry) or the picture's bytes (data, base64), and get the imageKey a photo slot takes. JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, judged from the bytes; counted against the plan's storage; the same picture again is not stored twice. For several photos with addresses, use manage_page/upload_photos instead. Place it soon: one no page shows is removed once it is an hour old, the next time a photo is added through an assistant or any page is saved, unless sent with keep: true, which holds it for 30 days.
- upload_photos: Store up to 20 photos from public addresses (urls) in ONE call, fetched and checked exactly as manage_page/upload_photo's url is, 4 at a time; per address, in the order sent, its imageKey or why it was not stored, so one bad address never fails the others. Storage is decided photo by photo: once the plan's storage refuses one, the rest are not fetched and what was stored stays. The way to bring in many photos, rather than one call each or base64. keep: true holds the unplaced ones for 30 days instead of an hour.
- photo_upload_link: A one-time, 30-minute link to a Drry page where the connected coach drops ONE photo from their device, for a photo you cannot send yourself (one attached in the chat). Returns the link and an uploadId for manage_page/uploaded_photos. keep: true holds that photo for 30 days if no page shows it yet.
- uploaded_photos: The community's own uploaded page photos, newest first (the page editor's Your photos), each with its imageKey, when it arrived, whether a page shows it yet and, for one no page shows, when it will be removed (an hour after it arrived, or the end of its 30 days when uploaded with keep); with uploadId, whether the coach has added that upload link's photo.
- edit_section: Rewrite ONE section by its id, leaving every other section exactly as stored. Send the section whole, as update takes it: its words are replaced by what is sent, while style settings, links, photos and videos left out carry over. The cheap way to change one block, and it works beside sections update cannot write (except a custom block off a plan with custom code, which blocks every save of its page until it is removed).
- insert_section: Add ONE new section at a position (the bottom when none is given).
- move_section: Move ONE section to a new position. Nothing else changes.
- duplicate_section: Copy ONE section to just below itself, with a fresh id to edit separately.
- remove_section: Remove ONE section. Refused for a section holding the coach's own photo or video, or one another button points at.
- customize_layout: Customize layout on ONE section of a WEBSITE page: the house section becomes a freeform layout holding the same words, photos and buttons as elements that move one by one, keeping its id and a phone layout; the answer names what did not carry over. One-way but for the page's history; live sections, page chrome and designed sections stay as they are.
- score: Check the page against a checklist that needs no traffic (headline, buttons, proof, readable colours, placeholders and fill-in text, search title, and words hidden inside custom code), 0 to 100, never Strong while fill-in text is left, with what to fix and the section it is in; a website page leaves out the sales checks.
- preview: Screenshots of the page as a visitor sees it, desktop, phone or both, a draft too; a whole page in screens, or one section. A custom block without a script is drawn from its HTML and CSS; one with a script shows as a placeholder, so it also gives a private link to the page as saved, drafts included, that anyone holding it can open for one hour without signing in, scripts running.
- history: The page's earlier versions, newest first, each the page as it stood before a change (who, when, through the console or an assistant); with a versionId, that version's sections and what restoring it would change.
- copy_section: Copy ONE section into the page as it is now, beside what is there: from an earlier version (versionId, manage_page/history), from the page in a website restore point (restorePointId, manage_site/history), or from another page of this community as it stands (fromPageId, with index for where it goes). Photos and videos come with it. The page as it was is kept first, so it can be undone.
- saved_sections: The sections this community saved for reuse (the editor's "Your saved sections"), each with its id and any page it cannot go on and why; with savedSectionId, one in full.
- save_section: Keep ONE of a page's sections, as stored, for reuse on any page of the community, under a name (its heading when none is given). The page does not change.
- insert_saved_section: Drop a fresh copy of a saved section into a page at a position (the bottom when none is given), with its own id; kept in the page's history.
- rename_saved_section: Give a saved section a new name. Pages using a copy do not change.
- restore: Put an earlier version back (name, sections, design, header; never the address or whether it is published). The page as it is now is kept first, so a restore can be undone.
- publish: Put a funnel or website page live at its address, or take one down. Search engines may index it unless it is hidden from search (pageSettings noindex), members only or behind a password.
- delete: Delete a page that is unpublished now (a draft, or one taken down, whatever it was before) and is not the home page, unless a published page, a live popup or anything else still sends people to it. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

pageId.description: Omit to list every page with its id.

title.description: What the coach will see in their list of pages.

slug.description: The URL segment, lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens: the page lives at /p/<slug>.

sections.description: The page, top to bottom; or leave it out and send `template`. Section ids are minted here, so any id you send is ignored. Sections take an optional align (default, left, center, right; default keeps the section's own alignment) except these types: announcement, logos, profileHeader, form, stickyCta, linkList, marquee, custom, freeform; an optional spacing (normal, compact, roomy) except: announcement, stickyCta, custom; and an optional bgTone (default, tint, inverted, accent) except: announcement, ctaBanner, hero, stickyCta. The page does not render those there, so they are refused there. A sticky call to action is a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen and takes none of the three. manage_page/read prints each one that is set. Every section also takes hidden (true keeps it in the editor and off the live page) and three custom colours, bgColor, accentColor and textColor (each "#rrggbb", or "" to follow the theme). Every section but a sticky call to action and a saved layout takes a colour fade behind it, bgGradient ({from, to, angle}, the angle 0 to 360 with 180 pointing down; null removes it), a background photo, bgImageKey, and while it holds one, bgOverlay, the shade over that photo (dark, darker, light, none; dark is the default), and bgMotion, how it moves as the page scrolls (none, the default; parallax; slowZoom; a visitor who asks for less motion sees it still). A section the read prints with bgVideo true holds a looping background video the coach uploaded in the page editor (videos are never uploaded here): it covers any photo or fade, takes bgOverlay and bgMotion like a photo, is kept while bgVideo is left out or sent as true with the section's id, and bgVideo null takes it off (the page's history keeps it, so it can be restored). A PHOTO SLOT (bgImageKey, a hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageKey, a before-and-after's beforeKey and afterKey, a gallery or logo row item's imageKey, a saved layout's or a custom block's image slot) takes a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos, like "stock:cover-coastline", a photo this page already holds, one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos; add a new one with manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link), or "" for none; never any other file. Videos are uploaded in the page editor, and every photo and video a section holds is kept when its id is copied back and the slot is left out (a gallery or logo row item's by the photo number manage_page/read printed beside it; a testimonial's while it keeps a name no other testimonial has). A profile header's avatar and a testimonial's photo are a person, so they are uploaded only. A hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageStyle, imageFinish, imageAspect and imageAlt, and an image section's imageLayout and caption, apply only while it holds an image, and so does a hero's or an image-and-text block's imageLayout ("bleed" runs a split photo to the screen edge). A hero and a cta banner take secondaryCta ({label, link, style}), a quieter second button beside the first, and an image-and-text block takes the hero's ctaLabel, ctaLink, ctaStyle and buttons for a button under its words. A form section's formId and a booking section's typeSlug are checked against what this community has. A custom code block (a plan with custom code) takes label, html, css and js, the code running sandboxed on the page, render (frame, the default, or inline: a block with no js drawn into the page through a sanitizer, so search reads its words), and fields, the values of the typed slots its html declares as {{type:key}} (text, markdown, link as a destination object, date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM, datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, image, and in an inline block form, a form id, and booking, a session type's slug, each mounting the real widget there), a patch where "" clears one; left out on a block whose id you copied back, each keeps what it has. THE COACH EDITS EVERY SLOT in the page editor's Content panel as a plain field, without touching code, and copy written straight into the html can only be changed in the code editor. So write each heading, paragraph, photo and button destination a coach would change as a slot ({{text:headline}}, , ) with its value in fields, and keep only structure and design in the html; a write's answer names any block whose copy or photos are fixed in the html. Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. Every section takes device (all, the default; desktop, hidden on phones; or phone, hidden on larger screens). Every section but a hero and a sticky call to action takes entrance, how it arrives as it scrolls into view: default (a quiet rise), none, fade, slideLeft, slideRight, zoom, or stagger (its items one after another, only on a section with items: value props, testimonials, stats, logos, steps, pricing, gallery, FAQ, link list and the four live sections). A FOCAL POINT, {x, y} in whole percentages from the left and the top (null is the centre), keeps the crop on what matters: imageFocus beside a hero's, an image-and-text block's, an image section's or a profile header's photo, bgImageFocus beside bgImageKey, a gallery item's focus, and a before-and-after's beforeFocus and afterFocus; each only while that photo is there, and a new photo starts centred. Beside each focal point the same photo takes an EDIT (imageEdit, bgImageEdit, a gallery item's edit, beforeEdit and afterEdit, and a freeform photo's style.edit): crop {x, y, w, h} in fractions of the turned photo (three decimals, w and h at least 0.1, inside the photo), turn 90, 180 or 270 clockwise, flip h or v (of the turned photo), adjust {brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth} each a whole number from -100 to 100, and filter (mono, sepia, fade, vivid, cool, warm); null removes it, left out it is kept while the photo stays, and a new photo starts unedited. A freeform photo's edit lives in its style, so it follows the style: a sent style replaces it whole (leave edit out of it to remove the edit), and a style left out keeps the edit while the photo stays. A built-in template photo (a stock key without "lib/") takes adjust and filter only: crop, turn and flip need an uploaded photo or a library photo. Every section but an announcement bar, a sticky call to action, a custom code block and a freeform layout takes exact space in whole pixels, padTop and padBottom (0 to 320), and maxWidth, the widest its content runs (360 to 1600); null clears one back to the section's own. Sent to one of those four, they are left out and the answer says so, rather than refusing the write. The same sections, and a freeform layout too, take dividers, a shape over the section's top and bottom edges, {top, bottom}, each {shape, height, flip, color} or null: shape one of wave, curve, tilt, triangle, zigzag, arch, cloud, drip; height sm, md (the default) or lg; flip true mirrors it; color a theme token (foreground, muted, accent, background) or "#rrggbb", left out to take the colour of the section next to it; dividers null removes both, and dividers left out keeps them. A section drawn as a photo beside words (an image-and-text block in its beside layout, or a hero in its split or splitLeft layout) also takes split, the left column's share of the row in whole percent (25 to 75), and phoneOrder, what a phone shows first where the columns stack: auto (as designed), photo, words, or hidePhoto. Every section but a sticky call to action takes customCss (a plan with custom code), the section's own CSS written as usual (h1 { letter-spacing: -0.02em; }): it applies to that section only, a url() must be https, and @import or a < is refused; "" clears it. Its rules WIN over the house styles inside the section, whatever their specificity (h2 { font-weight: 400; color: #333; } beats the bold headline and the Text colour). words.description: Short words or phrases that drift across the band, one each.

style.description: primary (a filled pill, for the one thing that matters most) or card (a quiet bordered row, the default for a new button).

source.description: all (the default: every published course a visitor may see, in the coach's own order, cut at `count`) or picked (exactly the courses in `courseIds`, in that order).

courseIds.description: The courses a picked section shows, in order, by id (manage_course/list prints them). A draft is accepted and shows once published. Kept when `source` is all, so switching back restores the list. A course locked to a membership tier shows locked, naming the tier; a hidden one never shows.

count.description: How many courses on all, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 6). A picked list is not cut by it.

layout.description: grid (the default, covers) or list (compact rows).

count.description: How many upcoming events, soonest first, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 3). Only events open to anyone with their public page on are listed; members-only, invite-only and tier-limited events never are.

layout.description: cards (the default, with covers) or list (compact rows with the date).

source.description: all (the default: every product the store sells and lists, newest first, cut at `count`) or picked (exactly the products in `productIds`, in that order).

productIds.description: The products a picked section shows, in order, by id (list_catalog/products prints them). Only a product on sale can be picked; one hidden from the store shows nothing. Kept when `source` is all.

count.description: How many products on all, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 6). A picked list is not cut by it.

layout.description: grid (the default, product shots) or list (compact rows).

collectionId.description: The website collection it shows (manage_collection/list prints each collectionId): its LIVE items only, read when the page renders. Left out on a new section, it shows nothing until one is set.

layout.description: grid (the default, cards), list (compact rows) or carousel (a row that scrolls sideways).

sort.description: manual (the default: the collection's own order), newest, oldest (by the item's first date, else when it was made) or title (A to Z).

tag.description: Show only items carrying this tag (any case); "" for every item.

count.description: How many items, 1 to 24 (a new section shows 6).

showLink.description: false hides the "See all" link to the collection's own page (shown by default, and only when its items have pages).

platform.description: instagram (the default), tiktok or youtube: the platform a bare post id is on. It does not limit the section: a link names its own platform, so one feed can mix Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Changing it keeps every post the section already holds on its own platform.

posts.description: The coach's own posts, embedded on the page, in order: each a post's full link (instagram.com/p/... or /reel/..., tiktok.com/@name/video/..., youtube.com/shorts/...) or the id manage_page/read printed (a post on another platform than the section's prints as tiktok:<id> or youtube:<id>; send it back as printed). A TikTok short share link cannot be read; send the full address. A YouTube link must be the Short's own youtube.com/shorts/ address: youtu.be, watch?v= and embed links can be regular videos, which are refused and belong in a video section.

postSize.description: standard (the default, three across on a wide screen) or large (two across, bigger).

mobileLayout.description: stack (the default, one under another on a phone) or swipe (one sideways row a visitor swipes through on a phone).

socials.description: The social icons under the name, as a PATCH: each network's full http(s) profile link, "" to hide that icon, and a network left out keeps what it has. The avatar is a photo, added in the funnel editor; without one the page shows the name's initial.

url.description: A YouTube or Vimeo link (an unlisted one included), embedded on the page. "" takes it off. An uploaded video is added in the funnel editor, never here, and one the section holds is kept when its id comes back.

source.description: Which the section shows: embed (the link) or native (the video uploaded in the page editor). A section sent a url and no source shows the link. Switching a section that holds an uploaded video to embed would delete that upload, so it is refused here.

imageLayout.description: How wide the photo sits: contained (the default, the reading column), wide or fullBleed (edge to edge).

caption.description: A short line under the photo.

layout.description: grid (the default), carousel (a swipeable slider), masonry (a staggered collage) or strip (the photos drifting slowly across the page).

animation.description: A carousel's transition: slide (the default), fade, rotate3d or coverflow. Only on a carousel.

autoplay.description: true advances a carousel on its own. Only on a carousel.

columns.description: How many columns a grid or masonry uses: "auto" (the default, from the photo count), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a carousel.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: What the photo shows, for screen readers.

layout.description: grid (the default) or marquee, the logos drifting slowly across the page.

columns.description: "auto" (the default), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a marquee.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: The brand or publication the logo stands for.

style.description: slider (the default, a draggable split), sideBySide or toggle (tap to swap).

beforeLabel.description: The corner label on the first photo; "" hides it.

afterLabel.description: The corner label on the second photo; "" hides it.

layout.description: centered (the default) or bar, a compact strip that shows no subtext.

subtext.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

proof.description: A reassuring line under the form.

successBody.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. collectName.description: true adds a name field before the email.

nameRequired.description: true makes that name field required. Only with collectName.

redirectUrl.description: Where a visitor goes after signing up: a path on this site like "/p/thanks", or an https address. "" shows the success message instead.

welcomeEmailId.description: A saved email sent to each new signup, by id (manage_email/read lists them). "" sends nothing.

listId.description: A contact list each signup is added to, by id. "" adds them to none (they are still captured as a contact).

width.description: contained (the default, a centred column) or full (edge to edge).

grid.description: standard (the default: 24 columns of 24px rows on desktop and tablet, 8 on a phone) or fine (48 columns of 12px rows, 16 on a phone), and every place in this section is on it. Switching moves every place the section keeps onto the new grid: to fine exactly (each number doubled), back to standard rounded to the nearest cell, and the answer says what rounded. minRows.description: The section's least height in grid rows (default 12, at most 200 on the standard grid and 400 on the fine one); content taller than it grows it.

name.description: The element's name in the editor's layers list, for the coach only: it is never drawn on the page. "" takes it off, and the list names the element from what it shows.

groupId.description: Elements sharing a groupId (any short word, like "hero-copy") are one group in the editor: they select and move together. A group needs two or more elements. null takes this element out of its group.

padding.description: Text only: space inside the box, in px.

rotation.description: Turned by this many degrees, either way.

edit.description: Image only: the photo's crop, turn, flip, adjust and filter, as a section photo's edit takes them. Left out, none.

mask.description: Image only: a shape the photo is cut to. It takes the place of the corners.

enter.description: How it arrives as it scrolls into view: rise, fade, slideLeft (in from the left), slideRight (in from the right) or zoom. Left out, it is simply there. Left out it keeps what is stored; null (or never set) means tablets show the desktop layout. An element it does not place sits under the tablet layout.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", which is the default and follows the page's own button style, which follows the community-wide one that manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS. The FILL is the exception: on these sections it is the section's own `ctaStyle` field (solid, outline or ghost) that the page renders from, so a `fill` here other than "auto" is REFUSED rather than stored, and the refusal says to send `ctaStyle` instead.

label.description: The block's name in the section list, for the coach only.

html.description: Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. With render inline (and no js) it can hold two NATIVE WIDGET slots that mount the real thing at that spot, inside the block's own layout: {{form:<key>}}, a form from the forms builder, and {{booking:<key>}}, a session type's booking picker. Which one: the slot's value in fields when set (a form id from list_catalog/forms, a session type's slug), else the key itself, so {{form:<form id>}} and {{booking:intro-call}} need no field. Each must sit in a <div>, a <section>, a list item or a table cell, never inside a paragraph, a heading or a link, and the form must be published for the page to publish. To put a real form beside a custom design otherwise, stack the sections: a custom block, then a form or booking section (style it with its customCss), then another custom block. Never build a form in the html: it submits nowhere, and the sanitizer removes it.

css.description: The block's own styles. Drawn inline, every rule is scoped to the block (html, body and :root mean the block itself; a rule reaching the block's siblings is dropped), and a sheet with a < character, a url() that is not https, or a script address is left out whole; an @import is removed (the page's own fonts apply). A native widget a slot mounts sits in a <div data-drry-widget="form"> or "booking" the styles can select.

js.description: Inline code only: the sandbox blocks external scripts and network calls. A block with any script always runs in its own frame, whatever render says.

render.description: How the block draws. "frame" (the default, and what a block left out of this field keeps) runs it sandboxed in its own frame, script included, where search does not read it. "inline" draws a block with NO script straight into the page so search engines read its words, after a strict sanitizer: no script, no event handler (onclick and every other on attribute), no javascript: or data: address, no data-* attribute, no frame, form, input, button, object, embed, base, meta, link or style tag; links must be https, a /path on this site, a #part, mailto: or tel:; pictures and videos https or a photo of this site; an inline style keeps only declarations that load nothing else. The write answer names what it removed. Only an inline block can hold a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot.

On a section whose id you copied back, leaving this out keeps where the button goes now.

fill.description: A shape's colour, and a BUTTON's own colour: a solid button's background. Left out, a button is drawn in the page's ink (foreground), so the section's accentColor does not recolour it; send accent to follow the accent, or #rrggbb. A button's label colour is color.

size.description: Text only. A step on the scale (xs 12px, sm 14px, base 16px, lg 18px, xl 20px, 2xl 24px, 3xl 30px, 4xl 36px, 5xl 48px, 6xl 60px, 7xl 72px), which follows the site, or an exact size in px (10 to 160). A large size draws smaller on a phone.

lineHeight.description: Text only. Unitless, 0.8 to 2.5, stored in steps of 0.05.

letterSpacing.description: Text only. In em, -0.1 to 0.5, stored in steps of 0.01.

textCase.description: Text only. Left out, the letters are as typed.

fill.description: Text only: a box filled behind the words, which they are then checked against.

opacity.description: In percent. Left out, fully opaque.

border.description: Text, image and shape. Width in px.

style.description: solid (the default), dashed or dotted.

color.description: Left out, foreground.

radius.description: Text, image and shape: corner rounding in px, one number for all four or each corner (tl, tr, br, bl). It takes the place of the element's own radius.

shadow.description: Text, image and shape: the house elevations, lowest first.

padding.description: Text only: space inside the box, in px.

rotation.description: Turned by this many degrees, either way.

focus.description: Image only: the point kept in view when the photo is cropped, in percent. Left out, the centre.

edit.description: Image only: the photo's crop, turn, flip, adjust and filter, as a section photo's edit takes them. Left out, none.

mask.description: Image only: a shape the photo is cut to. It takes the place of the corners.

style.description: The element's own style. Left out, the element keeps the style it has; sent, it REPLACES that style whole; null puts it back to the site style. Each kind takes only some fields (named on each). Colour, alignment, a shape's fill and a photo's fit stay on the element itself, beside its style, not in it. A text colour that would not read on what it sits on (below 4.5 to 1) is drawn in a readable shade of it on the page, and manage_page/read says so.

enter.description: How it arrives as it scrolls into view: rise, fade, slideLeft (in from the left), slideRight (in from the right) or zoom. Left out, it is simply there. One already on screen when the page opens is never hidden, and a section whose elements arrive on their own takes no section entrance.

delay.description: With enter only: wait this many tenths of a second before it arrives.

scroll.description: An effect tied to scrolling: parallaxSlow or parallaxFast (it drifts against the page), fadeIn, riseIn or scaleIn (each done once it is fully on screen), or fadeOut (as it leaves the top). At most 12 elements in a section. A browser without scroll-driven animations shows it still.

hover.description: Under the pointer, on screens that have one: lift, grow, shadow, tint (the brand colour: over a photo or a shape, or as the ink of a text or an icon) or dim (it fades back). Each kind takes only some: text lift, grow, shadow, tint; image lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; button lift, grow, shadow; shape lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; line lift, grow, dim; icon lift, grow, tint, dim. A text tint that would not read on what it sits on is left off the page, and manage_page/read says so.

pin.description: top: it stays in view below the header while the rest of its section scrolls past, on larger screens. On a phone it sits where it was placed.

motion.description: How the element moves. Left out, it keeps the motion it has; sent, it REPLACES that motion whole; null makes it still. A visitor who asks their device for less motion sees it still whatever is set.

tablet.description: The tablet layout (screens 768 to 1023px wide): a place for each element on the same grid as desktop (24 columns, 48 on the fine grid), keyed by element id like mobile. Left out it keeps what is stored; null (or never set) means tablets show the desktop layout. An element it does not place sits under the tablet layout.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", which is the default and follows the page's own button style, which follows the community-wide one that manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS. The FILL is the exception: on these sections it is the section's own `ctaStyle` field (solid, outline or ghost) that the page renders from, so a `fill` here other than "auto" is REFUSED rather than stored, and the refusal says to send `ctaStyle` instead.

label.description: The block's name in the section list, for the coach only.

html.description: Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. With render inline (and no js) it can hold two NATIVE WIDGET slots that mount the real thing at that spot, inside the block's own layout: {{form:<key>}}, a form from the forms builder, and {{booking:<key>}}, a session type's booking picker. Which one: the slot's value in fields when set (a form id from list_catalog/forms, a session type's slug), else the key itself, so {{form:<form id>}} and {{booking:intro-call}} need no field. Each must sit in a <div>, a <section>, a list item or a table cell, never inside a paragraph, a heading or a link, and the form must be published for the page to publish. To put a real form beside a custom design otherwise, stack the sections: a custom block, then a form or booking section (style it with its customCss), then another custom block. Never build a form in the html: it submits nowhere, and the sanitizer removes it.

css.description: The block's own styles. Drawn inline, every rule is scoped to the block (html, body and :root mean the block itself; a rule reaching the block's siblings is dropped), and a sheet with a < character, a url() that is not https, or a script address is left out whole; an @import is removed (the page's own fonts apply). A native widget a slot mounts sits in a <div data-drry-widget="form"> or "booking" the styles can select.

js.description: Inline code only: the sandbox blocks external scripts and network calls. A block with any script always runs in its own frame, whatever render says.

render.description: How the block draws. "frame" (the default, and what a block left out of this field keeps) runs it sandboxed in its own frame, script included, where search does not read it. "inline" draws a block with NO script straight into the page so search engines read its words, after a strict sanitizer: no script, no event handler (onclick and every other on attribute), no javascript: or data: address, no data-* attribute, no frame, form, input, button, object, embed, base, meta, link or style tag; links must be https, a /path on this site, a #part, mailto: or tel:; pictures and videos https or a photo of this site; an inline style keeps only declarations that load nothing else. The write answer names what it removed. Only an inline block can hold a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot.

anyOf.description: Where the button goes. join (the default) is the community's join or checkout page. The others take one more field each: page takes `slug` (another funnel page), surface takes `surface` (library, community, audio, events), course takes `courseId`, paymentLink and offer take `token`, product takes `slug` and an optional `buyHere` (true opens the buy sheet on the published page, in a designed section too; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the product's page), anchor takes `sectionId` (a section on this page whose id manage_page/read printed), booking takes `typeSlug` ("" for the page listing every session type) and an optional `buyHere` (true opens that session's time picker in a sheet on the published page; refused with the "" listing; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the page), form takes `slug` (a published form, /f/<slug>), event takes `id` (an event whose public page is on, /e/<id>), guide takes `slug` (a public guide's share slug, /g/<slug>), store takes nothing else (the published store), blog takes nothing else (the blog's front page, /blog, which follows the blog's own address), blogPost takes `postId` (a published post's id from manage_blog/read; /blog/post/<id> forwards to the post's current link, so a renamed post or blog still lands), external takes an https `url`. Both blog kinds need the blog switched on. popup takes `popupId` (a LIVE popup from manage_site/popups; website pages only: the button opens the popup over the page). A destination this community does not have (or a single-use payment link, or this same page) is refused, and the refusal lists the ones it has; one the page already points at is kept as it is. On a section whose id you copied back, leaving this out keeps where the button goes now.

section.description: The section, whole: its type and its fields. Sections take an optional align (default, left, center, right; default keeps the section's own alignment) except these types: announcement, logos, profileHeader, form, stickyCta, linkList, marquee, custom, freeform; an optional spacing (normal, compact, roomy) except: announcement, stickyCta, custom; and an optional bgTone (default, tint, inverted, accent) except: announcement, ctaBanner, hero, stickyCta. The page does not render those there, so they are refused there. A sticky call to action is a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen and takes none of the three. manage_page/read prints each one that is set. Every section also takes hidden (true keeps it in the editor and off the live page) and three custom colours, bgColor, accentColor and textColor (each "#rrggbb", or "" to follow the theme). Every section but a sticky call to action and a saved layout takes a colour fade behind it, bgGradient ({from, to, angle}, the angle 0 to 360 with 180 pointing down; null removes it), a background photo, bgImageKey, and while it holds one, bgOverlay, the shade over that photo (dark, darker, light, none; dark is the default), and bgMotion, how it moves as the page scrolls (none, the default; parallax; slowZoom; a visitor who asks for less motion sees it still). A section the read prints with bgVideo true holds a looping background video the coach uploaded in the page editor (videos are never uploaded here): it covers any photo or fade, takes bgOverlay and bgMotion like a photo, is kept while bgVideo is left out or sent as true with the section's id, and bgVideo null takes it off (the page's history keeps it, so it can be restored). A PHOTO SLOT (bgImageKey, a hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageKey, a before-and-after's beforeKey and afterKey, a gallery or logo row item's imageKey, a saved layout's or a custom block's image slot) takes a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos, like "stock:cover-coastline", a photo this page already holds, one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos; add a new one with manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link), or "" for none; never any other file. Videos are uploaded in the page editor, and every photo and video a section holds is kept when its id is copied back and the slot is left out (a gallery or logo row item's by the photo number manage_page/read printed beside it; a testimonial's while it keeps a name no other testimonial has). A profile header's avatar and a testimonial's photo are a person, so they are uploaded only. A hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageStyle, imageFinish, imageAspect and imageAlt, and an image section's imageLayout and caption, apply only while it holds an image, and so does a hero's or an image-and-text block's imageLayout ("bleed" runs a split photo to the screen edge). A hero and a cta banner take secondaryCta ({label, link, style}), a quieter second button beside the first, and an image-and-text block takes the hero's ctaLabel, ctaLink, ctaStyle and buttons for a button under its words. A form section's formId and a booking section's typeSlug are checked against what this community has. A custom code block (a plan with custom code) takes label, html, css and js, the code running sandboxed on the page, render (frame, the default, or inline: a block with no js drawn into the page through a sanitizer, so search reads its words), and fields, the values of the typed slots its html declares as {{type:key}} (text, markdown, link as a destination object, date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM, datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, image, and in an inline block form, a form id, and booking, a session type's slug, each mounting the real widget there), a patch where "" clears one; left out on a block whose id you copied back, each keeps what it has. THE COACH EDITS EVERY SLOT in the page editor's Content panel as a plain field, without touching code, and copy written straight into the html can only be changed in the code editor. So write each heading, paragraph, photo and button destination a coach would change as a slot ({{text:headline}}, , ) with its value in fields, and keep only structure and design in the html; a write's answer names any block whose copy or photos are fixed in the html. Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. Every section takes device (all, the default; desktop, hidden on phones; or phone, hidden on larger screens). Every section but a hero and a sticky call to action takes entrance, how it arrives as it scrolls into view: default (a quiet rise), none, fade, slideLeft, slideRight, zoom, or stagger (its items one after another, only on a section with items: value props, testimonials, stats, logos, steps, pricing, gallery, FAQ, link list and the four live sections). A FOCAL POINT, {x, y} in whole percentages from the left and the top (null is the centre), keeps the crop on what matters: imageFocus beside a hero's, an image-and-text block's, an image section's or a profile header's photo, bgImageFocus beside bgImageKey, a gallery item's focus, and a before-and-after's beforeFocus and afterFocus; each only while that photo is there, and a new photo starts centred. Beside each focal point the same photo takes an EDIT (imageEdit, bgImageEdit, a gallery item's edit, beforeEdit and afterEdit, and a freeform photo's style.edit): crop {x, y, w, h} in fractions of the turned photo (three decimals, w and h at least 0.1, inside the photo), turn 90, 180 or 270 clockwise, flip h or v (of the turned photo), adjust {brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth} each a whole number from -100 to 100, and filter (mono, sepia, fade, vivid, cool, warm); null removes it, left out it is kept while the photo stays, and a new photo starts unedited. A freeform photo's edit lives in its style, so it follows the style: a sent style replaces it whole (leave edit out of it to remove the edit), and a style left out keeps the edit while the photo stays. A built-in template photo (a stock key without "lib/") takes adjust and filter only: crop, turn and flip need an uploaded photo or a library photo. Every section but an announcement bar, a sticky call to action, a custom code block and a freeform layout takes exact space in whole pixels, padTop and padBottom (0 to 320), and maxWidth, the widest its content runs (360 to 1600); null clears one back to the section's own. Sent to one of those four, they are left out and the answer says so, rather than refusing the write. The same sections, and a freeform layout too, take dividers, a shape over the section's top and bottom edges, {top, bottom}, each {shape, height, flip, color} or null: shape one of wave, curve, tilt, triangle, zigzag, arch, cloud, drip; height sm, md (the default) or lg; flip true mirrors it; color a theme token (foreground, muted, accent, background) or "#rrggbb", left out to take the colour of the section next to it; dividers null removes both, and dividers left out keeps them. A section drawn as a photo beside words (an image-and-text block in its beside layout, or a hero in its split or splitLeft layout) also takes split, the left column's share of the row in whole percent (25 to 75), and phoneOrder, what a phone shows first where the columns stack: auto (as designed), photo, words, or hidePhoto. Every section but a sticky call to action takes customCss (a plan with custom code), the section's own CSS written as usual (h1 { letter-spacing: -0.02em; }): it applies to that section only, a url() must be https, and @import or a < is refused; "" clears it. Its rules WIN over the house styles inside the section, whatever their specificity (h2 { font-weight: 400; color: #333; } beats the bold headline and the Text colour). Every rule needs a selector: :scope (or &) is the section itself, and a declaration on it only inherits, so it never reaches a heading that sets the property itself. Stable hooks: the section's root carries data-section-type (its type), a headline is an h1, h2 or h3 with the class display, a small label above it is .eyebrow, body copy is p, and a button is an a. The screenshot (manage_page/preview) draws it as the page does.

position.description: Where it goes, 1 for the top. Omit to add it at the bottom.

to.description: Its new position, 1 for the top. Past the end means the bottom.

device.description: desktop (the default, 1280px wide), mobile (a phone, 390px wide), or both (desktop then phone in one answer; counts as two screenshots against the hourly limit).

fromScreen.description: The first screen to show, 1 for the top. The answer says how many there are.

versionId.description: Omit to list the versions; from that list to read one.

restorePointId.description: Or a website restore point holding the page, from manage_site/history.

fromPageId.description: Or another page of this community to copy from, as it stands now (manage_page/read with no pageId lists them). May be the page itself, which duplicates the section.

index.description: With fromPageId only: where it goes, 0 for the top. Absent puts it at the bottom.

savedSectionId.description: Omit to list them; from that list to read one in full.

name.description: What Add a section lists it under, up to 80 characters.

published.description: true to publish, false to take it back to a draft.

tools.name: manage_site
tools.title: Read and build the community website
tools.description:
The coach's own multi-page site: its pages, its menu, its footer, its chrome, the redirects that send a previous site's old addresses on to the new pages, its history (restore points of the whole site, and every menu, header and footer change), its languages (a version of each page in each language the site adds), its custom code (code that runs on every website page), and its popups (one section in a box over its pages). Every plan has the website, a beta: the Free plan holds up to five website pages (translations count). Popups, and languages beside the main one: Available on the Creator plan. Reading, taking down and removing work on every plan. To build a site, in order: manage_site/read, then a template (manage_site/apply_template) or pages (manage_site/create_page, then manage_page/update), the look (manage_site/set_look), the menu, footer and header (manage_site/set_menu, manage_site/set_footer, manage_site/set_chrome), search and sharing (each page's pageSettings on manage_page/update; manage_site/set_chrome for the whole site), a check of each page (manage_page/preview and manage_page/score), publishing each page (manage_page/publish), and the home page (manage_site/set_home).

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The whole site as it stands: what visitors see at the root of its address (a website page, a funnel page, the store, the blog or the join page) and how to change it, every page at its public address (/about; the home page at the root), how its header and footer are laid out and styled, the footer's social links in order, and how many popups, collections, custom code boxes and restore points it has. Start here.
- create_page: A new draft page on the coach's own website, added to the end of the menu (it shows there once published): empty, or filled in from a website page template (`pageTemplate`, a key from manage_site/page_templates).
- duplicate_page: Copy one website page, sections, look and settings, as a new draft at a new address, added to the end of the menu.
- set_home: Make a website page what visitors see at the root of the community's address, in place of whatever holds it now (another page, a funnel page, the store or the blog, each kept at its own address). Public at once for a published page.
- page_templates: The ready-made single website pages (About, Services, Contact, Team, Pricing, FAQ, Testimonials, Work with me, Start here, Class schedule, Free resource, Speaking, Press & media kit, Portfolio, Podcast, Retreat), each with its key, its suggested address and the sections it lays down; with `pageTemplate`, that page's full sections built for this community, to lay over an existing page with manage_page/update.
- templates: The website templates this community can start from: the designed ones first, then the starters, each with its key, the pages it makes, its look (palette, fonts, corners, buttons, header and footer) and its style (calm, bold, editorial or playful).
- apply_template: Lay a whole site down in one go from a template key (manage_site/templates): its new pages are drafts added to the end of the menu, but unless keepMyColours keeps the website's own look (kept by default once the website has pages), the template's look goes on every existing page, LIVE ones included, and on the header and footer at once, after a restore point manage_site/restore puts back. Its home page takes the root only when nothing holds it; the answer says when it did not, and manage_site/set_home moves it.
- set_menu: The site's navigation. Do this after the pages exist.
- set_footer: The links in the site's footer, each optionally under a column heading the columns footer groups them by (its tagline, social icons, layout and signup are manage_site/set_chrome's).
- set_chrome: The header (its layout: classic, transparent over the first section or centered; its style: standard, glass, pill or hideOnScroll, the last three always pinned; its button, announcement bar and stickiness), the footer's layout (simple or columns), its email signup (one of the community's forms), tagline and social icons (one ordered list of profile links, each shown as its platform's icon), and the website's search and sharing defaults: the description and social image (a stock photo) a page without its own uses, and whether the site belongs to a person or a business.
- redirects: Every old address the community sends on (a previous website's /about, /services-1) and the page each goes to.
- add_redirects: Send a previous website's addresses on to their new pages, up to 100 at a time, LIVE at once, so old links and the search ranking follow (a permanent 308). Each refused one says why.
- remove_redirects: Stop redirecting old addresses. Works on every plan.
- history: The website's restore points (the whole site at a moment: every website page plus the menu, header and footer; taken on a first publish, before a template, a restore or a delete, and on demand) and its menu, header and footer changes, newest first; with a restorePointId, the pages it holds and what restoring it (or one pageId of it) would change; with a frameVersionId, what undoing that change would put back.
- restore: Put the whole site back to a restorePointId (pages, menu, header and footer; a page deleted since comes back as a draft, a page made since is left alone), or one pageId of it, or undo one menu, header and footer change by frameVersionId. Never moves an address, the homepage or what is published, and saves the site as it is now first, so it can be undone.
- save_restore_point: Keep the whole website as it is now as a restore point, with an optional name. Changes nothing on the site.
- languages: The website's main language, the languages it adds (each with its address word, like /fr, and the coach's menu and footer words in it), and every website page's translation in each: its pageId, address (/fr/about), draft or published, and out of date when its main page was saved after it.
- set_languages: Set the main language, add languages (up to five beside it) or remove them (their pages are kept, off the site until the language is added again), and a language's words for the menu and footer labels.
- translate_page: Make a website page's version in an added language: a DRAFT copy of its sections to rewrite in that language with manage_page/update or manage_page/edit_section, then publish with manage_page/publish. It lives at the main page's address under the language (/fr/about).
- code: The website's custom code in full: the head, start-of-page and end-of-page boxes (each with its code, on or off, the pages it runs on and whether it waits for cookie consent), each page's own head code, the Google Tag Manager id, the custom section stylesheet and script every custom code section carries first, the versions it can go back to, and whether the community's ad tracking is connected.
- set_code: Put code on the website that RUNS ON EVERY PAGE (or chosen pages) and is live at once: any of the three boxes, a page's own head code, the Google Tag Manager id, the custom section stylesheet and script (`blockCss`, `blockJs`: written once, put into every custom code section ahead of its own code, so shared fonts and base styles are never repeated per section), or an earlier version back (`restoreVersionId`). Owner or admin only; every save is kept and the answer names the version that undoes it.
- look: The look the whole website wears (its colours, fonts, label font, corners and buttons) and every choice manage_site/set_look takes: the certified palettes, the tested font pairs, the label font, the corner and button steps.
- set_look: Change the whole website's look at once, on every page: a certified palette (or one brand colour built into one, refused when too pale to read), a tested font pair, a label font (eyebrows, buttons and the header navigation: any Google family, null takes it off), corners and buttons. Send only what changes: what is sent goes onto each page over its own look, and each one left out stays as each page has it. Saves a restore point first; on a live page it shows at once. The community's own Studio colours never change.
- restore_brand: Put the community's own Studio colours and fonts back on every website page (or the pages named), clearing what a template or a page's Design set. Words, corners and buttons are untouched; live pages show it at once.
- old_site: Moving from another site: read the old site's sitemap and match each old address to one of this website's pages (sure, a best guess to confirm, or none). Writes nothing.
- move_site: Save old addresses as redirects, each to a page named by its pageId, LIVE at once, so links to the old site keep working. Each refused pair is named.
- popups: Every popup, drafts included: its popupId, whether it is live, when it opens (only from a button, or by itself after a delay, a scroll or as the pointer leaves, on which pages and screens, and how often per visitor), which pages have a button to it, its last 30 days (shown, closed, clicked through, signed up), and its settings and section as JSON.
- save_popup: Make a popup (a draft, holding one freeform, form or offer section) or change one, only what is sent changing; on a live popup the change is seen at once. A website page's button opens it with the destination {"kind":"popup","popupId":"<id>"}.
- set_popup_live: Put a popup in front of visitors at once (live true: by itself as its settings say, and from every button that names it), or take it down (live false, on every plan).
- delete_popup: Delete a popup that was never live and that no live page's button opens. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: What the page is called in the console and, by default, in the menu. From a page template, its name is the usual choice.

slug.description: Its address: once published, the page answers at /<slug> on the community's own address ("about" is /about). 2 to 48 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Not a word the community already uses (/join, /library, /store and the like), nor the bio link's or the blog's own word. The two exceptions are terms and privacy: a PUBLIC website page published at /terms or /privacy replaces the community's own legal page at that address on the site, so a migrated site keeps its legal URLs. A missing address shows a not-found page in the site's own look, header and footer; there is nothing to build for it.

pageTemplate.description: Start the page from this website page template (manage_site/page_templates): a built-in key, or a designed one's lib- key. Omit for an empty page.

pageId.description: The website page to copy, from manage_site/read.

template.description: Which template to apply: a key from manage_site/templates.

keepMyColours.description: true keeps the website's own colours, fonts, buttons, header and footer; false brings the template's look to the whole website. Left out: false for a website with no pages yet, true for one that has some.

pageId.description: A site page's id, from manage_site/read or manage_page/read.

href.description: An https:// URL, or a path on the coach's own site starting with "/" ("/contact"). Nothing else is stored.

pageId.description: A site page's id, from manage_site/read or manage_page/read.

href.description: An https:// URL, or a path on the coach's own site starting with "/" ("/contact"). Nothing else is stored.

items.description: The dropdown's children. Pages or links, never another menu.

menu.description: The whole menu, left to right. At most 12 entries. Send [] to show no menu.

href.description: An https:// URL or a "/" path on the coach's own site.

group.description: The column heading this link sits under when the footer is "columns" (manage_site/set_chrome footerLayout), like "Help". Left out or "" = the "Links" column. The simple footer shows every link in one row.

links.description: The whole footer row, in order. At most 8. Send [] to clear it.

sticky.description: Keep the header pinned while the visitor scrolls. It changes nothing while headerStyle is glass, pill or hideOnScroll, which pin the header themselves.

buttonLabel.description: The header button's words. Send "" for the default, "Join".

buttonHref.description: Where the header button goes: an https:// URL or a "/" path. Send "" to send it to the community's own join/checkout flow.

announcement.description: The slim banner above the header, shown on every published website page. Send "" to remove it.

announcementHref.description: Where the banner links. Send "" to leave it as plain text.

announcementTone.description: How the banner looks: accent, soft or ink.
