tools.name: manage_collection
tools.title: Read and build the website's collections
tools.description:
The coach's website collections: lists of like things they keep, such as their portfolio, team, testimonials, press, case studies or services. Each has fields (text, rich text, image, link, date, number, tags, yes or no, or a relation linking the community's own classes, courses or products) and items, each a draft or live. A collection is shown on a page by a collection section (manage_page), and when it has pages, at /<word> and /<word>/<item>. Building collections: Available on the Creator plan. Reading them, unpublishing an item and deleting a draft work on every plan.

Set `act` to one of:
- list: Every collection, each with its collectionId, preset, card style, address, preview address and how many items are live. Start here.
- read: One collection in full: its fields, its settings, its item page (built-in, or the designed layout as JSON with what each element is filled from) and every item in order, drafts included, with each item's itemId, address, preview address and values as JSON. Read before every edit.
- presets: The ready-made collections create starts from (portfolio, team, testimonials, press, caseStudies, services, custom), each with its fields, card style, word and whether items get pages.
- create: A new, empty collection from a preset, its name, address word, fields, card style, item pages and intro the preset's unless sent.
- update: Change a collection's name, address word, card style, intro, whether items get pages, or its whole field list (a field left out drops its values from every item). Live at once.
- set_item_layout: Design the page every item of a collection gets: freeform sections whose text, image and button elements may each be filled from the item's title or one of its fields (a bind), hidden on an item where that field is empty; live at once on every item's page. null puts the built-in item page back.
- add_item: Add 1 to 50 items with a title and values each, as drafts unless publish is true (then live at once).
- edit_item: Change one item's title, address or values; only the value keys sent change. Live at once on a published item.
- reorder_items: Put every item of a collection in a new order.
- publish_item: Put one item live on the website at once, with its own page when the collection has pages.
- unpublish_item: Make one item a draft again, off the website at once. Works on every plan.
- duplicate_item: Copy one item, values and all, as a new draft right after it.
- delete_item: Delete one item that has never been live. Cannot be undone.
- delete: Delete a collection none of whose items has ever been live. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

name.description: Its name, like Our work. The preset's label by default.

word.description: Its address word, like work for /work: 2 to 48 lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens.

fields.description: Fields in place of the preset's, in order.

key.description: The key item values are stored under: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, numbers and underscores (title and slug are taken).

label.description: What the console calls the field.

kind.description: text, richText, image, link, date, number, tags, toggle, or relation (links the item to the community's own classes and events, courses or products, drawn live on its page).

target.description: A relation field only, and required there: what it links, events, courses or products.

itemPages.description: Whether each item gets its own page and the collection a page listing them.

intro.description: The line under the title on the collection's own page.

sections.description: Freeform sections, as the layout manage_collection/read prints.

layout.description: The item page's layout, or null for the built-in item page.

slug.description: The item's address after /<word>/: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

values.description: Field values by field key, each in its kind's shape: text and richText (markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [links](https://...), - lists) as words; image as { key, alt } with a stock photo key from manage_page/stock_photos or the key the item already holds; link as { href, label } with an https address or a path on this site; date as YYYY-MM-DD; number as a number; tags as a list of words; toggle as true or false; relation as a list of ids (events from manage_event/list, courses from list_catalog, products from manage_product/list, as the field's target says; only ones a visitor may see are shown). Send null, "" or [] to clear a field.

publish.description: true puts every added item live at once. Confirm with the coach first.

values.description: Field values by field key, each in its kind's shape: text and richText (markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [links](https://...), - lists) as words; image as { key, alt } with a stock photo key from manage_page/stock_photos or the key the item already holds; link as { href, label } with an https address or a path on this site; date as YYYY-MM-DD; number as a number; tags as a list of words; toggle as true or false; relation as a list of ids (events from manage_event/list, courses from list_catalog, products from manage_product/list, as the field's target says; only ones a visitor may see are shown). Send null, "" or [] to clear a field.

tools.name: manage_studio
tools.title: Read and set the community's branding
tools.description:
How the member surface looks and reads: the wordmark, the colours, the page copy, the welcome flow, the home rails, the paywall, and which automatic emails members get and what they say.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The whole theme as it stands, including what the automatic member emails say and the email footer's address and social links. Read before every edit.
- brand_look: Wordmark, colours and typography.
- read_website_brand: Read only: give it the coach's own website address and it reads that site's public HTML and CSS (running none of its scripts) and suggests a matching wordmark, background, text and accent colour as hex, and headline and body fonts matched to the curated menu, saying whether each is the same font or the nearest; plus any logo images it found, as addresses. Writes nothing: apply with manage_studio/brand_look.
- button_style: The community-wide default look for buttons: on the member home and join page, or on the funnel pages.
- page_copy: The words on the member home, library and community pages.
- member_onboarding: The welcome message (markdown-lite) and the profile questions a new member answers.
- member_emails: Switch the automatic member emails on or off: the new-content email, the welcome email, and session reminders (the reminders before a session and the gone-live email; invites, reschedules, cancellations, RSVP confirmations, tickets and booked sessions send either way). Also their wording: the subject and opening paragraph of the new-content and welcome emails, the receipt note, and the postal address in the footer of every email built in the email builder, and of new-content emails, digests and emailed posts. And the email signature of the coach: its words, where its saved pictures sit and how big, and whether it also signs the automatic emails (owner or admin only; a new picture is drawn, typed or uploaded in the console). Not the footer's social links (manage_marketing_org/assets).
- add_home_section: A new rail or block on the member home page, including an embedded page hosted elsewhere.
- update_home_section: Edit a home rail or message block (a coach's message can be signed by the owner and/or admins, and its body is markdown-lite; a Latest posts block takes which posts, how many and how they are laid out; an embedded page takes its address and height), restyle its button, or move it up the page.
- add_paywall_section: A new block on the join page. Staff only.
- update_paywall_section: Edit a join-page block, or restyle its button. Staff only.

"" shows Drry's instead, marked "Sent via Drry". One line.

Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone. A PICTURE is a line of its own: ![what it shows](picture:a), optionally followed by {small} or {large} (medium otherwise). Only the slots manage_studio/read lists as saved can be placed, at most 2, and at most 400 characters of words. Send the stored value back edited to keep its pictures. "" takes the signature off.

Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.). On every other section it is plain text with line breaks kept, so do not write markdown marks into it.

tools.name: manage_settings
tools.title: Community settings, and see storage use and the sending domain
tools.description:
The switches a coach sets once: what the tabs are called, which surfaces members see, and the rules for discussions, events and messages. Also reads storage use against the plan and what extra storage costs, which only the owner can switch on, in the console, and whether email goes out from the community's own domain.

Set `act` to one of:
- labels: Rename the community feed and courses tabs, switch the audio and events surfaces on or off, switch the Resources tab on or off and rename it, AND show or hide the blog's tab in the member menu and rename the blog (blogInMemberMenu, blogLabel: owner or admin only). The other tabs and switches are console only. LIVE immediately; keep the previous values it returns.
- community: The community's name, its timezone, the country it is based in (which decides whether its forms, checkouts, bookings, event sign-ups, free downloads and join pages ask visitors about email updates, as they do in the EU/EEA, the UK and Canada, and which country-limited background collections its bio link offers), and which alerts the coach is emailed. No description: that belongs to a discussion category. The surface toggles live on manage_settings/labels. Staff only.
- discussion: The community feed's attachment rules and AI moderation (live chat's are manage_settings/events). Staff only.
- discussion_category: Add, rename or reorder a discussion category. Staff only.
- events_read: Read only: the calendar's standing defaults and what live chat allows: the standing meeting link, what an instant meeting starts with, whether chat carries pictures, files and link cards, whether a webinar attendee's link is held, and whether chat is screened. Staff only.
- events: The calendar's standing defaults and live-chat rules: a default join link, instant-meeting recording/notes/chat, whether live chat carries pictures, files and link cards, whether a webinar attendee's link is held for a host, and whether live chat is screened by AI (screening is Growth). To show or rename the tab use manage_settings/labels. Staff only.
- messages: Direct-message rules: photos and files, the membership needed, whether members may message each other or only the hosts, and AI screening (screening is owner only).
- domains: Read only: every domain Drry holds or is moving in for the community's owner, with its status, who pays (free with the plan, free from Drry, or a paid yearly add-on and its price), when it renews or that it won't, whether this community's website is on it, and how far a move in has got. DNS records, the website's address, name search and moving in are manage_domain; buying, renewal and moving out stay in the console. Staff only.
- sending_domain: Read only: whether email goes out from the community's own domain, its sender address, whether it is verified, pending or lapsed (falling back to Drry's senders), whether its DMARC record is in place, and whether the plan includes it. Connecting or removing one stays in the console. Staff only.
- storage: Read only: storage used against what the plan includes and how much is over, whether extra storage can be bought and is on sale this period (and from when), whether extra usage is on and its spend cap, what storage has cost this period (charged on the period's peak, the most held past the plan at any point), and how much of the shared cap live video, email and storage take. Staff only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

communityLabel.description: What the community feed tab is called, e.g. "The Lounge".

coursesLabel.description: What the courses tab is called, e.g. "Programs".

audioEnabled.description: Whether the audio surface is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages opening; nothing is deleted.

eventsEnabled.description: Whether the events surface is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages opening; nothing is deleted.

resourcesEnabled.description: Whether the Resources tab (member files) is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages and downloads opening; nothing is deleted.

resourcesLabel.description: What the Resources tab is called, e.g. "Downloads".

blogInMemberMenu.description: Whether members get a Blog tab in their menu while the blog is on. It opens the blog itself. False takes the tab out; the blog and its posts stay public.

blogLabel.description: The blog's name, on its tab, its pages and its emails, e.g. "Journal". Empty goes back to "Blog".

name.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

timezone.description: The community's clock, as an IANA zone name like Europe/London or America/Los_Angeles, never a display name like "Pacific Standard Time". Anything scheduled on a wall clock reads it.

country.description: Where the community is based, as a two-letter ISO country code like US, GB or CA; null clears it. It decides TWO things. First, MARKETING CONSENT: a community based in the EU, the EEA, the UK or Canada asks visitors whether they want email updates before their address joins the list (a box on its checkouts, bookings, event sign-ups, free downloads and join pages, and on every form whose Marketing consent step is on; its Instagram auto-DM email step cannot ask, so someone new it saves lands Not opted in); anywhere else, or with no country, nobody is asked. Changing it turns that on or off on every page at once, and a change that stops the asking pauses every live Instagram auto-reply with an email step (its consent line is sent from then on, so it must go live again to be checked), so confirm with the coach first. Second, which country-limited background collections the bio link Library offers. It is not the Stripe account's country and changes no price or currency.

newMemberEmail.description: Email the coach when somebody joins or pays to join.

memberLeftEmail.description: Email the coach when a paying member cancels.

productSaleEmail.description: Email the coach when somebody buys a digital product.

weeklyPulseEmail.description: The Monday-morning summary of what changed in this community.

drryNewsEmail.description: Drry's own product news and feature announcements.

allowImages.description: May members attach pictures to a post. Pictures use storage.

allowFiles.description: May members attach files to a post. Files use storage.

maxAttachmentsPerPost.description: How many attachments one post may carry, 1 to 10.

polls.description: May a post carry a poll.

reactions.description: Does a post show the reaction bar beyond a plain like.

screenPosts.description: Screen posts with AI before they go live. ON means a post that looks like a violation is HELD out of the feed until the coach approves it. OFF means nothing is held.

screenStrictness.description: How cautious the screen is. relaxed holds only clear violations, strict holds borderline posts too.

screenGuidance.description: What this community is about, in the coach's own words, so the screen can tell an off-topic post from an on-topic one. Plain text; it is read as context, never as instructions.

screenFor.description: The complete list of categories to screen for: HA (Hate and harassment), ME (Mean-spirited), SX (Sexual content), VI (Threats and violence), SH (Self-harm crisis), MI (Dangerous misinformation), SP (Spam and self-promotion), OT (Off-topic). Anything not listed is NOT screened for, so send the whole set, not just the change. Omit to leave the current set alone.

categoryId.description: The category to edit. Omit to create a new one, which returns its id. No read tool lists a community's existing categories yet, so if you do not already have the id, say so rather than guessing one.

description.description: One line saying what belongs in here. Empty clears it.

hue.description: The colour of its chip, as a hue angle 0-360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue). Defaults to 18 on a new category.

position.description: Where it sits in the list, zero-based, 0 being first. The other rooms shuffle around it; nothing else about them changes.

defaultJoinUrl.description: The coach's standing meeting link (a Zoom personal room, a standing Google Meet), prefilled into every new event. A booking type with no link of its own ALSO falls back to this one, so members really are sent here. http:// or https:// only. Empty string clears it.

instantMeetingRecording.description: Whether an instant meeting starts recording. Recordings use the community's storage.

instantMeetingNotes.description: Whether an instant meeting transcribes and writes a recap. Inert below Growth.

instantMeetingChat.description: Whether an instant meeting opens with live chat on.

chatImages.description: May a live-chat message carry a picture at all.

chatFiles.description: May a live-chat message carry a file (PDF, Office document, CSV or text) at all. A file is always a download. In a webinar only a host may share one either way.

chatLinkPreviews.description: Does a link in live chat render a preview card.

chatHoldLinks.description: Hold a guest's link in a webinar until a host releases it.

screenChat.description: Screen live-chat messages with AI before the room sees them. Independent of the community feed's screen: neither inherits from the other.

screenChatGuidance.description: Community context for the chat screen. Plain text.

screenChatFor.description: The complete list of categories the chat screen enforces: HA (Hate and harassment), ME (Mean-spirited), SX (Sexual content), VI (Threats and violence), SH (Self-harm crisis), MI (Dangerous misinformation), SP (Spam and self-promotion), OT (Off-topic). Anything not listed is not screened for.

minTierId.description: The membership tier needed to reach out, from list_catalog/membership_tiers. Pass null to open messaging to everyone. Omit to leave the current rule alone. Blocking, reporting, leaving and clearing a conversation are never gated.

lockedTabIsVisible.description: When a tier is required, whether members below it still SEE the tab locked (true, the default) or it disappears entirely (false).

screenMessages.description: Point an AI screen at direct messages. Owner only, Growth only. It never holds, edits or blocks a message.

hostsOnly.description: true = members may message the owner and admins but not each other; conversations between members become read-only, and a group stays open while a host is in it. false = members may message each other again, which reopens those conversations. The hosts can always message anyone.

tools.name: manage_domain
tools.title: Read and change domain names, DNS records, the website's address and moving a domain in
tools.description:
The domains Drry holds for a coach, done for them: check a name and what it would cost them, read and add DNS records, point the website at one of their domains, and walk a domain they own elsewhere through moving in. Changing or removing a live record, buying, renewal, moving a domain out and the transfer code are confirmed by the owner in the console, through the links these answers give. The list of domains is manage_settings/domains.

Set `act` to one of:
- search: Read only: whether a .com is free, ideas when it is not, and what the owner's next domain costs them bought new or moved in (free with the plan, free from Drry, or a paid yearly add-on). Buying is in the console; the answer links there. Owner only.
- dns: Read only: every DNS record on one of the owner's domains, the coach's own with their recordId and Drry's locked, and whether they can change now. Staff only.
- add_record: Add an MX, TXT or CNAME record, after the console's own checks (Drry's names and clashes refused). Live at once: show the coach the record first. Owner only.
- change_record: Changes nothing: checks an edit to, or the removal of, one of the coach's records and answers with a console link that opens it highlighted with the change filled in, for the coach to save. Owner only.
- connect_website: Point the community's website at a host on a domain Drry holds (yourname.com, www or a subdomain); Drry writes its records. Moving it off an address it already has needs replaceCurrent, after the coach agrees. Owner only, Creator and up.
- move_in_start: Start moving in a .com the coach owns elsewhere: claim it, make its zone and copy its records, at the price manage_domain/search quoted. Nothing is charged here. Owner only.
- move_in: Read only: the step a move in is at, the nameservers to set when that is the step, and the console link for the transfer code. Staff only.
- move_in_confirm_records: The copied records look right: on to the nameservers step, answered with the two nameservers to set. Owner only.
- move_in_check: Ask whether the nameservers have switched; once they have, the answer links to the transfer-code step in the console. Owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

query.description: A name to check, like rootedwellness.com. Omit for ideas.

domain.description: A domain like yourname.com. For manage_domain/dns, manage_domain/add_record and manage_domain/change_record: one of the owner's domains from manage_settings/domains, omitted for the community's current one. For the move-in acts: the .com moving in, always required.

name.description: The host, relative to the domain: @ for the domain itself, or a name like mail2 or _dmarc. A full name under the domain is accepted too.

content.description: The value: the text for a TXT, the target host for a CNAME or MX.

priority.description: MX only: 0 to 65535, lower is preferred. Defaults to 10.

change.description: edit: change the record. delete: remove it.

replaceCurrent.description: True once the coach agreed to move the website off the address it has now.

expectedKind.description: The price quoted by manage_domain/search for moving one in.

tools.name: manage_email
tools.title: Read and write broadcast emails
tools.description:
The email a coach sends to members or leads. Drafted here with every block and design option the console's editor has, sent from the console, and referenced by automations and forms.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One email in full (every block and style option in the form the update takes, sender name, tracking, header and design, schedule and send results: opens, clicks and, staff only, what it SOLD within 7 days of a click, net of refunds), and which blog post each blog post block shows, or every email when emailId is omitted. Says whether it is LIVE.
- create: A new draft, written block by block (photos from the stock library, a blog post block showing one published post or the newest few, custom code blocks on plans with custom code) or started from a template. Sends to nobody until a person presses send.
- update: Edit a draft: name, subject, preview, blocks (a photo may be a stock photo; a blog post block shows one published post or the newest few; a custom code block is written in full on plans with custom code), sender name, tracking, header and design. The coach's own uploads are carried, never chosen. A name alone may change on any email. Editing a LIVE one changes what automations and forms send from now on.
- templates: Read only: the template gallery, with the key a new draft or a template swap takes, and the fifteen stock photos the templates are made with.
- stock_photos: Read only: every stock photo a photo in an email body may use, the fifteen the templates are made with and the stock library's photos this community may pick now, each with its key, shape, mood, the kinds of coach it suits, whether it shows people, its search words and what it shows; narrowed by query, niche and shape, at most limit of them.
- apply_template: Replace a draft's blocks, subject, preview and design with a template's. Refused where it would delete uploaded photos or files; a custom block it replaces is removed and named.
- saved_blocks: Read only: the coach's saved blocks and saved emails, with the id a savedBlock body item takes.
- unschedule: Take a scheduled email back to a draft so it does not go out.
- test_send: Send a test of an email to your own account address, and nobody else. Says when a block was left out because the blog is off.
- delete: Delete a DRAFT email that was never sent or scheduled and that no automation, form, session type or product uses. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

emailId.description: Omit to list every email with its id.

name.description: The coach's private label for it in their list.

subject.description: The subject line. Required unless a template is named.

previewText.description: The line shown after the subject in an inbox.

color.description: This heading's own text colour. Leave out for the theme's.

body.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone. Merge tags work in this copy and are filled in per recipient; the body parameter's description lists every one of them and the fallback syntax.

href.description: A full https:// address, a path starting with /, one of the link tags ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}), or {productLink:<id>} naming a product's id (see list_catalog/products); only a product currently FOR SALE resolves, a draft or archived one leaves the button out of the sent email with no warning at write time, or {formLink:<id>} naming a form's id (see list_catalog/forms); only a PUBLISHED form resolves, a draft one leaves the button out of the sent email with no warning at write time, ON ITS OWN. A link tag is substituted only when it is the ENTIRE value: one pasted inside a URL is either refused here or delivered to members as literal text inside a link that goes nowhere.

style.description: fill (accent), outline, ink (dark fill) or link (bare text).

shadow.description: none, raised (a soft lift, the console's Lift) or offset (a hard block, the console's Pop). A link-style button takes neither.

color.description: This button's own colour. Leave out for the brand accent.

spacing.description: The air above and below it.

color.description: The line's own colour. Leave out for the theme's.

part.description: A purchase insert, filled in per order on a product's receipt, download or refund email: delivery (the download button or a service's instructions), summary (the receipt table), refundPolicy, alsoFrom (what comes next) or refundDetails. A paid product's receipt must hold delivery and summary, a free product's download email delivery, a refund email refundDetails. An email holding one cannot be sent any other way, since there is no purchase to fill it.

options.description: The answers, 2 to 5, each a one-click link. A poll with fewer than 2 is not a question and is left out of the sent email.

endsAt.description: The deadline as an ISO-8601 instant, or "" while it is not set (the block is left out of the send).

timezone.description: The IANA timezone the deadline is written out in.

kinds.description: Which kinds it may show. Empty means all of them.

mode.description: post: one published blog post (postId). latest: the blog's newest published posts (limit). Each is drawn as its cover, title, card line and a Read more button; a members-only post shows its card line and a Members only marker, never its body. Resolved when the email sends; nothing shows while the blog is off.

postId.description: A published post's id (a uuid), from manage_blog/read. "" in latest mode.

limit.description: How many of the newest posts, 1 to 3. Latest mode.

refId.description: The id of a published course, lesson, audio track or event in this community.

ctaStyle.description: button, or link to make the whole card one link.

refId.description: The id of a published video or audio lesson in this community, drawn as a thumbnail that links to it.

refKind.description: product (a shop product), paymentLink, or checkout for the Their item card: the item each person left at checkout, filled in only on an email an automation sends when someone leaves checkout without paying.

refId.description: The id of an active shop product or payment link. Empty for checkout.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

fileKey.description: The file key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. A new one cannot be chosen here.

imageKey.description: A stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, or the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

imageKey.description: A stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, or the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

imageKey.description: The background photo: a stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, or "" for a solid band.

ctaHref.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

comp.description: The saved layout's design, as manage_email/read printed it.

fields.description: Its slots, as manage_email/read printed them: copy is written freely, a photo slot takes a stock:<name> key or a photo this email holds.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

label.description: The block's name in the coach's editor. Members never see it.

html.description: Table-based email HTML: the fragment only, no html, head or body. Kept: table, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, div, span, p, h1 to h6, a, img, br, hr, ul, ol, li, strong, em, b, i, u, s, small, sup, sub, blockquote, center, font, pre and code, with style and the usual table attributes. Removed: scripts, style tags, iframes, svg, forms, comments, on* handlers, and a style holding url(), expression() or a comment. Editable slots are tokens: {{text:key}} for copy, {{image:key}} (the ONLY src an img may have, so every photo is a slot), {{link:key}} (or a full https:// address or mailto:) for an href, and {{color:key}}, {{size:key}} or {{align:key}} inside a style value. A text, link or image token inside a style drops that whole style attribute. A link tag ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}) is not a destination inside the html: put it in a link slot's field. Up to 24 slots; a key is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The markup is rebuilt by the sanitizer on save, so read it back.

css.description: Optional CSS for media queries and class rules, scoped to this block when sent. A <, @import, url(), expression() or an unclosed comment drops the whole stylesheet, so it is refused here.

fields.description: A value for each slot the html declares, by slot key: text is plain copy (merge tags work), image a stock:<name> key or a photo this email holds, link what a button link takes, color a hex, named colour, rgb(), hsl() or gradient, size one to four lengths such as 28px, 1.5rem or 100%, and align left, center or right.

tsx.description: Inert source an older designer left on some blocks; nothing reads or runs it. Send back what manage_email/read printed, or leave it out.

savedBlockId.description: From manage_email/saved_blocks. Arrives as the blocks it holds.

body.description: The blocks of the letter, in order. Required unless a template is named. Merge tags, filled in per recipient at send time: {firstName|there}, {community}, {eventTitle|the session}, {eventDate}, {eventTime}, {eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {eventLocation}, {offerLink}, {offerPrice}, {offerEnds}, {productTitle|your purchase}, {productPrice}, {checkoutLink}, {offerCode}. Type one exactly as listed, in a heading, text, quote or button label, or in the subject or preview. Do not hand-type a greeting, a date, a place or a price that a tag can fill. The text after "|" inside a tag is the fallback used when that recipient has no value, and the tags above already carry one wherever a default helps. The link tags ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}) take no fallback and must be the WHOLE href of a button, never part of one: only the exact tag is ever substituted, so a tag pasted inside a URL is either refused here or delivered to members as literal text inside a link that goes nowhere. Event and offer tags need an email that an automation sends for that event or offer; in a standalone broadcast one of them with no fallback blocks the send. The checkout tags ({productPrice}, {checkoutLink}, {offerCode}) and the Their item card fill in only on an email a checkout_abandoned journey sends, which also fills the product name tag with the item they left. PHOTOS: an image, image-and-text, hero, saved layout photo slot or custom block image slot takes either a stock photo from Drry's own library (a stock:<name> or stock:lib/<id> key, listed by manage_email/stock_photos) or a key manage_email/read printed for this email (or one a saved block brings in), sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here, only carried: a new one is uploaded in the console. A download's fileKey is carried the same way. A body that leaves out an uploaded photo or file this email holds is refused, because dropping it deletes it; remove one in the console. A custom block (plans with custom code) is written in full, its html, css, label and slot fields, and leaving one out removes it, as deleting it in the console does. A saved block (manage_email/saved_blocks) goes in as one item of type savedBlock naming its savedBlockId, and arrives as the blocks it holds.

template.description: A template key from manage_email/templates. The draft arrives with the template's blocks, subject, preview and design, and a subject or body sent alongside it is refused.

senderName.description: The name in the From line for this one email. null or "" sends as the community name.

tracking.description: Whether this email records opens and clicks.

show.description: Show the logo and wordmark bar.

logo.description: image (the community's logo beside its wordmark), logoOnly, or wordmark. Both logo modes fall back to the wordmark when the community has no logo.

shell.description: The surface the email sits on.

accent.description: This email's accent. null returns it to the theme's.

displayFont.description: Headline typeface. null returns it to the theme's.

bodyFont.description: Body typeface. null returns it to the theme's.

paper.description: An exact card colour over the shell's own. null removes it.

signature.description: false leaves the email signature of the community off this email; true (the default) shows it. The signature itself is set with manage_studio/member_emails.

header.description: A PATCH over the stored header and design: only what you send changes. The logo is the community's own brand logo; a new one is uploaded in the Studio.

query.description: Words to search by, like "calm morning" or "kitchen": every word must appear in a photo's description, mood or search words. Leave it out to list every photo.

niche.description: Only photos made for this kind of coach (the coach kinds manage_site/templates files websites by).

shape.description: Only photos of this shape: wide (about 16:9), landscape, square or portrait.

limit.description: How many to list, 1 to 100; 40 when left out.

tools.name: manage_automation
tools.title: Read and build email journeys
tools.description:
A journey enrols people on a trigger and mails them on its own schedule. Compose it as a draft, then arm it deliberately.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One journey in full: its trigger and goal, what its emails sold, every step with its settings and where each way out goes, and the steps in the words manage_automation/set_steps takes, to edit and send back. Every journey when automationId is omitted.
- create: A new draft journey. Mails nobody.
- rename: Rename a journey. Does not change what it does.
- set_steps: Lay out the trigger (every option, including the goal, a repeating event, whether people already on a list enter, and for someone who leaves a shop checkout without paying an optional product and an optional offer its emails show) and the whole graph: waits, waits until a date, a condition or a time around the event, emails, direct messages, tags, lists, coach notifications, yes/no branches, multi-way splits, jumps, and an offer with its price and, on a community that sells membership tiers, the tier it discounts. Replaces the whole graph, works on a live journey under the live-edit rules the console uses, and turns nothing on. Offer steps, the steps leading to one and the trigger of a journey with one are the owner's to change.
- set_status: ARM or pause it. Arming mails everyone who matches, unattended, and un-sends nothing. Pausing closes any offer link the journey opened, for good.
- copy: Duplicate a journey, or start one from a recipe.
- delete: Delete a journey that has never been switched on. Its emails are kept. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

automationId.description: Omit to list every journey with its id.

name.description: What the coach will see in their list, e.g. “Welcome sequence”.

courseId.description: Course triggers. Required to go live.

source.description: signed_in_not_joined, entered_list: where they came from. null = any.

listId.description: entered_list (required), event_audience (null = every member). list_catalog/forms prints the listId of a form's audience.

eventId.description: The one event the journey is built around: event triggers, event-timed waits, event merge tags. From list_catalog/events. Clears seriesId.

seriesId.description: Instead of eventId: a repeating event, so every occurrence runs its own cohort. list_catalog/events prints it on each session of one. Event triggers only. Clears eventId.

attendeeListId.description: event_people: add people who attend to this contact list. null = off.

productId.description: checkout_abandoned: only checkouts of this shop product. null = any product. From list_catalog/products.

offerId.description: checkout_abandoned: an offer on shop products its emails show, as the offer tags, {offerCode} and the Their item card's price. An email that shows it also carries the shopper's code in its checkout link; one that does not (a plain nudge) links to the plain product page. null = a plain reminder. From list_catalog/offers. Community owner only, like an offer step. Each shopper gets their own {offerCode}.

codeDays.description: checkout_abandoned with an offerId: how many days each shopper's own code lasts, counted from the first email that shows the offer, to the end of that UTC day and never past the offer's end (default 3). Community owner only.

includeExisting.description: entered_list: also enrol everyone ALREADY on the list when it is turned on. Mails the whole list at once.

goal.description: Anyone who comes to match this leaves the journey early (e.g. is_paying on a sales sequence). null removes the goal.

anyOf.description: type is the test. course_completed needs courseId, has_tag needs tag, on_list needs listId, submitted_form needs formId; the rest take none.

trigger.description: Omit to keep the trigger it has. Naming one PATCHES it: fields left out keep their stored value. A field the type does not use is refused.

steps.description: Send [] to clear it. Omit to change only the trigger.

key.description: Names this step for edges. Send back the key manage_automation/read prints to keep a stored step (its offer and voice note ride it).

next.description: Where people go after it: a key, or null to end. Omitted = the next step in the list.

atHour.description: wait: release hour in the community's timezone.

attachIcs.description: send: attach the journey's event as a calendar invite.

body.description: send_dm. Required unless a voice note is kept.

voiceNote.description: send_dm: a stored step's recording. Kept by default; recordings are made in the console.

listId.description: list. Required. list_catalog/forms prints the listId of a form's audience.

condition.description: condition (required), or a wait_until that waits for it.

yes.description: condition: a key or null. Required.

no.description: condition: a key or null. Required.

paths.description: split: first match wins, top to bottom. Required.

condition.description: type is the test. course_completed needs courseId, has_tag needs tag, on_list needs listId, submitted_form needs formId; the rest take none.

next.description: A key, or null to end there. Required.

otherwise.description: split: where everyone else goes. Required.

maxDays.description: wait_until on a condition: the longest it holds. Default 7.

untilDate.description: wait_until: hold until YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or an ISO instant.

untilEvent.description: wait_until: timed from the journey's event.

offsetMins.description: Negative is before (-1440 = a day before), positive after.

any.description: Instead of an offset. before = a gate: people pass straight through while the event is still ahead, and a late arrival takes passed.

passed.description: wait_until with untilEvent.any before: where a late arrival goes. Omitted or null = they leave.

target.description: goto: the key of the step to hand people to.

title.description: create_offer: internal label. Required.

price.description: create_offer: the discounted membership price, whole units of the community's currency, below its standard price. Required.

interval.description: create_offer: the cadence discounted. Omit for the primary one.

tierId.description: create_offer: the membership tier (rung) it discounts, from list_catalog/membership_tiers. REQUIRED on a community that sells membership tiers, where the offer counts only on that rung and must be below that rung's price; omit on one that sells a single price. Checked against what the community sells when the journey goes live.

openDays.description: create_offer: days it stays open once opened, 0 = until closed. Default 7.

dropVoiceNotes.description: true to let this rewrite remove a message step that carries a voice note. Recordings cannot be made again from here.

live.description: true to turn it on, false to take it back to a draft.

recipe.description: Which ready-made journey to start from.

tools.name: manage_form
tools.title: Capture leads with a form, and read what people sent
tools.description:
A form collects an email address and sets off whatever you wire to it: a list, a tag, a file, an autoresponder. Reading the responses hands back the personal details people typed, so it is staff only.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new draft form. Collects nothing until you publish it.
- update: Its name, URL, questions (including a pre-fill name per question, whether to hide one that arrives pre-filled, show-if logic that hides a question or a whole step until earlier answers call for it, page breaks that split it into steps, quiz points, recalled answers in the wording, and the scale, ranking, matrix, website, time and hidden-from-the-link question types), outcomes by answer (a different audience or result per answer or quiz score), when it closes (a date or a response limit), the look and pacing of its page (one question per screen), success-screen copy, the audience a signup joins, the confirmation email each person is sent (one of the coach's saved emails), whether the coach is emailed each response, switching an already-uploaded freebie on or off and showing its download, a success-screen button, sending people somewhere instead of a success screen (a page, a link, a payment link, another published form, an event whose public page is on, a public guide or the published store), showing the logo and how big it is, whether submitting sells a product, and (for a community based in the EU/EEA, the UK or Canada) whether the form asks for marketing consent.
- publish: Publish the form so it starts collecting signups, or take it back to a draft. Publishing hands back the code to embed it on another website.
- responses: What people have submitted, newest first, with each person's email address and answers. Also the total and, on the first page, how the choice and rating answers fall and the 30-day drop-off (viewed, started, each step and question reached, submitted). Staff only.
- delete: Delete a DRAFT form nobody has filled in, unless a session type or another form still uses it. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

preset.description: general: An email field to start. Add fields and outcomes as you need them. waitlist: Collect emails for something coming soon. contact: Name, email, and a message field. leadMagnet: Trade a free file for an email. Needs a file.

name.description: What the form is called, and the heading visitors read. Defaults to the preset's own wording.

formId.description: From list_catalog/forms or manage_form/create. Read the form back with list_catalog/forms first: its questions carry the ids this call has to echo.

slug.description: The public URL segment: the form lives at /f/<slug>. Only changeable while the form is a draft.

fields.description: The whole question list, top to bottom: what is here IS the form afterwards. Omit it to leave the questions alone.

id.description: Keep the id a previous call printed to edit that question in place. Omit it for a new one.

type.description: email is always present and always required, whether you send it or not. heading and textBlock are copy on the form and collect no answer. pageBreak splits the form into steps: everything after it is the next step, reached by a button whose text is the break's label. url and time are validated answers; linearScale is a numbered scale (NPS); ranking orders its options; matrix asks every row to pick a column; hiddenValue is never shown and is filled only from the link (?key=value), needs a key, and is never required.

label.description: The question, or for heading/textBlock the words themselves, or for a pageBreak the button that leads to the next step (blank reads "Next"). {{key}} puts an earlier answer (the question with that key) in the words, and {{score}} a quiz total. A textBlock is formatted text: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

options.description: singleChoice, multiChoice and dropdown only. A choice question with no options cannot be published.

ratingMax.description: rating questions: the top of the scale.

key.description: The question's LINK NAME: a link ending ?plan=pro starts the question keyed plan filled in with pro, and {{plan}} recalls its answer in later wording. Letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, starting with a letter, unique within the form, and not score. email already works as a link name on every form without setting this.

hidden.description: Hide this question when it arrives already pre-filled, so somebody signed in is not asked for something we know. Needs a key, and it is ignored without one. The question still appears whenever the pre-filled value is missing or would be refused, so the form can never end up refusing an answer nobody can see. TODAY NOTHING PRE-FILLS A COACH'S OWN FORM: only Drry's console mints the signed token a pre-fill rides, so setting this changes nothing a visitor sees yet. Say that rather than reporting the question hidden.

points.description: QUIZ: points per option, in the same order as options (singleChoice, multiChoice, dropdown). The form's score is the sum over what was answered; route on it with fieldId _score. Omit for no scoring.

scored.description: rating and linearScale: the number picked counts towards the quiz score.

scaleMax.description: linearScale: where it ends. 0 to 10 is a Net Promoter question.

minLabel.description: linearScale: caption under the low end.

maxLabel.description: linearScale: caption under the high end.

rows.description: matrix: the rows. options are the columns every row picks from.

showIf.description: SHOW-IF LOGIC: the question appears only when these rules pass on the answers above it, and a hidden question is never required and never stored. On a pageBreak it skips the whole step that break starts. Not allowed on the email question or on the step that holds it. Omit (or null) for a question that is always shown. The reply prints what was stored, so a rule the form refused is visible there.

match.description: all = every rule must pass; any = one is enough.

fieldId.description: The id of a question ABOVE this one. A rule naming a later question is dropped.

op.description: answered / notAnswered for any question (checked or not, for a checkbox); equals / notEquals for text, number, rating, singleChoice and dropdown; contains / notContains for text and multiChoice; gt / lt for number and rating.

value.description: What to compare with. Omit for answered/notAnswered. For a choice question it must be one of its options, exactly.

successHeadline.description: The heading somebody sees after submitting.

submitLabel.description: The button they press. Defaults to "Submit".

audience.description: The contact list every submission joins, BY NAME: an existing audience with that exact name is used, otherwise one is created. This is what enrols somebody in a journey triggered by that audience, so say so before setting it. null takes the audience off, and the form then captures contacts without adding them to anything. Omit to leave whatever is wired.

sells.description: Turn this into a SELLING form: the slug of one of the community's products, taken from list_catalog/products. Submitting then opens checkout for it instead of showing a success screen, and NOBODY becomes a contact or joins the audience until the payment goes through. The product must be on sale (active, priced, with a file to deliver). null stops the form selling and puts its success screen back. Omit to leave it alone.

accent.description: This form's accent color as #rrggbb, or null for the community accent.

layout.description: card (the default, a raised card) or plain (fields straight on the page).

align.description: Headings and the step indicator: left (default) or center.

background.description: theme (default, the community background), tint (a soft wash of the accent) or accent (a bold accent backdrop; the form then always sits on a card).

flow.description: steps (default: the form's own page breaks) or focus (one question per screen, advancing on Enter, and by itself after a one-tap pick). Applies wherever the form appears, funnel pages included.

removeCover.description: Take the cover image off. A cover is uploaded in the console.

design.description: How the form's own page (/f/<slug>, and its embed) looks. Only the settings you name change. A form placed inside a funnel page takes that page's look instead.

routes.description: OUTCOMES BY ANSWER. Replaces the whole list; checked top to bottom after a submission and the FIRST whose rules pass swaps the audience and/or the result for that person. Nobody matching gets the form's own outcome. Ignored on a form that sells. null removes them all. Omit to leave them alone.

fieldId.description: Any question's id, or _score for the quiz total (on a form that scores).

audience.description: Join this audience BY NAME (found, or created) instead of the form's own. To keep an existing one, send its audienceId instead.

audienceId.description: Join this EXISTING audience, by the audienceId the read prints.

redirectUrl.description: Send them to this https link instead of a success screen.

redirectPage.description: Send them to this funnel page (its slug, as the read prints it) instead of a success screen.

redirectTo.description: Send them HERE instead of a success screen, in the shape the form's own redirectTo takes and the read prints: a reusable payment link, another published form, an event whose public page is on, a public guide, the published store, the blog or one published blog post (a page or an https link too). Send one of redirectTo, redirectUrl and redirectPage, not two.

closesAt.description: An ISO date-time after which the form stops taking responses. null removes it.

maxResponses.description: Stop after this many responses (enforced strictly). null removes it.

closedMessage.description: What people read once it is closed.

limits.description: When the form stops taking responses. Only the settings you name change.

redirectTo.description: Send people HERE after they submit instead of showing a success screen: {"kind":"page","slug":"<a funnel page slug>"}, {"kind":"paymentLink","token":"<a reusable payment link token>"}, {"kind":"form","slug":"<another published form's slug>"}, {"kind":"event","id":"<an event whose public page is on>"}, {"kind":"guide","slug":"<a public guide's share slug>"}, {"kind":"store"} (the published store), {"kind":"blog"} (the blog's front page, while the blog is on), {"kind":"blogPost","postId":"<a published post's id, from manage_blog/read>"} (follows the post's current link) or {"kind":"external","url":"<an https:// URL>"}. They are still stored as a contact first. null puts the success screen back (with default copy, unless successHeadline/successMessage are sent in the same call). Omit to leave it alone.

successButton.description: A button under the success screen's message. join (the community's join page) takes nothing else; page takes `slug`; surface takes `surface` (library, community, audio, events); course takes `courseId`; paymentLink takes a reusable link's `token`; blog takes nothing else (the blog's front page); blogPost takes a published post's postId (from manage_blog/read); external takes an https `url`. A destination the community does not have is refused with the ones it has. null takes the button off. Success screen only.

showDownload.description: Put the freebie's download button on the success screen. Needs the freebie on (deliverFile) and a success screen.

deliverFile.description: Switch the FREEBIE on or off: the file every signup is given. The file itself is uploaded in the console (media upload is not on the connector), so true needs a file already attached, which the read names. Off keeps the file for later. Paused while the form sells.

confirmationEmailId.description: The CONFIRMATION EMAIL each person who submits is sent: the emailId of one of the coach's saved emails, from manage_email/read (write one with manage_email/create). It is sent as saved, to everyone who fills the form in, so say so before setting it. A session type's booking confirmation cannot be used here. null sends no email. Paused while the form sells.

emailMeEachResponse.description: Email the coach a copy of every response, with reply-to set to the person who filled it in.

showLogo.description: Show the community's logo (or wordmark) at the top of the form's own page. On by default.

askConsent.description: The form's MARKETING CONSENT box, ONLY for a community based in the EU/EEA, the UK or Canada (list_catalog/forms with a formId says whether this one is; anywhere else it is refused, since no form there asks). true (the default) shows an "Email me occasional updates" box above the button, and only people who tick it join the mailing list. false turns the box off for this form, so everyone who submits joins the list: right for a form that IS a signup for the coach's emails, and the coach's responsibility, so confirm it with them first.

logoSize.description: How big that logo (or wordmark) is on the form's own page: small, medium (the default) or large. Kept while the logo is hidden, so it applies when showLogo is switched back on. Never shown in an embed.

published.description: true to open it to the public, false to close it.

cursor.description: The `cursor` the previous call returned. Omit for the newest responses.

tools.name: manage_booking
tools.title: Set up the booking calendar
tools.description:
The session types a member or a stranger can book, and the hours you are open for them.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new session type, created PAUSED: it takes bookings once resumed (manage_booking/update) and once hours are set.
- update: Wording, length, its own weekly hours or the coach's, how often it offers a start time, buffers, notice, caps, which owner or admin hosts it, which of the coach's saved emails a booker is sent as their confirmation (only the first one; the calendar invite and join link are always attached; null for the built-in), and whether it is listed or taking bookings.
- duplicate: A PAUSED duplicate of a session type with its own settings, a link made from the name you give it (else the original's plus -copy), and its own copy of any confirmation email. Not its intake form, and free until a product is linked in the console. Refused, with nothing written, when the original's member-tier limit cannot carry over. A session in a Drry room or on Google Meet is duplicated in the console.
- reorder: The order they are offered in. Send every id.
- availability: The weekly hours you accept bookings in, one-off dates (closed all day, different hours, or busy for part of the day), and the defaults every session type inherits. A session type with its own hours keeps them.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

description.description: What the session is, shown on the booking page. RICH TEXT, and a plain sentence is the normal thing to send: it is stored as one paragraph, with any angle brackets in it kept as written. To format, send real HTML with CLOSING tags (paragraphs, bold, italic, underline, bulleted and numbered lists, links, line breaks, and also quotes, code, rules and headings, though only h2 and h3 are headings here, an h1 or an h4 keeps its words and loses its heading-ness, and the console's own editor offers only the first set); anything else, scripts and event handlers included, is dropped at render. IT IS ONE CHOICE FOR THE WHOLE VALUE: a single closing tag anywhere makes all of it HTML, so once you format any part of it, write a literal less-than as < or the rest of that sentence is read as a tag and dropped. Markdown is NOT converted, so asterisks around a word show up as asterisks.

meetingUrl.description: The coach's own meeting room for THIS type, e.g. their standing Zoom or Meet link. Full URL starting https://. Without it the type falls back to the community's standing meeting link, and, once it is active, shows no times only if there is no standing one either. A newly created type is PAUSED regardless of this field, and stays that way until manage_booking/update sets active: true.

phoneField.description: Whether the booking form asks for a phone number. Defaults to off.

hostUserId.description: Who runs sessions of this type: their name goes on the calendar invite and the confirmation email, and the booking, moved and cancelled emails go to them. It must be somebody who already owns or administers this community, and anyone else is refused. null hands it back to the owner. Omit to leave it alone. It does NOT give them a way into the video room. To give this session different hours, send ownHours instead.

startTimeIncrementMins.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

bufferBeforeMins.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

bufferAfterMins.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

minNoticeHours.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

horizonDays.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

maxPerDay.description: Most of this session in one day. null is uncapped.

ownHours.description: THIS session's own weekly hours, replacing the coach's for this session only ("intro calls on Tuesday mornings"). Ranges are 24 hour HH:MM per weekday, like "09:00" to "12:00". It is a PATCH: days you leave out keep what this session offers now, which is the coach's hours if it had none of its own yet, so to offer ONLY some days send every other day as an empty list. A day sent as an empty list is switched off. null goes back to following the coach's hours, set with manage_booking/availability. The coach's timezone, days off and existing bookings still apply, and one-off hours the coach set for a date can only shorten this session's hours on that date, never add to them. The reply prints the week stored.

confirmationEmailId.description: The email sent to the person who books, in place of the built-in confirmation: the emailId of one of this community's saved emails (manage_email/read with no emailId lists them; manage_email/create drafts a new one). It must not be sent or sending, and not already an automation's, a funnel form's or a form's confirmation email. Two session types may share one. Only the first confirmation is replaced: moves, cancellations and reminders still use the built-in emails, and the calendar invite and join link are always attached. null goes back to the built-in confirmation. Omit to leave it alone.

listed.description: Show it on the public booking index. false keeps the direct link working: unlisted is not private.

active.description: false pauses it: the page stops taking bookings and its link 404s. Bookings already taken are untouched.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. Europe/London. Every hour below is read in it, and until one is set nothing is bookable at all.

hours.description: Working hours per weekday, each range 24 hour HH:MM ("09:00" to "17:30"). Days you leave out are untouched.

daysOff.description: Dates the coach is closed ALL DAY, YYYY-MM-DD. REPLACES every closed-all-day date, so send every one you want kept: read the current ones from list_catalog/booking_types, which prints this community's availability above its session types. Dates with different hours or busy times are left alone. To change one date without resending the rest, use oneOffDates.

oneOffDates.description: Set or clear single dates. MERGED BY DATE: each date sent becomes exactly what is sent, replacing whatever it had, and every date not sent is left as it is. Applied after daysOff when both are sent. Each date may appear once.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a day in the coach's timezone.

happens.description: closed: no times that day. hours: the times listed REPLACE the usual hours. busy: the times listed are taken OUT of the usual hours, the rest stand. clear: remove this date so the usual hours apply.

times.description: Needed for hours and busy, 24 hour HH:MM, each ending after it starts.

tools.name: manage_event
tools.title: Schedule a session, and read and set its ticket prices
tools.description:
Events on the community calendar: in person, somebody else's event, online by a pasted link, or hosted in a Drry video room or webinar, for every member or for specific people invited by email. New events are drafts; publishing, cancelling and moving a published one mail people, so confirm those with the coach in the same turn.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new DRAFT event: in person, external, online by a pasted meeting link or a new Google Meet link Drry makes on the community's connected Google account (`generateMeet`, instead of `joinUrl`; an owner or admin connects Google in the console), a Drry video room (Creator) or a Drry webinar (Growth). `visibility` is community (every member, the default) or private (only the people in `invitees`, up to 50 email addresses): ask the coach which. Invitees are saved on the draft and invited only when it is published; inviting by email, members included, needs the Creator plan (on Free leave `invitees` out); a private session may also be made with nobody invited. Can name which owner or admin hosts it. No price or seat limit.
- duplicate: A new DRAFT copied from an existing event: same details, cover and host, a week later unless `startsAt` says when. Keeps the membership limit, or refuses by name when it cannot (not on this plan, or a membership no longer sold). Always a community event, whatever the original was: a public original loses its public page and any invite to every member, and the answer says so. Never the invite list or contact lists; refuses an invite-only event and an event that sells tickets; needs a new `joinUrl` when the original uses a Google Meet room.
- update: Change an event's time, place, details, listing or host (not who is invited), by series scope, or make a DRAFT one-off repeat with `recurrence` (every new date a draft). Moving a PUBLISHED event mails the change to everyone holding it. Confirm first.
- publish: Publish a draft event and its draft series dates. Sends the invites, the announcement and the reminders at once (they count toward the monthly email allowance), and cannot be undone. A private event with nobody invited publishes and sends no invites. Confirm first.
- cancel: Cancel an event, or this and later dates, or a whole series. Mails a cancellation to everyone holding it. Refuses an event people have paid for. Confirm first.
- prices: A paid event's ticket prices: the regular price, the price in effect now, what a buyer with no link or code pays after the best automatic offer, every price change, and every offer on the event with its code. Owner or admin.
- set_price_changes: Replace a paid event's price changes (a name, a price in whole units and the moment it takes over, at most 5; an empty list removes them). From its start a change IS the ticket price; strangers are charged it, people who already bought keep what they paid. An early bird below the regular price is manage_offer/create_purchase_offer. Owner or admin.
- recording_shares: An ended event's recordings: each one's status, who sees it on the members' events page, whether it may be shared by a private link (and why not), whether a link is on and until when, and how many share emails went out by outcome. Never the link and never who was emailed. Owner or admin.
- revoke_recording_link: Turn off a recording's private share link: every copy stops working and share emails not yet sent are canceled. Making a link and emailing it stay in the console. Owner or admin.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

description.description: What the session is. Plain text.

format.description: in_person: somewhere physical, set `location`. external: somebody else's event, set `joinUrl`. online_link: an online session, EITHER `joinUrl` (a real meeting link) OR `generateMeet: true`, never both. drry_room: hosted in a Drry video room, members join from the event page, no `joinUrl`. drry_webinar: a Drry broadcast where the audience watches and can be brought on stage, no `joinUrl`.

startsAt.description: When it starts, as an ISO 8601 instant, e.g. 2026-10-02T18:00:00Z.

durationMins.description: How long, in minutes. Defaults to 60, at most 480.

timezone.description: IANA zone the times are shown in, e.g. Europe/London. Defaults to UTC.

location.description: Where it is. in_person events only.

joinUrl.description: The link members join or read about it at. Required for online_link unless `generateMeet` is true, optional for external, ignored for in_person, refused for drry_room and drry_webinar (the room is the door). Must start with http:// or https://.

generateMeet.description: online_link only: true makes a new Google Meet link on the community's connected Google account and stores it as the join link, instead of a pasted `joinUrl` (send one or the other, never both). Needs Google connected in the console (Events, Settings), which an owner or admin does; refused, saying so, when it is not. Each link is a real, permanent Meet room on that account, made only once everything else in the call is accepted. Refused on every other format.

listed.description: Show it on the member Events tab once published. Defaults to true. Only applies to a community event.

visibility.description: community: every member of the community can see and join it. private: only the people in `invitees` can. Defaults to community. Ask the coach which they mean rather than assuming.

invitees.description: private only: the email addresses to invite, at most 50. Someone who already has an account here is invited as a member and everyone else by email. Saved on the draft; NOBODY is emailed until manage_event/publish. Refused with a community event. Inviting anyone by email, members included, needs the Creator plan; on Free leave this out and pick members in the console. Omit for a private session nobody is invited to yet.

hostUserId.description: Who runs the session: their name goes on the calendar invite sent to everyone who is coming, and the reminders go to them. It must be somebody who already owns or administers this community, and anyone else is refused. Omit to leave it with whoever created it. It does NOT give them a way into the video room, and it is not how to invite anybody (that is `invitees`).

eventId.description: The event to copy, from list_catalog/events.

recurrence.description: Make a DRAFT one-off repeat: it becomes the first date of a series and the rest are added as drafts, starting from its start time (after any startsAt sent in the same call). Nobody is told; publishing it publishes every date. Refused on a published, canceled or booked event, an instant meeting, one that already repeats, and, for an editor, a paid event.

interval.description: Every N days, weeks or months. Defaults to 1.

monthlyMode.description: Monthly only: dayOfMonth repeats on the same date (the 14th; a month without that date is skipped), weekdayOfMonth on the same weekday position (the first Saturday). Defaults to dayOfMonth.

count.description: How many dates in all, counting this one: 2 to 52.

scope.description: For a recurring series only: this date (the default), this and every later date, or every date. Ignored on a one-off.

acknowledgeJourneys.description: Set true only after the coach has been told which live journeys are built around this event and still wants it cancelled. The first call without it names them.

label.description: A short name buyers never see, e.g. "Last minute".

price.description: The ticket price from then on, in WHOLE units of the community's own currency (99 means $99 for a US community, 99.5 means $99.50), at least the currency's minimum charge.

startsAt.description: When it takes over, ISO 8601 with a timezone. Each change needs its own moment.

priceChanges.description: The whole list. It replaces what is there; an empty list removes every price change.

tools.name: manage_audio
tools.title: Run the audio library
tools.description:
Tracks and the collections they sit in. Files are uploaded in the console; everything about them is set here.

Set `act` to one of:
- create_collection: A new collection for tracks to sit in, which is how members browse the audio library.
- update_collection: Rename a collection or move it.
- update_track: Title, description, tags, collection, position, and when members can open it (the lesson release rules: days after joining, or a fixed date).
- publish_track: Make a track audible now, or take it back to a draft. Queues the new-drops email, dripped or not, as a lesson does.
- set_chapters: Chapter marks inside a long track, so a listener can skip.
- podcast_show: The private podcast's show details in members' apps: title, host, description, category, language, explicit, newest-first or serial. Growth. Read them back with list_catalog/audio_tracks.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

description.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

collectionId.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

position.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

tags.description: Replaces the whole tag list. Send [] to clear them.

release.description: When members can open it, the same rules manage_course/update_lesson uses. "always" = as soon as it is published. "days_after_joining" needs releaseDays and is counted separately for every member. "on_a_date" needs releaseDate and opens it for everyone at once. Omit to leave it alone. Either way the new-drops email goes out when the track is published, as it does for a lesson.

releaseDays.description: Days after a member joins. Required for "days_after_joining".

releaseDate.description: For "on_a_date": the day it opens, as YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO timestamp. A bare date means midnight UTC of that day.

published.description: true to publish, false to take it back to a draft.

atSeconds.description: Where the chapter starts, in whole seconds from the beginning. A chapter at or past the track's length is dropped.

title.description: What a member reads in the chapter list.

chapters.description: The complete chapter list, at most 30. Send [] to clear them.

author.description: The host shown as author. "" falls back to the wordmark.

category.description: An Apple Podcasts top-level category, spelled exactly.

language.description: The show's language code, e.g. en, es, fr.

showType.description: episodic = newest first; serial = oldest first, numbered.

tools.name: manage_file_library
tools.title: Read and run the Resources library of member files
tools.description:
The Resources tab: free files (PDFs, worksheets, slides) members download, and links to pages elsewhere, in folders. Files and covers are uploaded in the console; here you add links and arrange, describe, publish and email about everything.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One file or link in full (a link's address, downloads and views or opens), or the library: folders with counts and a page of files and links, searchable and filterable. Start here.
- update: A file's or link's title or description, a link's address (url) or whether it opens inside the community (openInside), or move it into a folder or out of every folder (folderId "unfiled"). Not an uploaded file itself, its cover or its status.
- add_link: Add a link to a page elsewhere (https), as a draft; with no title, the page's own; openInside shows it inside the community in a frame instead of a new tab. No cover photo.
- publish: Publish files or take them back to drafts. With emailMembers, also one email to members who can open them (owner or admin only; counts on the email allowance).
- reorder: The order of the files in one folder, or in Unfiled (folderId "unfiled"). Send every id.
- email_members: Email members about files already published, one email each. Owner or admin only; counts on the email allowance; at most 20 community emails a member a day.
- create_folder: A new folder with a title and description.
- update_folder: Rename a folder or change its description.
- reorder_folders: The order folders appear in. Send every folderId.
- delete: Delete a file that was never published or downloaded. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

resourceId.description: One file. Omit for the library.

folderId.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

status.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

description.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

url.description: A link's new address (https). Refused for an uploaded file.

openInside.description: A LINK only. true shows the page INSIDE the community (in a frame on its own page, under the community's header) instead of in a new tab; false puts it back in a new tab. A page on Drry itself is refused. Some sites refuse to be shown inside another site, so suggest the coach opens it once to check.

resourceIds.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

emailMembers.description: Default false. Confirm with the coach first: it reaches members.

tools.name: manage_blog
tools.title: Read, write and publish the blog
tools.description:
The blog: posts a coach writes for readers, each a draft until it is published. Images and covers are uploaded in the console; here you write, publish and arrange.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The blog's settings and every post with its state, review state, assignee, open team comment threads and who is editing it right now (Growth), or only the posts that match a search query, or one post in full with its body as the block list write takes, its version (which approve takes as ifUpdatedAt), and who holds it in the editor and who else has it open. Start here.
- create: A new post, always a draft nobody can see; from a template when given its templateId.
- write: A post's title, subtitle, excerpt, search text, cover alt and position (or take the cover off), and its whole body as blocks (replaced, not appended), including funnel sections (a booking, an offer, a form) shown inside the post, buttons to any page, course, offer or link, cards that show a course, event, product, guide, session or page as it is today, galleries of photos the post already holds, Spotify, Instagram or TikTok embeds, tables, bookmarks to other sites, two or three columns side by side (stacked on a phone), @ mentions of a course, event, product, guide, session, page, lesson, audio track, membership offer or another post inside the prose (a link under its name as it is when read), and the members-only line (a paywall block) where a members post's free part ends. A live post's changes wait until publish. A post a teammate is editing in the console is refused by name unless takeOver is true, which takes over from them (their editor turns read-only).
