- link: The post's link, /blog/<link>. Applies at once, live or not; a post that was ever live keeps its old link working. A link set here stays put; a draft's otherwise follows its title.
- feature: Feature a post on the blog home, or stop.
- audience: Who can read a post: everyone, members, or members on a tier and up. Everyone still sees its title, cover, excerpt and what sits above its members-only line; an email made from it after that carries only that, and its waiting launch email is remade. With a tier, hidden makes it vanish for everyone below the tier (no listing, a 404 at its link) instead of showing a lock. Applies at once. A tier, and hiding, are the owner's or an admin's to set. A post cannot be opened to more people than who can read the whole blog (manage_blog/settings whoCanRead).
- publish: Make a draft live, or a live post's waiting changes live. Anyone can read it while the blog is on. A first publish also emails the blog's subscribers when the coach has that on (emailSubscribers false skips it), and, while the members' new-content email is on, joins it (leaving out anyone an email of the post already reached); a post scheduled with its own email sends that instead. Where editors' posts need approval, an editor is refused and uses manage_blog/submit_review.
- unpublish: Take a live post off the blog; it becomes a draft with every word kept.
- schedule: Set a draft to go live on its own at a time (an ISO date-time with its offset), or move its time. Going live emails the blog's subscribers when the coach has that on (emailSubscribers false stops it); an email the coach set up in the console goes instead.
- unschedule: Take a post off the schedule; it stays a draft.
- email: Make a draft email from a live post, for the coach to address and send in the console. Sends nothing.
- discard: Throw away a live post's unpublished changes. They stay in the post's history, so restore can bring them back. Refused while a teammate is editing it, unless takeOver is true.
- history: A post's earlier versions, newest first, with who and through which door; with a versionId, what restoring it would change.
- templates: The saved post templates, each with what it is for, its first headings and how many pictures and words. Start a post from one with create.
- save_template: Save a post's shape (title, words, layout, pictures) as a template for the next post.
- rename_template: Rename a template or change what it says it is for. Deleting one is done in the console.
- score: A post scored 0 to 100 against a checklist that needs no readers, worst first, each open check naming the act and field that fixes it.
- stats: How the blog, or one post with postId, is doing over a range (30d, 90d, 12mo, all; clamped to the plan's history): views, readers, reads and read rate, where readers came from, subscribers gained, free and paid joins, sales, and the revenue they took net of refunds, top posts, by category and on Growth by author, and a post's emails with their opens and clicks. Counts, never who. Owner or admin, Creator and up.
- import_preview: Read another blog by its address (or one post), and say what bringing it over would add: posts, pictures, categories, authors, and what will not come across. Writes nothing. Owner or admin only.
- imports: How bringing a blog over went: each recent import's progress, then one import's report (posts brought over, pictures copied, what was renamed or left out and why). Reads only; starting and undoing an import are in the console. Owner or admin only.
- bulk: One change across many posts: publish, publish imported drafts with their original dates, unpublish, delete never-published drafts, add or remove a category, set the authors, or schedule or unschedule them. Publishing them never emails the subscribers; a scheduled post that goes live does, when the coach has that on (emailSubscribers false stops it). Refusals are named.
- restore: Put an earlier version back. Undoable; on a live post it waits for publish and keeps the link; a never-published draft's link follows the restored title. Refused while a teammate is editing it, unless takeOver is true.
- settings: Turn the blog on or off, and set its kind, name, headline and intro, its subscribe band (which published form it shows, its words, and whether it shows the subscriber count), stop emailing new posts to subscribers, its own address word (instead of /blog, which keeps forwarding), its home layout (grid, list or magazine), whether members get a Blog tab in their menu (inMemberMenu), who can read the whole blog (whoCanRead: everyone, members, or a tier and up, moving every post below it up and putting them back when set back), whether it is the homepage of the community's address, and whether editors' posts need approval (Growth). Owner or admin only.
- subscribe_form: Make and publish a new email-only form that puts readers on a list named for the blog, and show it as the subscribe band. Owner or admin only.
- delete: Delete a post that was never published. Cannot be undone. Refused while a teammate is editing it, unless takeOver is true.
- save_category: Add a category, or rename one or change its description; its link never changes. Owner or admin only.
- reorder_categories: Put the categories in the order readers see them. Owner or admin only.
- post_categories: Replace a post's categories, in order; the first is named on its card. Live at once on a live post.
- save_author: Add a guest author, set up a teammate's profile, or edit a name, title, bio or links. A photo is uploaded in the console.
- post_authors: Say who a post is by, in order; nobody means the owner. Live at once on a live post.
- submit_review: Send a post to the owner or an admin for approval, which is how an editor's post goes live where editors' posts need approval. Publishes nothing.
- approve: Approve a post waiting for review: publish it now, or schedule it with at. Pass ifUpdatedAt (the version read printed) to approve only what was read. Approving is publishing (public, and a first publish can email subscribers). Owner or admin only.
- send_back: Return a post waiting for review to its writer with a note saying what to change. Owner or admin only.
- assign: Assign a post to a teammate (a userId from read's Team line) and set its due date, or clear either. A teammate it newly goes to, other than the caller, is told by email and in the console; a due date alone tells nobody. Setting is Growth; clearing is any plan.
- comments: A post's internal team comment threads: what each is on (quoted words, a block, or the whole post) and whether that is still in the post, open or resolved, and every comment with its commentId, who wrote it, when, whether it was edited, and whom it mentions. Open only unless include is all. Only the team sees them. Any plan.
- comment: Start a team comment thread on a post (on exact words given as quote, or the whole post), or reply in one with threadId (a resolved thread opens again), mentioning teammates by userId from read's Team line. Mentioned teammates, and on a reply whoever started or was mentioned in the thread, are told by email and in the console. Growth.
- edit_comment: Change the words of a team comment the caller wrote (a commentId from manage_blog/comments), and with mentionUserIds who it mentions; it then shows as edited. Only its writer can. A teammate newly mentioned is told by email and in the console; one taken out is not un-told. Growth.
- resolve_comment: Resolve a team comment thread, or reopen it with resolved false. Nobody is notified. Resolving is any plan; reopening is Growth. Deleting a comment is done in the console.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

postId.description: One post. Omit for the whole blog.

query.description: Words to find in the posts (the last one may be half typed; quote a phrase). Lists only the matching posts, best first. A live post with unpublished changes is matched by the words readers see. Not with postId.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

templateId.description: Start from this template, from manage_blog/templates.

coverAlt.description: Only when the post has a cover.

removeCover.description: Take the cover off. Its file is kept with the post; a new cover is added in the console.

blocks.description: The whole body, at most 300 blocks. Omit to leave it alone.

items.description:
One block. richText {html}: paragraphs,

/

, lists, quotes, bold, italic, links, and @ mentions. A MENTION names one page|course|event|product|booking|guide|lesson|audio|offer|post from the community inline, inside any html (richText, callout, toggle): Label, REF being a course's courseId, an event's id, a session's typeSlug (empty for the booking page) or a guide's, product's or page's slug, exactly as a card's link names it (course:, guide:), or a lesson's lessonId, an audio track's trackId, a membership offer's offerId or another post's postId (lesson:, audio:, offer:, post:), which no card shows; an offer is always drawn under Label, since its name is internal. The post draws it as a link under the thing's name as it is when read, so a rename follows; Label is what shows if the thing is gone, a draft or not public (then it is plain words, never a dead link). image {key, alt, caption, width: normal|wide|full}: only a key the post already holds. gallery {images: [{key, alt}], caption, layout: grid|feature}: 1 to 12 photos shown together (feature draws the first one large); each key must be one the post already holds, as an image block's. video {provider: youtube|loom|vimeo, videoId, caption}. embed {ref, caption, provider: spotify|instagram|tiktok}: a Spotify episode, show, track, album, playlist or artist, an Instagram post or reel, or a TikTok, played inside the post. ref is the share link (its host decides the provider, so provider is needed only with a bare ref such as episode/ as manage_blog/read prints it); a YouTube, Loom or Vimeo link is a video block. table {rows, header: row|none, caption}: rows is a list of rows, each a list of plain-text cells (no html), at most 50 rows of 8 cells and 500 characters a cell; a short row is padded with empty cells; header row makes the first row the column headings. bookmark {url, title, description, siteName, imageKey}: a link to another site drawn as a card; url is an https address, and the connector does not read the page, so send the title and description the card should show; imageKey is only a key the post already holds (a bookmark's picture is copied in when a coach adds it in the console), or leave it out. callout {tone: tip|note|careful, html}. pullQuote {text}. divider {}. paywall {}: the members-only line, at most one; on a post for members everything above it is the free part anybody reads and everything below it only members read (who can read the post is set with manage_blog/audience; on a public post the line does nothing). code {language, code}: a sample shown exactly as typed, with a copy button; language is a short label like json. toggle {summary, html}: a line readers tap to open the words under it. toc {title}: a list of the post's own h2 and h3 headings, linked, which follows them as they change. button {label, link, style: solid|outline, align: start|center}: one button; link is a destination in the shape manage_page/edit_section takes for a button's ctaLink, and leaving it out sends readers to the join page. A post has no section to jump to and no checkout of its own, so there is no anchor kind and no buyHere: a product button opens the product's page and a booking button the booking page. (A call to action inside an embedded funnel SECTION is different: there buyHere opens checkout or the time picker in place, as on a page.) card {link}: one page|course|event|product|booking|guide from the community, drawn live from the thing itself (its cover, title and one fact such as a price, a date or a lesson count) whenever the post is read; link is required, in the same shape as a button's, of those kinds only, and a card for something a visitor cannot open (a draft, a private guide, a canceled event) is left out of the post. section {section}: one funnel section shown inside the post, in the shape manage_page/insert_section takes, of type form|booking|offer|ctaBanner|faq|steps|statsBand|pricing (a booking, the membership offer, a form, a call to action, a price table, questions, steps or numbers). Send a section back with the id manage_blog/read printed to keep it as it is; a section in a post holds no photo. columns {columns: [{blocks}, ...]}: 2 or 3 columns side by side (stacked on a phone, column by column), each a list of up to 30 blocks of any kind above except columns and paywall (a column holds no columns and no members-only line; put the line above the columns). Every block in a column counts toward the 300 a body holds.

takeOver.description: Only when manage_blog/read says a teammate is editing this post: take over from them. If they have it open in the console, their editor turns read-only and anything they typed in the last few seconds may not be saved. Ask the coach first.

tierId.description: With members: the tier a reader must hold, or above. Omit or null for any member.

hidden.description: With a tierId: true hides the post from everyone below the tier (no lock card, no listing, a 404 at its link); false shows it to them with a lock. Left out, a post keeping its tier keeps what it has.

emailSubscribers.description: false publishes without emailing the subscribers. Leave it out to follow the coach's choice; true is taken only when that choice is already on (turning email on is the coach's to do in the console).

at.description: When it goes live: an ISO date-time with its offset.

versionId.description: A version from this list, to read what restoring it changes.

name.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

description.description: What it is for, in a line.

range.description: 30d (the default), 90d, 12mo or all. Longer than the plan's history is clamped and the answer says so.

source.description: feed: a whole blog by its address. url: one post by its address.

url.description: The address, as a person would type it.

importId.description: One import, from an earlier answer. Leave out for the newest.

authorRefs.description: For set_authors: authorRefs from manage_blog/read, in byline order; an empty list bylines them to the owner.

spread.description: For schedule: none (all at once, the default), day (one a day) or week (one a week).

kind.description: What the blog is for. It changes nothing readers see: who can read is set per post (manage_blog/audience) or for the whole blog (whoCanRead), whichever kind is set.

label.description: The blog's name in menus, for example Journal. Empty goes back to the default name.

subscribeFormId.description: The published form the subscribe band shows (from list_catalog/forms). An empty string takes the band down. A draft form is refused. To make a new one, use manage_blog/subscribe_form instead.

subscribeCount.description: Show "Join N readers" on the band, counted from the form's list. Off by default; the coach's call.

emailNewPosts.description: false stops emailing each new post to the band's list on its first publish. Only false is taken here: turning it on sends email to people, so it is the coach's to do in the console.

homeLayout.description: How the blog's home lists posts; its category and author pages follow it. grid: The newest post large, then cards in rows of three. list: One post per row: the date, the title, a line about it and a small picture. magazine: A lead story, two beside each other under it, then the rest as a tight list. grid is what every blog starts on.

subscribeHeading.description: The band's heading. Empty uses "Get new posts by email".

subscribeBody.description: The line under it. Empty uses "One email when something new goes up. Unsubscribe any time.".

path.description: The blog's own address word, so it lives at /<word> instead of /blog (for example journal). Lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, 2 to 48 characters, and not a word another page uses or the bio link's. An empty string puts it back at /blog. /blog and every earlier word keep forwarding to it.

homepage.description: true makes the blog the homepage of the community's address (the blog must be on, or be turned on in the same call); false gives the root back to the join page. manage_blog/read says what holds it now.

inMemberMenu.description: Show the blog in the member menu: true gives members a tab named after the blog (label) that opens the blog while it is on; false takes the tab out. On by default.

whoCanRead.description: Who can read the WHOLE blog. members: every post open to more people becomes members-only at once (each keeps its title, cover, excerpt and anything above its members-only line public), and new and imported posts start members-only; no post can then be set open to more people. everyone puts back exactly the posts this setting moved; posts the coach limited themselves stay. A waiting launch email on a post that moves is remade from the post as it now is. Owner or admin only. Confirm with the coach first.

whoCanReadTierId.description: With whoCanRead members: limit the whole blog to members on this tier and up (a tierId from list_catalog/membership_tiers, not the entry one). Growth, to set a new one. Left out, any member.

reviewEditorPosts.description: Editors' posts need approval: true makes an editor's publish, schedule and bulk publish wait for the owner or an admin (the editor uses manage_blog/submit_review; staff answer with manage_blog/approve or manage_blog/send_back); false lets editors publish their own posts. Turning it on is a Growth feature (Available on the Growth plan).

categoryIds.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

authorId.description: From manage_blog/read, to edit an author with a profile.

userId.description: A teammate's user id (their authorRef without user:), to set up their profile.

bio.description: Plain text; a blank line starts a new paragraph.

ifUpdatedAt.description: The post's Version as manage_blog/read printed it. The approval is refused, and nothing changes, when the post was edited after that read, so what goes live is what was read. Without it, the post as it is when this call reads it.

note.description: What needs changing. Plain text; paragraphs are kept.

assigneeUserId.description: A userId from the Team line of manage_blog/read, or null for nobody.

dueAt.description: A day like 2026-10-09, or an ISO date-time with its offset, or null for none.

include.description: open (the default) or all, which adds resolved threads.

threadId.description: A threadId from manage_blog/comments, to reply in that thread.

quote.description: For a new thread: the exact words of the post it is about. Leave out to comment on the whole post.

body.description: The comment. Plain text; paragraphs are kept.

mentionUserIds.description: Teammates to mention: userIds from the Team line of manage_blog/read.

commentId.description: A commentId from manage_blog/comments, of a comment the caller wrote.

tools.name: manage_transcript
tools.title: Read and fix a transcript
tools.description:
The words a track or a video was transcribed to, and the corrections you make to them.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The transcript as it stands, with its hash.
- edit: Correct a passage. Needs the hash the read returned.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

trackId.description: From list_catalog/audio_tracks. Name this OR lessonId, not both.

lessonId.description: From manage_course/read. Name this OR trackId, not both.

fromIndex.description: Start reading at this line number. 200 lines come back per call.

transcriptHash.description: The fingerprint manage_transcript/read printed. It proves you are fixing the transcript you read; a stale one is refused rather than written over somebody else's corrections.

text.description: The whole corrected line. It replaces that line's words.

edits.description: Only the lines you are changing. Others are left alone.

tools.name: manage_tier
tools.title: Read and build a membership ladder, and gate content by it
tools.description:
The rungs a community sells, and what each one opens. Add a rung, rename it, price it, archive it, and point a course, guide, event, track, or Resources file or folder at it so only members at that rung or above can open it (a blog post's rung is set with manage_blog/audience). A price is for new members; everyone already on a rung keeps the rate they joined at. Confirm prices and archives with the coach first.

Set `act` to one of:
- list: The rungs you can gate at, with their ids.
- set_gate: Put a row behind a rung, locked or hidden.
- create: Add a rung above the ones that exist, WITHOUT a price: it is never sold and no upgrade prompt names it until it is priced with price. Never the first rung on a community: on one that already charges, that rung takes over the live price, so it stays a console step. Owner only.
- rename: Change a rung's NAME or its description, the words members read beside their charge. Members keep their rate.
- price: Set a rung's price for new members, whole units, with an optional second price on the other cadence. An unpriced rung goes on sale when priced; everyone already on it keeps their rate. Growth, owner only.
- archive: Stop selling a rung; everyone on it keeps it and keeps paying. Refused while content is limited to it unless forced. Cannot be undone. Any plan, owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

kind.description: What sort of thing is being limited.

tierId.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

visibility.description: "locked" (the default) shows members below the tier a locked card naming the membership that opens it, which is what sells the upgrade. "hidden" makes it vanish for them entirely. Ignored when tierId is null.

name.description: What members will see this rung called. The coach's words, not a stock name.

description.description: What this rung offers, in the coach's words. Omit to leave it blank and write it later.

interval.description: Which cadence the coach intends to bill this rung on, month by default. It sets no price and charges nobody; manage_tier/price does that.

currentName.description: The tier's name right now, exactly as list_catalog/membership_tiers prints it.

price.description: The main price in WHOLE units of the community's currency (99 is $99 for a US community). There is a minimum per currency; the server names it when it refuses.

altPrice.description: A second price on the OTHER cadence, whole units. Null or 0 removes it. Omitted keeps the one the rung has, unless the main cadence changes, when it must be given.

force.description: Archive even though content is limited to it, hiding that content from every member until it is re-pointed.

tools.name: manage_product
tools.title: Create, price and sell a product, and set what it delivers
tools.description:
The community's shop: make a product (always a draft), set its name, PRICE and description, put it on sale or archive it, the shop's refund policy, and what each product delivers and offers alongside itself. A price is what a stranger's card is charged on a public page, so confirm prices and going on sale with the coach first. A product's file and cover photo are uploaded in the console, and deleting one stays there too (archive stops selling). Read them with list_catalog/products.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new product as a DRAFT: name, price, description, file or service, web address, download window, and whether it is in the shop. A file can be FREE (priceCents 0): visitors get it by giving their email, and no Stripe is needed; a service always needs a price. Nobody can get it until status puts it on sale. Community owner only.
- edit: Change a product's name, PRICE, description, web address or download window, each left alone when omitted. priceCents 0 makes a file FREE (its add-on offer is removed, and it is refused while another product offers it as an add-on). A new price applies to the next checkout; buyers keep what they paid. Community owner only.
- status: Put a product on sale (active; a free file is then given away for an email), take it back to a draft, or archive it (off sale, buyers keep their downloads). Going on sale is refused while it has nothing to deliver.
- refund_policy: The shop's refund policy, shown before payment and in every receipt. Replaces the whole text; empty states no policy.
- delivery: Whether buyers get a FILE they download or a SERVICE with no file, the instructions a service shows them in place of a download, and the contact list buyers of EITHER kind are added to when they pay (which is how an automation picks them up). Each of the three is left alone when omitted. It refuses rather than leaving a product that is already on sale with nothing to deliver. Community owner only.
- framing: Where the SUBJECT of the product's cover photo is, so the boxes that are not the shape it was cropped to (the wide bio card, the square product page and checkout panel, the share card) crop around that point instead of around the middle. It re-crops nothing and uploads nothing: it stores two numbers beside the photo. Null goes back to the centre, omitted leaves it alone, and a product with no cover photo is refused. Community owner only.
- visibility: Whether the product is BROWSABLE: in the shop with its own /shop page, or kept out of it. A SECOND AXIS, not the same as whether it is on sale, and a hidden product stays fully active and still takes money wherever it is linked, most often from a paid session type it exists to back. It changes no price and nothing about what the buyer receives. Hiding 404s an address that may already be in an email, so it is reversible rather than harmless. Community owner only.
- purchase_emails: Which saved email a product's buyers get as their RECEIPT (or free download email) and as their REFUND email, or, with no `productId`, the STORE's defaults every product without its own uses (`receiptEmailId`, `downloadEmailId` for free products, `refundEmailId`). null goes back to the store's default (or the built-in email for the store itself); one left out is kept. The email must hold the purchase inserts its role needs (manage_email block type purchase): a paid receipt delivery and summary, a download email delivery, a refund email refundDetails. A free download takes no refund email. {productTitle} fills in once it is attached. Community owner only.
- upsell: Offer one of the community's other products alongside this one, either as a tick box at checkout (both items, one payment) or as the first suggestion after checkout (a separate purchase). It sets both fields together, so `upsellProductId` null OR OMITTED stops offering one: changing only `mode` means passing the current `upsellProductId` too. Community owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: The product's name.

priceCents.description: The price in MINOR units of the community's own currency (cents for USD, pence for GBP, yen for JPY which has no minor unit). The currency is always the community's own and is not an argument. 0 makes a FILE product FREE: visitors get it by giving their email (a signed-in member in one click), it needs no Stripe, and the coach gets their address as a contact. A service cannot be free. Any other price has a minimum, which depends on that currency and so is not in this schema: the server refuses anything under it and names the floor.

description.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

kind.description: `digital` (the default) is a file buyers download, uploaded in the console. `service` has no file: buyers get the instructions.

instructions.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

slug.description: Its web address under /shop/. Omitted, one is made from the title.

downloadWindowDays.description: File products: how many days a buyer's download link works, one of 7, 30, 90, 365. Defaults to 30.

listed.description: False keeps it out of the shop, with no /shop page of its own, so it sells only where it is linked. Defaults to true.

status.description: active is on sale; draft and archived are not.

policy.description: The whole policy, plain text. An empty string clears it.

buyerListId.description: Add every buyer of this product to this contact list, for either kind. Null stops adding them. Omitted leaves it as it is. From manage_contacts.

focalPoint.description: Where the subject is. Send null to go back to the centre, which is what every product starts as. OMITTED leaves the framing alone. A product with NO cover photo is REFUSED rather than quietly accepted, because uploading a cover later clears the framing and the coach would never learn the call did nothing.

x.description: Across the photo. 0 is the left edge, 1 the right.

y.description: Down the photo. 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom.

receiptEmailId.description: The saved email buyers get when they buy (on a free product, when they claim it), from manage_email/read with no emailId. null goes back to the store's default, or the built-in receipt; omitted keeps what it is.

downloadEmailId.description: STORE ONLY (no productId): the saved email every FREE product sends unless it has its own. null goes back to the built-in download email; omitted keeps what it is.

refundEmailId.description: The saved email buyers get when they are refunded, from manage_email/read with no emailId. null goes back to the store's default, or the built-in refund email; omitted keeps what it is.

upsellProductId.description: The product to offer alongside it. Null OR OMITTED stops offering one, because this act sets the pair together rather than patching one field. Must be a different product of the same community, and one that is on sale (active, priced, with its file uploaded).

mode.description: Where it is offered. Defaults to pre_purchase, the checkout tick box. THIS ACT SETS BOTH FIELDS TOGETHER: a call that omits upsellProductId clears the add-on, so to change only the mode you must pass the current upsellProductId alongside it.

tools.name: manage_offer
tools.title: Read and run offers, and set the free trial
tools.description:
Membership offers (discounted ways to join, each on its own /join?offer= link), offers on what the community sells (a sale price, a private link or a discount code on event tickets, shop products or paid sessions), and the free trial first-time joiners get. An offer is charged to strangers the moment it is live and every card charged through it stays charged, so confirm the price and terms with the coach before creating or changing one. List them with list_catalog/offers.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One offer's whole terms, either kind. A membership offer: price against the standard price, the rung it discounts (or why its link charges full price), cadence, window, cap, audience, join-page words, how many have seen and taken it, status and link. An offer on tickets, products or paid sessions: its items by name and id with the price now and with the offer (a session at its linked product's price), discount, how buyers get it, code, window, uses, badge, paid sales, money taken and private links. Read before editing.
- create: Mint an offer: a price below the standard one, optionally dated, capped or for new members only, with a badge and a line on the join page. Returns its live link. On a community that sells membership tiers it names the rung it discounts (tierId) and counts on that rung only. Community owner only.
- edit: Change an offer's terms, PRICE and rung included; everything not named is kept and the whole offer is re-checked. Same link; people who already joined keep what they pay. Community owner only.
- duplicate: Copy an offer under a new live link with no dates and nobody counted yet. How an ended offer runs again. Community owner only.
- end: Stop an offer for good, either kind: a membership offer's link charges the standard price from now on; an offer on tickets, products or sessions stops its link, code and sale price at once. Whoever already joined or bought keeps what they pay. Owner or admin.
- create_purchase_offer: An offer on event tickets, shop products (an add-on line is priced by an offer on that product) or paid sessions (priced at the session type's linked product): percent off, an amount off (whole units) or a new price for one item; automatic for every buyer (an early bird), on a private link, on a code buyers type, or a link and a code; optionally dated and capped (a per-person limit is for event tickets only), with a badge. Ids from list_catalog/events, list_catalog/products or list_catalog/booking_types. Live and charged to strangers once it starts; returns any private links. Community owner only.
- edit_purchase_offer: Change an offer on tickets, products or sessions: its name, items, discount, doors, code, window, caps or badge; everything not named is kept and the whole offer is re-checked. What it applies to is fixed: for another kind, end it and create a new one. A link keeps its address; people who already bought keep what they paid. Community owner only.
- trial: Switch the free trial for new members on or off, its length, and which rungs carry it. Community owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: What the coach calls it, e.g. "Founding members".

price.description: The offer price in WHOLE units of the community's own currency (19 means $19 for a US community), charged each period for a monthly or yearly membership, or once for lifetime access. It must be BELOW the standard price of the cadence it discounts, and above the currency's minimum; the server names both when it refuses.

interval.description: Which cadence this discounts, when the community (or, on a ladder, the rung) sells both. Omitted on create, the main one; omitted on edit, the one the offer already discounts. Ignored for lifetime access.

tierId.description: The membership level (rung) this discounts, from list_catalog/membership_tiers. REQUIRED on a community that sells membership tiers, where an offer counts only on the rung it names and must be below THAT rung's price; refused on one that sells a single price (null moves an offer back onto the single price). On edit, omitted keeps the current rung, and moving to another rung takes that rung's main cadence unless interval is named.

startsAt.description: When the link starts working, ISO 8601 with a timezone. Null or omitted: straight away.

expiresAt.description: When it stops, ISO 8601 with a timezone, in the future and after startsAt. Null: no end. After it, the link quietly reverts to the standard price.

maxRedemptions.description: How many people may take it. Null: no cap.

newMembersOnly.description: True refuses anybody who is or was already a member.

badge.description: A short pill above the price on the join page, e.g. "Founding member price". Null clears it.

greeting.description: One line above the price, e.g. "You were here early." Null clears it.

countdown.description: Show a live countdown to the end instead of a date. Only shows when there is an end.

appliesTo.description: What it discounts. "event": event tickets. "product": shop products; a product offered as an add-on at another product's checkout is priced by an offer naming THAT product (or all products), never by one on the main product. "booking_type": paid sessions; a session's price is the price of the product linked to its session type, so that is the price the offer lowers.

targetIds.description: The items it applies to, every one of the kind in appliesTo and in this community. event: eventIds from list_catalog/events, each a PAID event. product: productIds from list_catalog/products, each on sale with a price. booking_type: bookingTypeIds from list_catalog/booking_types, each with a linked product that is on sale. Leave out and set targetAll for every item of that kind.

targetAll.description: True for every item of the kind that charges, now and later: every event that sells tickets, every product on sale (add-on lines included), or every session type with a paid product. Not with a new price (discountKind price needs exactly one item) or a private link (a link opens one item's page).

discountKind.description: percent: a percent off. amount: an amount off. price: a new price for ONE item, below what it costs now (a ticket's price in effect, a product's price, a session's linked product's price).

discountValue.description: For percent, a whole number from 1 to 99. For amount and price, WHOLE units of the community's own currency (49 means $49 for a US community, 49.5 means $49.50). An offer cannot make anything free, and never charges below the currency's minimum; the server names both when it refuses.

doors.description: How buyers get it. automatic: every buyer, shown as a sale price (an early bird); two automatic offers on one item cannot overlap in time. link: only people holding its private link, one per item (the event's /e/ page, the product's /shop/ page or the session's /book/ page with ?offer=), returned in the answer. code: anyone who types the code at checkout. link_code: both.

code.description: The code buyers type, 3 to 24 letters and numbers (stored upper-case), for doors code or link_code only. Unique in this community across every offer; a taken one is refused with a free suggestion.

maxPerPerson.description: EVENT TICKET offers only: how many times one buyer may use it, 1 to 100. Omitted or null: 1. Refused for products and paid sessions, which have no per-person limit; cap them with maxRedemptions instead.

showRemaining.description: Show buyers how many are left at this price. Only with a cap (maxRedemptions); off by default, since it tells strangers the cap.

days.description: The length when switching on. Omitted, the length already set, else 7.

tiers.description: Per-rung choices on a laddered community. Rungs not named keep theirs.

offersTrial.description: Whether new joiners at this rung get the trial.

tools.name: manage_store
tools.title: Read, style and publish the bio link and store page
tools.description:
The one link a coach puts in their Instagram or TikTok bio: a header, a look, and an ordered list of what they offer. Every write is saved as a draft (unpublished edits, on a page that is already live) and nothing reaches visitors until publish. Uploading photos and connecting a Shopify shop stay in the console.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The page as it is being edited: live or draft, whether it is the homepage, any unpublished edits, its ad-tracking state, the header, the whole style, every item with its id and whether it is actually showing, the search settings and the templates. Start here.
- template: Switch to a ready-made look. Style only: the header, the items and the coach's own accent, colours and fonts are kept.
- header: Name, tagline, headerLayout (classic, hero, split or minimal), name size and alignment, hero framing, how large the hero photo shows (heroSize) and whether it fades into the page (heroBlend), photo frame (circle, rounded, square, or original for no crop) and the colour behind the photo (avatarBg), verified tick, photo and banner (clear or reuse, never upload), and the social icons: where they sit, how they look, and the list, which is replaced whole.
- style: Background (with an overlay colour on a photo or library one, a blurred photo, a slowly drifting gradient, or a faint pattern on a colour), buttons, cover shape, shadow, card surface (solid, glass or clear) and card border, spacing, section headings, layout (stack or grid), movement, accent colour, per-role colours (buttons, button text, text, cards) and fonts, including the coach's uploaded ones, each left alone when omitted.
- items: Replace the item list whole, in order: keep an item by its id, add one by kind and what it points at, and relabel, resize, feature, hide, highlight (up to two), give an icon or schedule (showFrom, showUntil) as you go. Also adds the blocks that are not links: text (a paragraph), image (a photo, optionally linked), divider, embed (a YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, SoundCloud or TikTok player, from its link in embedUrl), feed (a YouTube channel's newest videos as a swipeable row that fills itself, from channelUrl, with feedShow and feedCount), blogPost (one published blog post as a card, from blogPostId) and blogFeed (the blog's newest posts, kept up to date, from every post or one category or one author, with blogCount and blogLayout), and sets a heading's sectionLayout (list, grid or carousel for the items under it). Says which items are saved but not showing, and which are scheduled or ended.
- seo: The title, description and share image search engines and link previews show, and the page's own address word (path: links puts it at the community address /links, and /store redirects there).
- publish: Put the page live, or ship its unpublished edits. Visitors see it straight away.
- unpublish: Take the page offline; its link shows not-found until it is published again.
- discard: Throw away the unpublished edits on a live page.
- home: Make the page the community's homepage (what a logged-out visitor sees at the root of its address, so the address is the bio link), or stop. Needs a published page; takes the root from any funnel page, which stays live at its own address.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

displayName.description: Up to 60 characters. Empty shows the community name.

tagline.description: One line under the name, up to 140 characters.

avatarShape.description: The photo frame: circle (the default), rounded, square, or original for no crop, no ring and no shadow, so a transparent logo or wordmark shows whole at its own shape. A photo already cropped square stays cropped; the coach uploads the original again in the console.

headerLayout.description: classic: photo over an optional banner, centred. hero: the banner (or the photo) full width at the top with the name over it. split: photo left, name beside it. minimal: no photo, the name set large.

titleSize.description: The name's size: md, lg or xl.

align.description: center or left. The split layout is always left.

heroFocus.description: For hero: which part of the photo stays in frame, as percentages across and down. 50/50 is the centre.

heroSize.description: For hero: how large the photo shows. fit (the default) is sized to the screen, so the page trims a little of a 3:4 crop's top and bottom, more on a computer; large is three wide by four high on every screen, medium is square, small is four wide by three high. Kept when another layout is chosen.

heroBlend.description: For hero: how the photo meets the page. shade (the default) darkens the photo's lower edge and sets the name in white over it; fade dissolves the photo into the page background and sets the name just under it in the page's text colour. Kept when another layout is chosen.

avatarBg.description: A colour behind the profile photo, as a hex like #f4efe6, which shows through a logo with a transparent background. Null removes it (the default: the page shows through).

socialsPosition.description: bottom (the default, after what is for sale) or top (under the name).

socialsStyle.description: plain icons, circle (ringed) or filled (on an accent disc).

verified.description: The decorative check badge beside the name. Nothing is verified by it.

avatarKey.description: Null goes back to the community logo.

socials.description: The social icons, in order, up to 8. Replaces the whole list; an empty list removes them all.

color.description: For color: the page colour. For pattern: the base colour under the pattern.

angle.description: For gradient: degrees, 0 to 360. 180 runs top to bottom.

drift.description: For gradient: true makes the colours drift slowly behind the page. Still for visitors who ask for less motion, and on a page whose movement is off.

blur.description: For image: true blurs the photo heavily, so any picture reads as soft colour. The page's own profile photo key (from manage_store/read) works here.

pattern.description: For pattern: which one. It is drawn faintly over color, in the accent when the text stays readable over it, otherwise in the text colour or a tone of color; manage_store/read says which.

density.description: For pattern: sm is fine, md (the default) medium, lg large.

imageKey.description: For image: a key manage_store/read returned. Uploading a new photo is a console step.

overlay.description: For image, stock and video: the darkening scrim, 0 to 80 percent.

stockId.description: For stock: a library background id, from the BACKGROUND LIBRARY that manage_store/read lists.

tint.description: For image and stock: the overlay's colour as a hex value, washing the background in that colour instead of darkening it. Null or omitted is black.

background.description: The page background. theme inherits the community's own; stock is a photo or silent video loop from the free library; pattern is a faint pattern on a base colour; the others need the fields named for them. video is the coach's own clip, which is uploaded and trimmed in the console.

coverAspect.description: The crop for cover cards: wide, square, or tall (for book and workbook covers).

motion.description: full animates the page; off keeps it still for everyone.

headingTone.description: How section headings are drawn: quiet, rule (underlined) or solid (filled).

layout.description: stack is one column on a phone; grid puts cover cards two across.

cardSurface.description: solid (the default) cards sit on their own fill; glass frosts whatever is behind them; clear drops the fill and keeps the edge. Applies with buttonFill solid; outline already draws every card clear.

cardBorder.description: The card edge: hairline (the default), none, or bold. A card with no fill keeps a hairline, or it would disappear.

colors.description: Per-role colours, each a hex value or null for automatic. Only the ones sent change.

button.description: The solid button fill, or an outline button's border.

buttonText.description: The label on a solid button.

text.description: The page's text: name, tagline, headings, and card text.

card.description: The fill of a solid card.

id.description: An EXISTING item's id from manage_store/read. Send it to keep that item (and its click history); any other field you send changes it. Omit it only for a NEW item.

kind.description: A NEW item's kind. paymentLink, product, guide, form, event, booking and landingPage point at something the community already has (ids from manage_payment_link/list, list_catalog/products, manage_guide/read, list_catalog/forms, list_catalog/events, list_catalog/booking_types, manage_page/read; a landing page shows only while it is published); membership is the join card; external is any URL; heading is a section title (its label is the text, and its sectionLayout lays out the items under it); text is a short paragraph (its words go in body); image is a photo (an imageKey from manage_store/read, optionally a url to link it); divider is a line or space; embed plays a video, track or podcast right on the page (its link goes in embedUrl); feed is a swipeable row of a YouTube channel's newest videos, which fills itself as the coach posts (the channel goes in channelUrl); blogPost is one published blog post as a card (blogPostId, a postId from manage_blog/read); blogFeed is the blog's newest published posts, which fills itself as the coach publishes (blogCount, blogLayout, and at most one of blogCategoryId or blogAuthorId). Both blog kinds show only while the blog is on, and a members-only post shows its title, cover and card line with a lock. shopifyProduct cannot be added here, only kept by id.

landingPageId.description: For landingPage: a published funnel page's pageId, from manage_page/read. A website page is not offered.

bookingTypeId.description: One session type. Null (or omitted on a new booking item) is the whole booking menu.

blogPostId.description: For blogPost: a published post's postId, from manage_blog/read. A draft, or an unpublished post, does not show.

blogCount.description: For blogFeed: how many of the newest posts show, 1 to 6. 3 is the default.

blogLayout.description: For blogFeed: list stacks the posts as rows (the default); grid puts them two across; carousel is one swipeable row of cover cards.

blogCategoryId.description: For blogFeed: only this category's posts, a categoryId from manage_blog/read. Not together with blogAuthorId. Null shows every post again.

blogAuthorId.description: For blogFeed: only this author's posts, an authorRef from manage_blog/read that is a profile id (a teammate with no profile yet has none; set one up with manage_blog/save_author). The owner's profile also takes posts nobody is picked for. Not together with blogCategoryId. Null shows every post again.

offerToken.description: For membership: a discount offer to apply. Null removes it.

url.description: For external: an https URL or a path on the community. For image: where tapping the photo goes (leave it out for a photo that is not a link).

body.description: For text: the paragraph, up to 1000 characters counted on the markup. Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone. A link's url is https:// or a path on the community ("/join"); anything else shows as plain words.

sectionLayout.description: For heading: how the items under it (until the next heading) are laid out. list stacks them, the default; grid puts them two across; carousel is one swipeable row. In a grid or carousel every link shows as a cover card.

embedUrl.description: For embed: the link to play, from YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, SoundCloud, TikTok, e.g. https://youtu.be/<id> or an open.spotify.com episode. Only the provider and the item's id are kept, never the address itself, and nothing loads from the provider until a visitor taps play. A short share link (vm.tiktok.com, spotify.link, on.soundcloud.com) is refused: open it and send the full address. On an existing embed, sending a new one swaps what it plays.

channelUrl.description: For feed: the YouTube channel whose newest videos the row shows, as youtube.com/@handle, a youtube.com/channel/UC... link, or a bare @handle. It is looked up once, now, and stored by YouTube's channel id, so a later rename of the handle does not break the row. A link to one video is refused: that is an embed. On an existing feed, sending a new one switches the channel.

feedShow.description: For feed: all (the default) shows every upload, videos only regular videos, shorts only Shorts.

feedCount.description: For feed: how many of the newest videos the row shows, 3 to 15. 6 is the default.

dividerStyle.description: For divider: line (a hairline, the default) or space (just room).

dividerSize.description: For divider: sm (the default) or lg.

inline.description: Retired: every form card opens the form in a drawer over the page, and there is no on-page form any more. Sending true is refused.

label.description: Your title for the card, up to 80 characters. Empty uses the source's own title. Required text for a heading.

subtitle.description: A line under the title, up to 120 characters. Empty uses the source's.

size.description: auto lets the kind decide; card is a big cover card; compact is a slim row.

featured.description: The one big card at the top. Only the FIRST featured item in the list keeps it.

hidden.description: Kept in the list but not shown publicly.

imageKey.description: A cover override: a key manage_store/read returned, or null to use the source's own art. Uploading is a console step.

highlight.description: A small repeating motion that draws the eye: pulse (an accent halo), shimmer (a sheen crossing the card) or nudge (a short sideways tug); none removes it. At most 2 per page, in list order; a call that would need a third is refused, naming the items that hold them. Not on a heading. Nothing moves on a Still page or for a visitor who asked for less motion.

icon.description: An icon beside the title, in place of the kind's own: one of star, heart, sparkles, flame, zap, gift, tag, percent, ticket, shopping-bag, download, play, video, camera, music, mic, headphones, podcast, book-open, newspaper, graduation-cap, brain, dumbbell, leaf, flower, sun, moon, coffee, utensils, hand-heart, smile, baby, paw-print, palette, laptop, briefcase, users, message-circle, mail, phone, calendar, clock, map-pin, globe, link, rocket, trophy, crown, or a single emoji. Null removes it. A cover photo, when the item has one, still wins. Not on a heading.

showFrom.description: When the item starts showing, as an ISO 8601 date-time with an offset (e.g. 2026-10-06T09:00:00-07:00). Until then it is saved but not on the page. Null removes the start.

showUntil.description: When the item stops showing, ISO 8601 with an offset like showFrom. It must come after showFrom when both are set. Null removes the end.

sensitive.description: Retired: Drry has no sensitive-content cover, since the platform does not host content that needs one. Sending true is refused.

items.description: Every item the page should carry, top to bottom.

path.description: The page's own address word, e.g. links for /links. Null or an empty string: /store only.

home.description: true: this page is the homepage. false: it is not, and the root shows the join page.

tools.name: manage_payment_link
tools.title: See and manage payment links
tools.description:
A link that takes money: for ONE named client, or reusable for many people who each sign and pay for themselves. LIVE the moment it exists: confirm the amount before creating one, not after.

Set `act` to one of:
- list: Every link and what it charges, every other way to pay it offers, where the client goes after paying, and for an agreement, who has signed it, by name, and whether they paid.
- create: A new link, for one client or reusable for many, one-time or in installments monthly or every N days, with up to two other ways to pay the client chooses between (pay in full or 6 monthly payments), optionally opening community access on a set date and sending the client on to a page after paying. Nobody is charged until somebody opens it and pays.
- update: Edit a link that nobody has paid yet: price, plan and days between payments, its other ways to pay, access and the date it opens, terms, whether it is reusable, and where the client goes after paying.
- duplicate: Copy a link, pay page and all, into a new one with its own URL. How to change a link somebody has already paid.
- archive: Stop a link taking new payments.
- reactivate: Put an archived link back in service.
- send: Email a link to the one client it is addressed to, from the community's sender, with reminders 1, 3 and 7 days later that stop when they sign or pay. Emails a real person: confirm first.
- reminders: Switch the reminders for a link's latest send on or off.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: What the client is paying for, e.g. "12-week coaching package".

amountCents.description: The amount in MINOR units of the community's own currency (cents for USD, pence for GBP, yen for JPY which has no minor unit). For a one-time link this is the whole price; for installments it is the amount charged EACH month, not the total. There is also a MINIMUM, which depends on the community's currency and so is not in this schema: the server refuses anything under it and names the floor.

mode.description: A single charge, or the same amount every month. Installments need the Creator plan; one-time links work on every plan.

installmentMonths.description: Required when mode is installments. How many charges in total, the first taken at checkout (the name is from when every plan was monthly).

installmentIntervalDays.description: Installments only. Days between charges, e.g. 14 for every two weeks. Leave it out (or send null) for MONTHLY charges, which is the default.

grant.description: What paying gives them: nothing beyond the payment (off), community access for a period (temporary), or access that does not expire (permanent).

accessDurationDays.description: Required when grant is temporary. Days of access, counted from when access OPENS (the start date when there is one, else payment).

accessStartsAt.description: Optional, only when grant is not off. When community access OPENS, as an ISO 8601 date-time WITH an offset (e.g. 2026-10-15T09:00:00-04:00): ask the coach what time and timezone they mean. Payment is still taken at checkout; somebody who pays before this gets in when it arrives, and somebody who pays after gets in straight away. Leave it out (or null) for access at payment.

clientEmail.description: Optional. Set it and the checkout is locked to that person; leave it blank and Stripe collects it.

agreementText.description: Optional terms the client must agree to before paying. Their agreement is snapshotted at purchase and cannot be edited afterwards. Needs the Creator plan; a link without terms works on every plan. Write money, names and dates as fields rather than typing them, so the terms always match what the link charges: {{client_name}} (client name), {{coach_name}} (your name), {{total}} (total), {{installments}} (number of payments), {{installment_amount}} (payment amount), {{start_date}} (date signed), {{payment_interval}} (how often they pay), {{access_starts}} (when access starts). Each is filled in when the client signs. Any other name in double braces is refused.

reusable.description: Default false: the link closes the moment one person pays it, which suits an invoice for one named client. Set it true for a link many people pay, each signing any agreement for themselves: it stays open after every sale, so it is the one to put behind a funnel button. A reusable link cannot name a client, so leave clientName and clientEmail off it.

paymentOptions.description: Optional, up to 2. Needs the Creator plan. OTHER ways the client may pay this same link, beside the plan set by amountCents/mode, e.g. the link is 120000 one_time and one option is 22000 installments x 6. The client picks one on the pay page. No two may charge the same way. Write any money in agreementText as fields ({{total}}, {{installments}}, {{installment_amount}}): they fill in with the option the client picks, where a typed amount is wrong for the others. On update, leave it out to keep the link's options, send [] to remove them all, or send the full list to replace them.

amountCents.description: Minor units, like the link's own amountCents: the whole price for one_time, the amount of EACH charge for installments.

installmentMonths.description: Required for installments: how many charges in all.

installmentIntervalDays.description: Installments only. Days between charges; leave out for monthly.

afterPaymentHref.description: Optional. Where the client is sent after paying, once the payment is confirmed: a page of this community as a path ("/" for the community home, "/p/<slug>" for a landing page, "/library" for courses) or a full https:// address. Leave it out (or null) for the link's own thank-you screen. A client who bought community access but is not signed in is asked to sign in on the way to a members-only page.

reminders.description: Send reminders 1, 3 and 7 days later. Defaults to true.

on.description: True to send the reminders, false to stop them.

tools.name: manage_agreement
tools.title: See and manage sign-only agreements
tools.description:
A contract with NO payment (a confidentiality agreement, a media release, a coaching agreement billed elsewhere) that a client signs on its own public page. One agreement, many links: each is for ONE client by email, or reusable for anyone who holds it. A link for one client can be emailed to them (send), with reminders until they sign; a reusable link is shared by its URL. Who signed is readable by name only. For a contract that takes money, use manage_payment_link.

Set `act` to one of:
- list: Every agreement, with its id, open links, how many opened and signed it, and the newest ten signers by name. Archived ones only with includeArchived. Staff only.
- read: One agreement in full: its title and text, whether it is archived, whether the coach's countersignature covers its current text, every link (for whom or reusable, status, opened, signed, whether and when it was sent with reminders on or off, share and preview URLs), and who signed, by name and date. Staff only.
- create: A new agreement from a title and its text, countersigned with the coach's adopted signature, optionally with a first link: clientEmail (and clientName) for one client, or reusable. Hands back the URL to share; emails nobody. Creator plan, owner only.
- update: Change the title or the text; whatever is left out is kept. Links ask for the new text from now on, signings already made keep the words they signed, and the new text is countersigned. Creator plan, owner only.
- new_link: Another link to an agreement that is not archived: for one client by clientEmail (and clientName), or reusable. Hands back the URL to share; emails nobody. Creator plan, owner only.
- link_status: Close one link to new signatures (archived) or open it again (active, Creator plan). A single-use link somebody signed is consumed and cannot be reopened. Staff only.
- archive: Stop every link of an agreement taking signatures. Nothing is deleted and signings stay readable. Staff only.
- reactivate: Bring an archived agreement back; its active links take signatures again at the same URLs. Creator plan, staff only.
- send: Email a link to the one client it is addressed to, from the community's sender, with reminders 1, 3 and 7 days later that stop when they sign. Stamps the coach's countersignature. Emails a real person: confirm first. Creator plan, owner only.
- reminders: Switch the reminders for a link's latest send on or off. Off works on every plan; on needs the Creator plan. Owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

includeArchived.description: True to include archived agreements. Defaults to false.

title.description: What the agreement is, as the signer reads it at the top, e.g. "Media release".

body.description: The full text the client reads and signs, in plain text or Markdown. There is no payment on it, so the only fields it can use are {{client_name}} (the signer's full name), {{coach_name}} (the community's name), {{start_date}} (the day they sign), each filled in when the client signs. Any other name in double braces is refused, the payment fields included.

clientEmail.description: Address the link to ONE client: only this email address can sign it, and it closes once they have. Leave it out and set reusable instead for a link anyone holding it can sign.

clientName.description: Optional, with clientEmail only: the client's name, which greets them and fills {{client_name}}.

reusable.description: True for a link anyone who holds it can sign, each person once, which stays open after every signature (a release form, a waiver). It cannot name a client, so leave clientEmail and clientName off it.

status.description: archived closes the link to new signatures; active opens it again.

reminders.description: Send reminders 1, 3 and 7 days later. Defaults to true.

on.description: True to send the reminders, false to stop them.

tools.name: manage_contacts
tools.title: Import contacts, put people on lists and tags, and see what was imported
tools.description:
Importing the mailing list a coach is moving from another platform, taking a batch back out if it went wrong, and putting people the community already has on lists and tags by the email addresses the coach gives. Nothing here lists who is on a list or carries a tag.

Set `act` to one of:
- import: Up to 500 rows, each with first and last name, its own tags, and whether the old platform had them unsubscribed (those go on the blocked list instead, never mailed); tags for the whole call too. ASK about permission to email before setting the flag. The Free plan imports up to 100 new contacts in total (addresses already held cost nothing); undoing an import gives none back, and a call that would go past it is refused whole. From the Creator plan there is no such limit. Support can raise the limits for one community, so call rather than refuse in advance: a refused call writes no contacts and says why. Undo and history work on every plan.
- undo: Remove one batch. Each import call is its own batch.
- history: What has been imported and when.
- list_add: Put up to 100 existing contacts on a list, by email address, matched exactly. When the list starts a live automation it refuses and names the journeys until called again with confirmAutomation, after the coach agrees. Reports how many were added, how many were already on it, and any address that is not a contact.
- list_remove: Take up to 100 people off a list, by email address. Anyone already enrolled in an automation the list started stays in it.
- tag: Give up to 100 members or contacts a tag, by email address. A tag is an audience: the answer names any unsent email aimed at it that will now reach them. At most 25 tags per person.
- untag: Take a tag off up to 100 people, by email address, from both their member and contact records.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

name.description: Their first name, or their whole name when the export has only one name column.

lastName.description: Their surname, when the export splits it out. Joined onto the first name with a space, as the console upload does.

status.description: What the OLD platform says about this person. unsubscribed: they opted out there, so they are NOT imported and go on this community's blocked list instead, never to be mailed. Read it from the export's status or subscribed column. Left out means subscribed.

tags.description: This person's OWN tags, from the export's tags column. Never copied onto anybody else in the file.

Tags put on EVERYONE this call imports, on top of each row's own, e.g. "from kajabi". Recorded on the history entry for the import. A person holds at most 25 tags, these and their own together (one tag in two spellings counts once), and a row over that is refused.

source.description: Where the list came from, e.g. "Kajabi export".

hasPermissionToEmail.description: Confirm the coach has permission to email these people. Ask them before setting this. Importing a bought or scraped list is how a sending domain dies. Not needed when every row is unsubscribed, since that makes nobody mailable.

emails.description: The email addresses of the people, as the coach gave them, at most 100. Matched exactly. Only people this community already has are touched; any other address is reported back.

confirmAutomation.description: Set only after the coach has agreed that the people added will be enrolled in the live automations the refusal named.

tag.description: The tag. An existing one, or a new one to start.

tools.name: manage_marketing_org
tools.title: Read and organise the marketing workspace
tools.description:
The folders, lists, tags, saved segments, saved replies and reusable blocks the email side is filed into. Read first: it hands back every id the other acts take.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The list at a glance (people, members and not joined, new in 30 days, share engaged, and how many need a look), then every email folder (in order, with colour and icon), contact list and tag with how many people are on each, a tag's spelling and colour, the saved segments with their rules in the form the segments act takes, the footer social links, and for owners and admins the saved replies. With segmentId, that one segment in full: its rules in words, how many people it matches now, and the unsent emails aimed at it. Names nobody.
- folders: Make, rename, restyle or reorder an email folder, or file emails into one.
- lists: Make or rename a contact list. Makes it EMPTY; manage_contacts/list_add puts people on it.
- segments: Create a saved segment, rename one, or replace its rules (match all or any; subscription, join recency, source, tag, membership tier, email engagement). A rule change says how many people it matched before and matches now, and names every unsent email aimed at it, which will reach the new match. Cannot delete one, list who is in one, or aim an email at one.
- tags: Define a contact tag (its colour and spelling; whatever is left out is kept) or rename one. Tags nobody; manage_contacts/tag does.
- assets: Duplicate an email, save a block, set footer socials.
- saved_replies: The canned replies used in messages.
- funnel_pages: Duplicate a funnel page, make a funnel page the home page, or clear the home page. For a website page, use manage_site/set_home and manage_site/duplicate_page.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

segmentId.description: Read this one segment in full instead of the whole workspace. Every segment's id is in the answer without it.

action.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

folderId.description: The folder to act on, or to file into. From manage_marketing_org/read, which lists every folder in order.

name.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

color.description: One of slate, violet, spring, marigold, coral, or a hex like #7c5cff.

afterFolderId.description: reorder: the folder it sits AFTER. Omit for the top.

beforeFolderId.description: reorder: the folder it sits BEFORE. Omit for the bottom.

emailIds.description: file: the emails to move. From manage_email/read.

unfile.description: file: true takes the emails OUT of every folder.

listId.description: The list to rename. From manage_marketing_org/read, which lists every list with how many people are on it.

match.description: all: somebody must satisfy every rule. any: one rule is enough. Left out, a new segment matches all, and set_rules keeps the segment's current setting.

op.description: The operator, per field: subscription: is | isNot. joinRecency: within. source: is | isNot. tag: is | isNot. tier: atLeast | is | isNot. engagement: didNotOpen | didNotClick | opened | clicked.

value.description: subscription: cancelled (Cancelled) | active (Active paid) | free (Free member) | trial (Free trial). joinRecency (days): 7 | 30 | 90. source: webinar | signup_form | event_invite | paywall | purchase | added | imported | form | automation | instagram | free_download | checkout. tag: a tag this community has (manage_marketing_org/read lists them). tier: the id of an active membership tier. engagement: 30 or 90 for any email in that many days, or campaign:<emailId> for one email that has been sent.

tag.description: The tag. Stored lower-case with inner spaces collapsed, so "VIP" and "vip" are one tag.

label.description: How it is spelled on screen, e.g. "Denver Workshop". Left out, an existing tag keeps its spelling and a new one is spelled as typed.

socials.description: Full https:// profile URLs, per network. Only the networks you name change; send "" to take one down. Anything that is not an http(s) URL is refused rather than quietly dropped.

replyId.description: The saved reply to rewrite. From manage_marketing_org/read, which prints each one's title and body; a rewrite replaces both, so send the body back unchanged to retitle one.

title.description: What the coach types after "/" to find it. Short and distinctive.

body.description: The message itself. Line breaks are kept. It is a starting point the coach edits, not a canned send.

tools.name: list_catalog
tools.title: See what the community sells and offers
tools.description:
One read over everything a coach has set up. Say what you want with `act`; each answer carries the ids the write tools need.

Set `act` to one of:
- forms: Lead-capture forms and their signup counts, with the id of each (the id names a {formLink:<id>} email button destination).
- products: Store products with their /shop address and id (the id names a {productLink:<id>} email button destination), their prices (Free for a file given away for an email, with how many people claimed it; with what a buyer pays now when an automatic offer lowers one), whether each is a file or a service, any contact list its buyers are added to, any add-on offered alongside one, and how many shop checkouts were abandoned in the last 30 days (counts only). Staff only.
- offers: Every offer, both kinds, with how people get it (Automatic, Link, the code, Link + code), its status (Scheduled, Live, Used up, Ended), uses against its cap and the real money taken through it: membership offers with their price and the rung each discounts (or why its link charges full price), offers on tickets, products and paid sessions with their discount and the items by name. Plus the free trial new members get: its length, which rungs carry it, and how trials have gone. manage_offer changes them. Staff only.
- booking_types: Bookable session types, with their ids, what each costs (and what a booker pays now when an automatic offer lowers it), which confirmation email each sends (and its emailId), who hosts each one when that is not the owner, and the coach's hours and one-off dates (days off, different hours, busy spans). Staff only.
- membership_tiers: Membership rungs in order with their ids, what each costs new members (or that it has no price and is not sold), its description, how many members hold each, and which carry the free trial. Staff only.
- audio_collections: Audio collections, in the order members see them.
- audio_tracks: Audio tracks, with the collection each sits in, when members can open each one (days after joining or a fixed date), the first-published date, plus the private podcast's show settings.
- events: Upcoming and recent events, with their ids, who is hosting each one, where each happens (its join link, saying when it is a Google Meet link), and for a paid event what a ticket costs now (the price in effect after any price change, and the automatic offer lowering it).

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

formId.description: Omit to list every form with its id.

trackId.description: Leave this out to list the whole library. Give one (from a previous call) to read just that track, with its full chapter list.

tools.name: manage_community
tools.title: Talk in the community feed
tools.description:
Post, reply and pin in the community feed, as the connected account. A post or a reply is live at once and notifies members, so confirm the words with the coach in the same turn. Removing a post or ruling on a held one stays in the console. Staff only.

Set `act` to one of:
- post: Publish a text post, optionally in a room, optionally showing a page hosted elsewhere in a frame under it (embedUrl). Every member gets an in-app notification; with emailMembers the members who take announcements are emailed, and those emails count toward the monthly email allowance. Confirm first.
- reply: Reply to a post, or answer one reply under it. The person answered and anyone @mentioned are told. Confirm first.
- pin: Pin a published post to the top of the feed, or unpin it. Nobody is notified.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: The post's title.

body.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

categoryId.description: The room's categoryId. community_insight/thread prints the room a post is in, with its id; if you do not have one, ask the coach which room, send your best guess and the refusal lists every room with its id. Omit to post with no room.

emailMembers.description: Also email the members who take announcements about this post. Each email counts toward the monthly email allowance. Off unless the coach asks for it.

embedUrl.description: An https page to show in a frame under the post (an embedded page). A page on Drry itself is refused. Some sites refuse to be shown inside another site, so suggest the coach checks the post.

embedHeight.description: How tall the embedded page's frame is, px (default 640). Only with embedUrl.

parentCommentId.description: To answer one reply, its commentId from community_insight/thread. Omit to reply to the post itself.

pinned.description: true to pin, false to unpin.

tools.name: manage_messages
tools.title: Read and answer your direct messages
tools.description:
The coach's OWN direct-message conversations, 1:1 and group: see them, read one, reply in one. Never a conversation between members, and never a new conversation. A reply is delivered at once, so confirm the words with the coach in the same turn. Staff only.

Set `act` to one of:
- inbox: Your conversations, most recent first, with who each is with, the last message and how many are unread. Does not mark anything read.
- read: One of your conversations, oldest first, voice notes by transcript. Does not mark it read.
- reply: Send a text reply, as you, in a conversation you are already in. Everyone else in it is notified. Confirm first.
- mark_read: Mark one of your conversations read, as opening it in the console does. Nobody is notified.
- react: Add a tapback to one message, or take yours back. Everyone else in it sees it.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

cursor.description: From a previous answer, to see older conversations.

body.description: The message, as plain text.

reaction.description: Which tapback, or null to take yours back.

tools.name: community_insight
tools.title: See who is here, what they are saying and what needs the coach
tools.description:
Reads over the people, the conversation and what is waiting on the coach. No member email address is ever returned.

Set `act` to one of:
- attention: What is waiting on the coach right now and what is on today and tomorrow, each with a one-click console link. Start here for "anything I should know?". Staff only.
- next_step: The one next step for a community still getting started, and which act does it. Staff only.
- members: Who belongs, by display name and join date, each with the userId the member act takes. Staff only.
- member: One member in detail: seat, when last seen and what that means, access and whether it is about to change, tags, and course progress on a plan with analytics. Never their email, notes or payments. Staff only.
- posts: Recent post titles, who wrote them and how much they drew, which show an embedded page, each with its threadId.
- thread: One published post in full with its replies, who wrote each, any embedded page under it, and the commentId manage_community/reply takes.
- moderation_queue: What automatic moderation held, and how many reports are open. Staff only.
- growth: How membership has moved. Staff only.
