- revenue: Money in: this month by source, the monthly trend with new paying members and cancellations, revenue by tier, paying and trial counts, and bio link page sales, in the community's currency. Staff only, Creator and up.
- engagement: Whether members show up: active, going quiet and dormant counts, weekly and monthly actives, new-member activation, listening hours, lessons completed and member email opens and clicks. Counts only. Staff only, Creator and up.
- content_performance: Course completion, most-viewed lessons, most-played audio, busiest threads and uptake of new content; with courseId, how far members get lesson by lesson. Staff only, Creator and up.
- audio_listening: How the audio lands: listeners, finishers and drop-off per track, and private podcast feed adoption, as counts. Staff only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

search.description: Optional: match a member's name or handle. It does NOT match email addresses.

userId.description: From community_insight/members, or a post or reply's author.

page.description: Which page of replies, 1 being the first. Omit for 1.

courseId.description: One course, lesson by lesson. From manage_course/read.

trackId.description: One track, from list_catalog/audio_tracks. Omit for the overview.

tools.name: list_communities
tools.title: List your communities, or read one's setup
tools.description: With NO communityId, lists every community you can manage with the id other tools need and the seat you hold in each. Call it first: every other community tool requires a communityId and there is no default. With a communityId, reads that one's setup instead: its name and address, which member surfaces are switched on, what each tab is called, its plan, its currency, and whether it is admitting new members. Read that before changing anything, so a suggestion fits what is already there.

communityId.description: Omit to list them all. Name one to read its setup.

tools.name: pending_member_email
tools.title: Pending member email
tools.description: The new-content email your community is about to receive, and the way to call it off. Publishing a lesson, a course, an audio track or a guide queues ONE email to every member with access, and an announced event joins the same batch. It is sent a few hours after the first thing you published, so later publishes join the same email instead of adding another. Each member it reaches counts toward the community's monthly email allowance, and when it does not fit what is left the email is skipped, not held, and this says so. Call this after publishing to tell the coach what is about to go out and when. Pass cancel: true to stop it. Cancelling is safe and not permanent: the content stays published, and publishing anything else queues a fresh email.

cancel.description: Leave this out to just report what is queued. Set it to true to call the email off. Ask the coach before cancelling: it is their announcement.

tools.name: search_help_articles
tools.title: Search Drry documentation
tools.description: Full-text search across the published Drry help centre. Use this first to answer any question about how the product works: courses, the community feed, email, funnels, payments, events, members and settings. Returns ranked matches with a snippet and the slug needed to read the full article.

query.description: Search terms. Ordinary words work better than a sentence.

tools.name: read_help_article
tools.title: Read a Drry documentation article
tools.description: Return the full text of one published help article by its slug. Get a slug from search_help_articles or list_help_categories.

tools.name: list_help_categories
tools.title: List Drry documentation sections
tools.description: Every published section of the Drry help centre with the articles in it. Use this to see what the documentation covers when a search has not found the right words.

tools.name: manage_course
tools.title: Read, build and publish courses
tools.description:
A course, its modules, its lessons and the order a member meets them in. Reading costs nothing and is where to start. Anything you CREATE here lands as a DRAFT nobody can see until you publish it.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One course in full, or every course when courseId is omitted. Start here.
- create_course: A new course. Answers with its courseId AND a first moduleId.
- update_course: Retitle a course, change its subtitle, move it with `position`, set its locked-lesson and quiz wording, or aim `coverFocalPoint` at the subject of its cover photo. It does NOT set the cover colour.
- publish_course: Make a course visible. Queues the new-drops email to every member with access.
- create_module: A second section inside a course.
- update_module: Rename a module, or move it with `position`.
- create_lesson: A lesson inside a module. Needs moduleId.
- write_lesson: Replace a lesson's body, rename it, or move it within its module. This is how you write the actual teaching.
- update_lesson: How a lesson unlocks: drip, a date, or after earlier lessons, plus the quiz pass mark. NOT its title or body.
- move_lesson: Move a lesson to another module or another position.
- publish_lesson: Make one lesson visible. Mails members only once its course is published.
- unpublish_lesson: Take a lesson back out of view. Deletes nothing.
- unpublish_course: Take a whole course back out of view, lessons included. Each lesson keeps its own status, so which were live is not lost, but manage_course/publish_course is NOT a clean undo: it also publishes every draft lesson and emails members again. Deletes nothing.
- set_prerequisites: Which COURSES must be finished before this course opens. For lesson order use manage_course/update_lesson.
- set_quiz: The questions on a quiz lesson, and the score needed to pass.
- delete_course: Delete a DRAFT course no member has ever reached, with its modules and lessons. Refused, with the reason, for anything published or used. Cannot be undone.
- delete_module: Delete a module none of whose lessons was ever published or opened, with its lessons. Cannot be undone.
- delete_lesson: Delete a DRAFT lesson nobody has opened, with its sub-lessons. For a published one use manage_course/unpublish_lesson. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

courseId.description: Omit to list every course with its id.

lessonId.description: One lesson in full, body and quiz questions included. Takes precedence over courseId.

title.description: The course title.

subtitle.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

firstModuleTitle.description: Name of the first module. Defaults to "Module 1".

position.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

lockedMessage.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

quizPassMessage.description: What a member reads after passing a quiz in this course. Send an empty string for the default.

quizFailMessage.description: What a member reads after failing a quiz in this course. Send an empty string for the default.

coverFocalPoint.description: Where the subject of the cover photo is, so the places that show it in a different shape crop around that point instead of the middle. A cover is cropped to 16:9 once, but the home banner is much wider and the teasers are square, so a subject near an edge gets cut off. Send null to go back to the center. Omit to leave it alone. Read manage_course/read first for the framing it has now. A course with NO cover photo is REFUSED rather than quietly accepted, because uploading a cover clears the framing, so anything set beforehand would be discarded by that upload; send null on a coverless course and it is allowed, since clearing is already the state.

x.description: Across the photo. 0 is the left edge, 1 the right.

y.description: Down the photo. 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom.

release.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

releaseDays.description: Days to wait. Required for "days_after_joining" (at least 1). For "after_previous_section", 0 means the moment the previous section is finished.

body.description: Lesson text as simple HTML paragraphs.

releaseDate.description: For "on_a_date": the day it opens, as YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO timestamp. A bare date means midnight UTC of that day.

prerequisiteLessonIds.description: Lessons that must be finished before this one unlocks. They must be in the SAME course; anything else is dropped. Send [] to clear them.

quizPassMark.description: Percentage needed to pass, for a quiz lesson. Default 70.

targetModuleId.description: The section it should end up in, from manage_course/read.

prerequisiteCourseIds.description: Courses that must be finished before this one opens. Send [] to clear them. Omit to leave them alone.

requirePreviousCourse.description: Also require the course immediately above this one in the library, whichever that turns out to be.

delayDays.description: Extra days to wait after a member qualifies. 0 means open it the moment they do.

options.description: The answers to choose from, in the order shown.

correctOptions.description: Which options are correct, as zero-based positions in `options`. One entry makes it single-choice; more than one makes it select-all-that-apply.

questions.description: The whole quiz, in the order members answer it.

passMark.description: Percentage needed to pass. Omit to leave the current mark alone.

tools.name: manage_guide
tools.title: Read, write and publish guides
tools.description:
Guides are the standalone written pieces beside your courses: recipes, protocols, checklists. Built step by step, published when you say so.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One guide in full, or every guide and collection when guideId is omitted.
- create: A new draft guide. Members cannot see it until you publish.
- update: Title, summary, collection and the rest of the header.
- write: Replace the guide's steps. This is the writing itself.
- publish: Make it visible to members, or take it back to a draft. Publishing queues the new-drops email, like any other publish.
- reorder: The order guides appear in. Send every id in the collection.
- share: Turn the public share link on or off.
- save_atom: Save one what-you-need line or one step to the coach's drawer, to reuse in a later guide. Keyed on its name, so a repeat REPLACES.
- saved_pieces: Read that drawer. Console-only; no member sees a saved piece.
- delete: Delete a guide that has never been published. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

guideId.description: Omit to list every guide with its id.

title.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

collectionId.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

intro.description: The opening, as simple HTML paragraphs.

kind.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

coverHue.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

meta.description: The fact chips; send [] to clear them.

label.description: e.g. "Prep time".

type.description: What the value MEANS, so a consumer can find it without the label. Omit for a free-form chip.

heading.description: What the list is called, e.g. "Ingredients".

checkable.description: Whether members can tick items off. On by default.

id.description: The itemId from manage_guide/read. Send it back unchanged: it holds members' ticks. Omit only for a new line.

text.description: The thing itself, e.g. "Olive oil".

quantity.description: Free-form amount, e.g. "2 tbsp" or "to taste".

amount.description: Structured magnitude, for a list a member can scale. Omit if not a number.

category.description: For a merged shopping list, e.g. "Produce". Never shown in the guide.

group.description: In-guide section heading, e.g. "For the sauce".

steps.description: In the order you send them.

id.description: The stepId from manage_guide/read. Send it back unchanged: it holds the step's image or video. Omit only for a new step.

body.description: The step, as simple HTML paragraphs.

notes.description: The closing block, e.g. "Tips", as simple HTML.

published.description: true to publish, false to take it back to a draft.

orderedIds.description: Every guideId, in the order members should see them.

visibility.description: public: anyone with the link reads the whole guide. private: members only. Omit to change only the link name.

slug.description: The link name, 2 to 48 characters of lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Omit to keep the one it has, which is minted from the title the first time it goes public.

label.description: What it is called in the drawer. Defaults to its own text or title.

text.description: The line itself, for kind "need".

body.description: The step words as simple HTML, for kind "step".

tools.name: manage_guide_collection
tools.title: Group guides into collections
tools.description:
A collection is the shelf a guide sits on, and what members browse.

Set `act` to one of:
- create: A new shelf for guides to sit on, which is what members browse.
- update: Rename it or change its description.

tools.name: manage_page
tools.title: Read and write funnel and website pages
tools.description:
Public pages built from typed sections: funnel pages, and the pages of the coach's website (manage_site owns the site's menu, footer and header). Draft, read back what was stored, refine, then publish.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One page's sections, or every page when pageId is omitted. Read before every edit.
- create: A new draft FUNNEL page nobody can see (at /p/<slug>), from sections or from a template key. A website page is manage_site/create_page.
- update: Replace the page WHOLE. Compose every section from what read just returned. Every section type is writable, on a funnel page or a website page alike (a website page also takes a freeform layout, its elements placed anywhere on a grid and kept by id (editElements changes some by id and keeps the rest), each with its own style if wanted: text size, weight, spacing and case, a fill, border, corners, shadow, turn and opacity, and a photo's focus and shape, how each element moves (how it arrives as it scrolls into view and after what delay, an effect as the page scrolls, what it does under the pointer, and staying in view while its section scrolls past), and a layer name and groupId for the editor's layers list, so elements sharing a groupId select and move together): the copy blocks, forms (by formId), booking sections (by typeSlug), the LIVE sections that show the community's own courses (courseCatalog, every published one or a picked list of course ids), upcoming public events (eventsList), store products (productGrid, every listed one or a picked list of product ids) and one of the website's collections (collection, by collectionId from manage_collection/list, with a layout, an order, a tag to show only and a count; adding one, or a button that opens a popup: Available on the Creator plan, while one a page already holds keeps saving), each read when the page renders and only what a stranger may see, link lists, announcement bars, stats, marquees, social feeds, Latest posts from the blog (the newest, one category's or author's, or picked posts by id), profile headers, video links, image, gallery, logo and before-and-after blocks, pricing tables and the designer's saved layouts the templates are built from. Every photo slot takes a photo from the stock library (manage_page/stock_photos), one the page already holds, or one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos, or a new one from manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link); a photo or video the coach uploaded is kept when its section's id is copied back (a gallery's or logo row's by the photo number read prints), and no other file of theirs (a lesson video, a resource) is ever taken. On a plan with custom code (every plan today) a custom code block is written and edited here too, its name, HTML, CSS, JavaScript and slot values, and whether it runs in its own frame or is drawn into the page (render inline, only with no script: sanitized, read by search, and able to mount a real form or booking picker where a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot sits; otherwise stack a custom block, a form or booking section and another custom block, never a form built in HTML), and any section's own CSS (customCss); the retired email box is edited, never added. Every button's style and destination is part of its section (on a pricing table, of its tier; on a link list, of its button), and so are each section's alignment, spacing (or its own space above and below and its widest, in pixels; on a two-column section the column split and what a phone shows first), background tone, custom colours, colour fade, hidden flag, which screens it shows on (every screen, desktop only or phones only), how it arrives as it scrolls into view (a curated entrance: a quiet rise, none, fade, slide from the left or right, zoom, or its items one after another; never on a hero or a sticky bar), the focal point that keeps each photo's crop on what matters, and its own variants, so they are read and written here too. Also lays a template over a DRAFT page, moves the page to a new address, shows or hides its header, and sets the page's own button style, fonts (headings, body, and a label font for eyebrows, buttons and the header navigation), colours, header button, footer, social links and search title and description, whether search engines may list it, the picture a shared link to it shows (a stock photo or one of the community's uploaded page photos), and who can see a WEBSITE page (pageSettings.audience: everyone, members only, with tierId members on one tier and up, or anyone with the password, set with a write-only pageSettings.password that is never shown back; the home page stays public).
- layouts: The designer's saved layouts a section can use, by category; with a comp key, that design's slots, caps, repeating items and buttons, plus a blank section to fill.
- templates: The finished funnel page templates, by what the page is for, with the key create and update take to start a page from one.
- stock_photos: Drry's own stock photos, the same ones the page editor's Choose from stock offers: the set the templates ship with, then the stock library's page photos this community may pick now. Each with the key a photo slot takes, its shape, mood, the kinds of coach it suits, whether it shows people, its search words and what it shows; narrowed by query, niche and shape, at most limit of them. A profile photo or a testimonial's photo takes none (it stands for a real person). Ends with any photo the coach uploaded in the last hour that no page shows yet.
- upload_photo: Store ONE new photo in the community's storage for its pages, from a public address (url, fetched by Drry) or the picture's bytes (data, base64), and get the imageKey a photo slot takes. JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, judged from the bytes; counted against the plan's storage; the same picture again is not stored twice. For several photos with addresses, use manage_page/upload_photos instead. Place it soon: one no page shows is removed once it is an hour old, the next time a photo is added through an assistant or any page is saved, unless sent with keep: true, which holds it for 30 days.
- upload_photos: Store up to 20 photos from public addresses (urls) in ONE call, fetched and checked exactly as manage_page/upload_photo's url is, 4 at a time; per address, in the order sent, its imageKey or why it was not stored, so one bad address never fails the others. Storage is decided photo by photo: once the plan's storage refuses one, the rest are not fetched and what was stored stays. The way to bring in many photos, rather than one call each or base64. keep: true holds the unplaced ones for 30 days instead of an hour.
- photo_upload_link: A one-time, 30-minute link to a Drry page where the connected coach drops ONE photo from their device, for a photo you cannot send yourself (one attached in the chat). Returns the link and an uploadId for manage_page/uploaded_photos. keep: true holds that photo for 30 days if no page shows it yet.
- uploaded_photos: The community's own uploaded page photos, newest first (the page editor's Your photos), each with its imageKey, when it arrived, whether a page shows it yet and, for one no page shows, when it will be removed (an hour after it arrived, or the end of its 30 days when uploaded with keep); with uploadId, whether the coach has added that upload link's photo.
- edit_section: Rewrite ONE section by its id, leaving every other section exactly as stored. Send the section whole, as update takes it: its words are replaced by what is sent, while style settings, links, photos and videos left out carry over. The cheap way to change one block, and it works beside sections update cannot write (except a custom block off a plan with custom code, which blocks every save of its page until it is removed).
- insert_section: Add ONE new section at a position (the bottom when none is given).
- move_section: Move ONE section to a new position. Nothing else changes.
- duplicate_section: Copy ONE section to just below itself, with a fresh id to edit separately.
- remove_section: Remove ONE section. Refused for a section holding the coach's own photo or video, or one another button points at.
- customize_layout: Customize layout on ONE section of a WEBSITE page: the house section becomes a freeform layout holding the same words, photos and buttons as elements that move one by one, keeping its id and a phone layout; the answer names what did not carry over. One-way but for the page's history; live sections, page chrome and designed sections stay as they are.
- score: Check the page against a checklist that needs no traffic (headline, buttons, proof, readable colours, placeholders and fill-in text, search title, and words hidden inside custom code), 0 to 100, never Strong while fill-in text is left, with what to fix and the section it is in; a website page leaves out the sales checks.
- preview: Screenshots of the page as a visitor sees it, desktop, phone or both, a draft too; a whole page in screens, or one section. A custom block without a script is drawn from its HTML and CSS; one with a script shows as a placeholder, so it also gives a private link to the page as saved, drafts included, that anyone holding it can open for one hour without signing in, scripts running.
- history: The page's earlier versions, newest first, each the page as it stood before a change (who, when, through the console or an assistant); with a versionId, that version's sections and what restoring it would change.
- copy_section: Copy ONE section into the page as it is now, beside what is there: from an earlier version (versionId, manage_page/history), from the page in a website restore point (restorePointId, manage_site/history), or from another page of this community as it stands (fromPageId, with index for where it goes). Photos and videos come with it. The page as it was is kept first, so it can be undone.
- saved_sections: The sections this community saved for reuse (the editor's "Your saved sections"), each with its id and any page it cannot go on and why; with savedSectionId, one in full.
- save_section: Keep ONE of a page's sections, as stored, for reuse on any page of the community, under a name (its heading when none is given). The page does not change.
- insert_saved_section: Drop a fresh copy of a saved section into a page at a position (the bottom when none is given), with its own id; kept in the page's history.
- rename_saved_section: Give a saved section a new name. Pages using a copy do not change.
- restore: Put an earlier version back (name, sections, design, header; never the address or whether it is published). The page as it is now is kept first, so a restore can be undone.
- publish: Put a funnel or website page live at its address, or take one down. Search engines may index it unless it is hidden from search (pageSettings noindex), members only or behind a password.
- delete: Delete a page that is unpublished now (a draft, or one taken down, whatever it was before) and is not the home page, unless a published page, a live popup or anything else still sends people to it. Cannot be undone.

sections.description: The page, top to bottom; or leave it out and send `template`. Section ids are minted here, so any id you send is ignored. Sections take an optional align (default, left, center, right; default keeps the section's own alignment) except these types: announcement, logos, profileHeader, form, stickyCta, linkList, marquee, custom, freeform; an optional spacing (normal, compact, roomy) except: announcement, stickyCta, custom; and an optional bgTone (default, tint, inverted, accent) except: announcement, ctaBanner, hero, stickyCta. The page does not render those there, so they are refused there. A sticky call to action is a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen and takes none of the three. manage_page/read prints each one that is set. Every section also takes hidden (true keeps it in the editor and off the live page) and three custom colours, bgColor, accentColor and textColor (each "#rrggbb", or "" to follow the theme). Every section but a sticky call to action and a saved layout takes a colour fade behind it, bgGradient ({from, to, angle}, the angle 0 to 360 with 180 pointing down; null removes it), a background photo, bgImageKey, and while it holds one, bgOverlay, the shade over that photo (dark, darker, light, none; dark is the default), and bgMotion, how it moves as the page scrolls (none, the default; parallax; slowZoom; a visitor who asks for less motion sees it still). A section the read prints with bgVideo true holds a looping background video the coach uploaded in the page editor (videos are never uploaded here): it covers any photo or fade, takes bgOverlay and bgMotion like a photo, is kept while bgVideo is left out or sent as true with the section's id, and bgVideo null takes it off (the page's history keeps it, so it can be restored). A PHOTO SLOT (bgImageKey, a hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageKey, a before-and-after's beforeKey and afterKey, a gallery or logo row item's imageKey, a saved layout's or a custom block's image slot) takes a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos, like "stock:cover-coastline", a photo this page already holds, one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos; add a new one with manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link), or "" for none; never any other file. Videos are uploaded in the page editor, and every photo and video a section holds is kept when its id is copied back and the slot is left out (a gallery or logo row item's by the photo number manage_page/read printed beside it; a testimonial's while it keeps a name no other testimonial has). A profile header's avatar and a testimonial's photo are a person, so they are uploaded only. A hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageStyle, imageFinish, imageAspect and imageAlt, and an image section's imageLayout and caption, apply only while it holds an image, and so does a hero's or an image-and-text block's imageLayout ("bleed" runs a split photo to the screen edge). A hero and a cta banner take secondaryCta ({label, link, style}), a quieter second button beside the first, and an image-and-text block takes the hero's ctaLabel, ctaLink, ctaStyle and buttons for a button under its words. A form section's formId and a booking section's typeSlug are checked against what this community has. A custom code block (a plan with custom code) takes label, html, css and js, the code running sandboxed on the page, render (frame, the default, or inline: a block with no js drawn into the page through a sanitizer, so search reads its words), and fields, the values of the typed slots its html declares as {{type:key}} (text, markdown, link as a destination object, date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM, datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, image, and in an inline block form, a form id, and booking, a session type's slug, each mounting the real widget there), a patch where "" clears one; left out on a block whose id you copied back, each keeps what it has. THE COACH EDITS EVERY SLOT in the page editor's Content panel as a plain field, without touching code, and copy written straight into the html can only be changed in the code editor. So write each heading, paragraph, photo and button destination a coach would change as a slot ({{text:headline}}, , ) with its value in fields, and keep only structure and design in the html; a write's answer names any block whose copy or photos are fixed in the html. Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. Every section takes device (all, the default; desktop, hidden on phones; or phone, hidden on larger screens). Every section but a hero and a sticky call to action takes entrance, how it arrives as it scrolls into view: default (a quiet rise), none, fade, slideLeft, slideRight, zoom, or stagger (its items one after another, only on a section with items: value props, testimonials, stats, logos, steps, pricing, gallery, FAQ, link list and the four live sections). A FOCAL POINT, {x, y} in whole percentages from the left and the top (null is the centre), keeps the crop on what matters: imageFocus beside a hero's, an image-and-text block's, an image section's or a profile header's photo, bgImageFocus beside bgImageKey, a gallery item's focus, and a before-and-after's beforeFocus and afterFocus; each only while that photo is there, and a new photo starts centred. Beside each focal point the same photo takes an EDIT (imageEdit, bgImageEdit, a gallery item's edit, beforeEdit and afterEdit, and a freeform photo's style.edit): crop {x, y, w, h} in fractions of the turned photo (three decimals, w and h at least 0.1, inside the photo), turn 90, 180 or 270 clockwise, flip h or v (of the turned photo), adjust {brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth} each a whole number from -100 to 100, and filter (mono, sepia, fade, vivid, cool, warm); null removes it, left out it is kept while the photo stays, and a new photo starts unedited. A freeform photo's edit lives in its style, so it follows the style: a sent style replaces it whole (leave edit out of it to remove the edit), and a style left out keeps the edit while the photo stays. A built-in template photo (a stock key without "lib/") takes adjust and filter only: crop, turn and flip need an uploaded photo or a library photo. Every section but an announcement bar, a sticky call to action, a custom code block and a freeform layout takes exact space in whole pixels, padTop and padBottom (0 to 320), and maxWidth, the widest its content runs (360 to 1600); null clears one back to the section's own. Sent to one of those four, they are left out and the answer says so, rather than refusing the write. The same sections, and a freeform layout too, take dividers, a shape over the section's top and bottom edges, {top, bottom}, each {shape, height, flip, color} or null: shape one of wave, curve, tilt, triangle, zigzag, arch, cloud, drip; height sm, md (the default) or lg; flip true mirrors it; color a theme token (foreground, muted, accent, background) or "#rrggbb", left out to take the colour of the section next to it; dividers null removes both, and dividers left out keeps them. A section drawn as a photo beside words (an image-and-text block in its beside layout, or a hero in its split or splitLeft layout) also takes split, the left column's share of the row in whole percent (25 to 75), and phoneOrder, what a phone shows first where the columns stack: auto (as designed), photo, words, or hidePhoto. Every section but a sticky call to action takes customCss (a plan with custom code), the section's own CSS written as usual (h1 { letter-spacing: -0.02em; }): it applies to that section only, a url() must be https, and @import or a < is refused; "" clears it. Its rules WIN over the house styles inside the section, whatever their specificity (h2 { font-weight: 400; color: #333; } beats the bold headline and the Text colour). Every rule needs a selector: :scope (or &) is the section itself, and a declaration on it only inherits, so it never reaches a heading that sets the property itself. Stable hooks: the section's root carries data-section-type (its type), a headline is an h1, h2 or h3 with the class display, a small label above it is .eyebrow, body copy is p, and a button is an a. The screenshot (manage_page/preview) draws it as the page does.

bullets.description: What the offer includes, one short line each.

showPrice.description: true shows the community's live membership price in the block. The price itself is never written here.

ctaEnabled.description: false hides the offer's button. Omitted or true shows it.

ctaStyle.description: The button's fill: solid (the default), outline, or ghost. This is the one axis `buttons` does not carry.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", which is the default and follows the page's own button style, which follows the community-wide one that manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS. highlighted.description: true marks this tier as the one to pick. Only the first highlighted tier is shown that way.

tiers.description: Up to four tiers, left to right. A tier keeps its destination, label and highlight when it keeps a name no other tier has, before and after the edit.

comp.description: Which design, by key: manage_page/layouts lists them, and manage_page/read prints the key of each one already on the page.

slots.description: The design's words, keyed by slot. Text is plain and held to the cap manage_page/layouts gives for that slot. groups.description: The design's repeating items (quotes, cards, rows), keyed by group, each item keyed by slot. A group sent here replaces that group whole, and must hold as many items as the design allows.

links.description: Where each of the design's buttons goes, keyed by the button's slot. The same destinations as a hero's `ctaLink`.

variant.description: A design choice the layout offers, such as a skin. manage_page/layouts lists the values; the first is the default.

buttons.description: How the buttons in this layout look: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing, fill and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", the default, which follows the page's own button style.

formId.description: The form this section shows, by id (list_catalog/forms lists them; manage_form/create makes a new one as a draft). The whole form renders here: its fields, its button and what happens after a submit. A draft is accepted but shows nothing on the live page, and the page cannot be published, until the form is. "" leaves the section waiting for a form.

typeSlug.description: The session type visitors book right on the page, by slug (list_catalog/booking_types lists them). Its real availability renders here. "" leaves the section waiting for one.

body.description: Plain text. A single newline is a line break; no other formatting is rendered here.
Optional line under the title.

mode.description: Which posts the blog shows here: latest (the default, the newest published posts, kept up to date as the coach publishes), category (one category's, with categoryId), author (one author's, with authorId; the owner's profile also takes posts with no byline), or picked (the posts in postIds, in that order). Only published posts show; a members-only post shows with a lock.

layout.description: grid (the default, the blog home's own cards), list (compact rows), carousel (one row that swipes) or featured (the first post large, the rest listed).

count.description: How many posts, 1 to 12 (default 3). A picked section shows every post it names instead.

categoryId.description: The category a category section lists, by the categoryId manage_blog/read prints. "" clears it.

authorId.description: The author an author section lists, by the authorRef manage_blog/read prints for an author with a profile (a "user:" ref has no profile, so no posts). "" clears it.

postIds.description: The posts a picked section shows, in order, by the postId manage_blog/read prints; up to 12, each once. A post that is not published shows nothing until it is.

showAuthor.description: Who each post is by (default off).

viewAll.description: A View all button under the posts (default on), to the blog, or to the category's or author's page.

viewAllLabel.description: The View all button's words. "" means "View all posts".

label.description: What it counts, like "members".

placement.description: inline (the default) sits in the page like any section; top sits above the header and scrolls away with the page.

tone.description: inverted (the default, dark), accent (the brand colour) or plain.

text.description: The one line. Plain text.

ctaLabel.description: An optional inline link's words. "" shows the text alone, with no link.

tone.description: The band: accent (the default, the brand colour), soft or ink.

words.description: Short words or phrases that drift across the band, one each.

label.description: The button's words.

style.description: primary (a filled pill, for the one thing that matters most) or card (a quiet bordered row, the default for a new button).

source.description: all (the default: every published course a visitor may see, in the coach's own order, cut at `count`) or picked (exactly the courses in `courseIds`, in that order).

courseIds.description: The courses a picked section shows, in order, by id (manage_course/list prints them). A draft is accepted and shows once published. Kept when `source` is all, so switching back restores the list. A course locked to a membership tier shows locked, naming the tier; a hidden one never shows.

count.description: How many courses on all, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 6). A picked list is not cut by it.

layout.description: grid (the default, covers) or list (compact rows).

count.description: How many upcoming events, soonest first, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 3). Only events open to anyone with their public page on are listed; members-only, invite-only and tier-limited events never are.

layout.description: cards (the default, with covers) or list (compact rows with the date).

source.description: all (the default: every product the store sells and lists, newest first, cut at `count`) or picked (exactly the products in `productIds`, in that order).

productIds.description: The products a picked section shows, in order, by id (list_catalog/products prints them). Only a product on sale can be picked; one hidden from the store shows nothing. Kept when `source` is all.

count.description: How many products on all, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 6). A picked list is not cut by it.

layout.description: grid (the default, product shots) or list (compact rows).

collectionId.description: The website collection it shows (manage_collection/list prints each collectionId): its LIVE items only, read when the page renders. Left out on a new section, it shows nothing until one is set.

layout.description: grid (the default, cards), list (compact rows) or carousel (a row that scrolls sideways).

sort.description: manual (the default: the collection's own order), newest, oldest (by the item's first date, else when it was made) or title (A to Z).

tag.description: Show only items carrying this tag (any case); "" for every item.

count.description: How many items, 1 to 24 (a new section shows 6).

showLink.description: false hides the "See all" link to the collection's own page (shown by default, and only when its items have pages).

platform.description: instagram (the default), tiktok or youtube: the platform a bare post id is on. It does not limit the section: a link names its own platform, so one feed can mix Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Changing it keeps every post the section already holds on its own platform.

posts.description: The coach's own posts, embedded on the page, in order: each a post's full link (instagram.com/p/... or /reel/..., tiktok.com/@name/video/..., youtube.com/shorts/...) or the id manage_page/read printed (a post on another platform than the section's prints as tiktok:<id> or youtube:<id>; send it back as printed). A TikTok short share link cannot be read; send the full address. A YouTube link must be the Short's own youtube.com/shorts/ address: youtu.be, watch?v= and embed links can be regular videos, which are refused and belong in a video section.

postSize.description: standard (the default, three across on a wide screen) or large (two across, bigger).

mobileLayout.description: stack (the default, one under another on a phone) or swipe (one sideways row a visitor swipes through on a phone).

socials.description: The social icons under the name, as a PATCH: each network's full http(s) profile link, "" to hide that icon, and a network left out keeps what it has. The avatar is a photo, added in the funnel editor; without one the page shows the name's initial.

url.description: A YouTube or Vimeo link (an unlisted one included), embedded on the page. "" takes it off. An uploaded video is added in the funnel editor, never here, and one the section holds is kept when its id comes back.

source.description: Which the section shows: embed (the link) or native (the video uploaded in the page editor). A section sent a url and no source shows the link. Switching a section that holds an uploaded video to embed would delete that upload, so it is refused here.

imageLayout.description: How wide the photo sits: contained (the default, the reading column), wide or fullBleed (edge to edge).

caption.description: A short line under the photo.

layout.description: grid (the default), carousel (a swipeable slider), masonry (a staggered collage) or strip (the photos drifting slowly across the page).

animation.description: A carousel's transition: slide (the default), fade, rotate3d or coverflow. Only on a carousel.

autoplay.description: true advances a carousel on its own. Only on a carousel.

columns.description: How many columns a grid or masonry uses: "auto" (the default, from the photo count), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a carousel.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: What the photo shows, for screen readers.

layout.description: grid (the default) or marquee, the logos drifting slowly across the page.

columns.description: "auto" (the default), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a marquee.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: The brand or publication the logo stands for.

style.description: slider (the default, a draggable split), sideBySide or toggle (tap to swap).

beforeLabel.description: The corner label on the first photo; "" hides it.

afterLabel.description: The corner label on the second photo; "" hides it.

layout.description: centered (the default) or bar, a compact strip that shows no subtext.

subtext.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

proof.description: A reassuring line under the form.

successBody.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

collectName.description: true adds a name field before the email.

nameRequired.description: true makes that name field required. Only with collectName.

redirectUrl.description: Where a visitor goes after signing up: a path on this site like "/p/thanks", or an https address. "" shows the success message instead.

welcomeEmailId.description: A saved email sent to each new signup, by id (manage_email/read lists them). "" sends nothing.

listId.description: A contact list each signup is added to, by id. "" adds them to none (they are still captured as a contact).

width.description: contained (the default, a centred column) or full (edge to edge).

grid.description: standard (the default: 24 columns of 24px rows on desktop and tablet, 8 on a phone) or fine (48 columns of 12px rows, 16 on a phone), and every place in this section is on it. Left out it keeps the section's grid. Switching moves every place the section keeps onto the new grid: to fine exactly (each number doubled), back to standard rounded to the nearest cell, and the answer says what rounded. Places sent in the same call are read on the new grid.

minRows.description: The section's least height in grid rows (default 12, at most 200 on the standard grid and 400 on the fine one); content taller than it grows it.

name.description: The element's name in the editor's layers list, for the coach only: it is never drawn on the page. "" takes it off, and the list names the element from what it shows.

groupId.description: Elements sharing a groupId (any short word, like "hero-copy") are one group in the editor: they select and move together. A group needs two or more elements. null takes this element out of its group.

text.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

preset.description: A text element's size and role: body (the default) renders the formatting `text` takes; h1, h2, h3 and eyebrow are plain text. An h1 takes the page's one main heading.

color.description: A text's, a line's or an icon's colour, and a BUTTON's label colour (also the line of an outline or ghost button). accent follows the section's accentColor.

ctaLink.description: Where the button goes. join (the default) is the community's join or checkout page. fill.description: A shape's colour, and a BUTTON's own colour: a solid button's background. Left out, a button is drawn in the page's ink (foreground), so the section's accentColor does not recolour it; send accent to follow the accent, or #rrggbb. A button's label colour is color.

size.description: Text only. A step on the scale (xs 12px, sm 14px, base 16px, lg 18px, xl 20px, 2xl 24px, 3xl 30px, 4xl 36px, 5xl 48px, 6xl 60px, 7xl 72px), which follows the site, or an exact size in px (10 to 160). A large size draws smaller on a phone.

lineHeight.description: Text only. Unitless, 0.8 to 2.5, stored in steps of 0.05.

letterSpacing.description: Text only. In em, -0.1 to 0.5, stored in steps of 0.01.

textCase.description: Text only. Left out, the letters are as typed.

fill.description: Text only: a box filled behind the words, which they are then checked against.

opacity.description: In percent. Left out, fully opaque.

border.description: Text, image and shape. Width in px.

style.description: solid (the default), dashed or dotted.

color.description: Left out, foreground.

radius.description: Text, image and shape: corner rounding in px, one number for all four or each corner (tl, tr, br, bl). It takes the place of the element's own radius.

shadow.description: Text, image and shape: the house elevations, lowest first.

padding.description: Text only: space inside the box, in px.

rotation.description: Turned by this many degrees, either way.

focus.description: Image only: the point kept in view when the photo is cropped, in percent. Left out, the centre.

edit.description: Image only: the photo's crop, turn, flip, adjust and filter, as a section photo's edit takes them. Left out, none.

mask.description: Image only: a shape the photo is cut to. It takes the place of the corners.

style.description: The element's own style. Left out, the element keeps the style it has; sent, it REPLACES that style whole; null puts it back to the site style. Each kind takes only some fields (named on each). Colour, alignment, a shape's fill and a photo's fit stay on the element itself, beside its style, not in it. A text colour that would not read on what it sits on (below 4.5 to 1) is drawn in a readable shade of it on the page, and manage_page/read says so.

enter.description: How it arrives as it scrolls into view: rise, fade, slideLeft (in from the left), slideRight (in from the right) or zoom. Left out, it is simply there. One already on screen when the page opens is never hidden, and a section whose elements arrive on their own takes no section entrance.

delay.description: With enter only: wait this many tenths of a second before it arrives.

scroll.description: An effect tied to scrolling: parallaxSlow or parallaxFast (it drifts against the page), fadeIn, riseIn or scaleIn (each done once it is fully on screen), or fadeOut (as it leaves the top). At most 12 elements in a section. A browser without scroll-driven animations shows it still.

hover.description: Under the pointer, on screens that have one: lift, grow, shadow, tint (the brand colour: over a photo or a shape, or as the ink of a text or an icon) or dim (it fades back). Each kind takes only some: text lift, grow, shadow, tint; image lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; button lift, grow, shadow; shape lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; line lift, grow, dim; icon lift, grow, tint, dim. A text tint that would not read on what it sits on is left off the page, and manage_page/read says so.

pin.description: top: it stays in view below the header while the rest of its section scrolls past, on larger screens. On a phone it sits where it was placed.

motion.description: How the element moves. Left out, it keeps the motion it has; sent, it REPLACES that motion whole; null makes it still. A visitor who asks their device for less motion sees it still whatever is set.

editElements.description: INSTEAD OF elements, to change some elements and keep the rest: each entry names a stored element by id (with its kind) and carries only what changes; every element it does not name is kept exactly as it is, in its place. An id the section does not hold is refused (add a new element through elements). Sending elements replaces the list whole: an element left out of it is removed.

tablet.description: The tablet layout (screens 768 to 1023px wide): a place for each element on the same grid as desktop (24 columns, 48 on the fine grid), keyed by element id like mobile. Left out it keeps what is stored; null (or never set) means tablets show the desktop layout. An element it does not place sits under the tablet layout.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", which is the default and follows the page's own button style, which follows the community-wide one that manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS. The FILL is the exception: on these sections it is the section's own `ctaStyle` field (solid, outline or ghost) that the page renders from, so a `fill` here other than "auto" is REFUSED rather than stored, and the refusal says to send `ctaStyle` instead.

label.description: The block's name in the section list, for the coach only.

html.description: Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. With render inline (and no js) it can hold two NATIVE WIDGET slots that mount the real thing at that spot, inside the block's own layout: {{form:<key>}}, a form from the forms builder, and {{booking:<key>}}, a session type's booking picker. Which one: the slot's value in fields when set (a form id from list_catalog/forms, a session type's slug), else the key itself, so {{form:<form id>}} and {{booking:intro-call}} need no field. Each must sit in a <div>, a <section>, a list item or a table cell, never inside a paragraph, a heading or a link, and the form must be published for the page to publish. To put a real form beside a custom design otherwise, stack the sections: a custom block, then a form or booking section (style it with its customCss), then another custom block. Never build a form in the html: it submits nowhere, and the sanitizer removes it.

css.description: The block's own styles. Drawn inline, every rule is scoped to the block (html, body and :root mean the block itself; a rule reaching the block's siblings is dropped), and a sheet with a < character, a url() that is not https, or a script address is left out whole; an @import is removed (the page's own fonts apply). A native widget a slot mounts sits in a <div data-drry-widget="form"> or "booking" the styles can select.

js.description: Inline code only: the sandbox blocks external scripts and network calls. A block with any script always runs in its own frame, whatever render says.

render.description: How the block draws. "frame" (the default, and what a block left out of this field keeps) runs it sandboxed in its own frame, script included, where search does not read it. "inline" draws a block with NO script straight into the page so search engines read its words, after a strict sanitizer: no script, no event handler (onclick and every other on attribute), no javascript: or data: address, no data-* attribute, no frame, form, input, button, object, embed, base, meta, link or style tag; links must be https, a /path on this site, a #part, mailto: or tel:; pictures and videos https or a photo of this site; an inline style keeps only declarations that load nothing else. The write answer names what it removed. Only an inline block can hold a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot.

template.description: A template key from manage_page/templates: the page is made from that finished design, its sections, colours, fonts and search copy, all placeholders to edit afterwards. Instead of `sections`, never with them. pageSettings and pageButtons sent beside it are laid over the template's look.

hideHeader.description: true makes the page with its header bar (the logo, its button and its social icons) hidden.

pageButtons.description: How every button on THIS page looks, over the community's funnel default (manage_studio/read prints it under BUTTONS) and under any one section's own `buttons`. Send only the axes to change: one left out keeps what the page has, and "auto" puts it back to following the community default. manage_page/read prints what the page sets.

pageSettings.description: The rest of this page's settings, as a PATCH: send only what changes; a field left out keeps what the page has, and manage_page/read prints every one that is set. navCtaLabel is the header button's words ("" is "Join"), showNavCta false hides that button, navCtaLink is where it goes (the same destinations as a section's button; {"kind":"join"} is the join page). displayFont (headings) and bodyFont (paragraphs) take a font name, or "" to follow the Studio: any Google Fonts family by its name (e.g. "Archivo Black", "Instrument Sans"), served by Drry; the curated menu is Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Cormorant Garamond, Spectral, Bricolage Grotesque, Space Grotesk, Montserrat, Lato, System Sans, Libre Caslon Text, Young Serif, EB Garamond, Dancing Script, Marcellus, IBM Plex Serif, Bitter, Alegreya, Vollkorn, Petrona, Averia Serif Libre, Bodoni Moda, Italiana, Cinzel, Literata, Newsreader, Zilla Slab, Crimson Pro, Libre Bodoni, Besley, Gloock, Anton, Archivo Black, Sora, Space Mono, Fragment Mono, Oswald, Familjen Grotesk, Rubik, Gabarito, Unbounded, Schibsted Grotesk, Syne, Outfit, Jost, Red Hat Display, Albert Sans, Barlow, Figtree, Alegreya Sans, Hanken Grotesk, Inter, Work Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Nunito Sans, Lora, IBM Plex Sans, Karla, Public Sans, Manrope, Mulish, Epilogue, Chivo, Assistant, Cabin, Raleway, Source Sans 3, Red Hat Text, Archivo, IBM Plex Mono, Georgia, Palatino, System Mono. labelFont is a THIRD font for the page's eyebrows, its buttons and the site header's navigation, the same names (a mono suits it, e.g. "IBM Plex Mono"), or null (or "") to take it off so each keeps the face it was designed in. accentColor and paper (the page background) take "#rrggbb", or "" to follow the Studio. showFooter false hides the footer (on a website page, the SITE footer, on this page alone: for a page that draws its own, say in one custom code block; true shows it again); copyright is a funnel footer's line ("" writes the year and the community name). showSocialsInNav and showSocialsInFooter show the social icons there; socials sets each network's full http(s) profile link (instagram, facebook, tiktok, threads, x, pinterest, linkedin, youtube, substack, website), "" hiding its icon; contactEmail adds an email icon. metaTitle and metaDescription are what search results and shared links show ("" derives them from the page). noindex true keeps search engines off the page (it stays open to anyone with the link and leaves the sitemap); false lists it again. socialImage is the picture a shared link shows: a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos, or "" for the default (on a website page the site's default, set with manage_site/set_chrome, else a card made from the page); the coach's own photo is chosen in the console. WEBSITE PAGES ONLY: audience members makes the page members-only (visitors see its name in the menu with a lock and a panel asking them to join or sign in; members, and the coach's team, see the page; search engines are asked to leave it out), public opens it to everyone again; tierId (an id from list_catalog/membership_tiers, above the entry tier, Growth, owner or admin only) limits it to members on that tier and up, and null with audience members lets any member in. audience password, with password (at least 6 characters), puts the page behind a shared password: anyone who types it opens the page, no account needed, and the coach's team opens it signed in; members get no way round it. password is WRITE-ONLY: it is stored only as a hash, never shown back by any read, and sending a new one to a password page changes it, which makes everybody who opened it with the old one type the new one. The home page, and a page whose address is a word the community already uses, stay public. It applies at once, live or not.

comp.description: A design key from this list, or as manage_page/read printed it. Omit to list them all.

query.description: Words to search by, like "calm morning" or "kitchen": every word must appear in a photo's description, mood or search words. Leave it out to list every photo.

niche.description: Only photos made for this kind of coach (the coach kinds manage_site/templates files websites by).

shape.description: Only photos of this shape: wide (about 16:9), landscape, square or portrait.

limit.description: How many to list, 1 to 100; 40 when left out.

url.description: The picture's own public address (https:// or http://), not a page that shows it. Send this or data.

data.description: The picture's bytes, base64 (or a data:image/...;base64, address), at most 3 MB decoded. Send this or url.

keep.description: true holds a photo no page shows yet for 30 days instead of an hour, for one the coach will place later. After the 30 days it is removed like any unplaced photo. Leave it out for a photo you are about to place.

urls.description: 1 to 20 public addresses (https:// or http://) of the pictures themselves, not pages that show them.

uploadId.description: From manage_page/photo_upload_link, to ask about that link's photo.

sectionId.description: The section's id, as manage_page/read printed it.

subtitle.description: A lighter line under the headline. Plain text; "" removes it.

count.description: How many upcoming events, soonest first, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 3). Only events open to anyone with their public page on are listed; members-only, invite-only and tier-limited events never are.

layout.description: cards (the default, with covers) or list (compact rows with the date).

source.description: all (the default: every product the store sells and lists, newest first, cut at `count`) or picked (exactly the products in `productIds`, in that order).

productIds.description: The products a picked section shows, in order, by id (list_catalog/products prints them). Only a product on sale can be picked; one hidden from the store shows nothing. Kept when `source` is all.

count.description: How many products on all, 1 to 12 (a new section shows 6). A picked list is not cut by it.

layout.description: grid (the default, product shots) or list (compact rows).

collectionId.description: The website collection it shows (manage_collection/list prints each collectionId): its LIVE items only, read when the page renders. Left out on a new section, it shows nothing until one is set.

layout.description: grid (the default, cards), list (compact rows) or carousel (a row that scrolls sideways).

sort.description: manual (the default: the collection's own order), newest, oldest (by the item's first date, else when it was made) or title (A to Z).

tag.description: Show only items carrying this tag (any case); "" for every item.

count.description: How many items, 1 to 24 (a new section shows 6).

showLink.description: false hides the "See all" link to the collection's own page (shown by default, and only when its items have pages).

platform.description: instagram (the default), tiktok or youtube: the platform a bare post id is on. It does not limit the section: a link names its own platform, so one feed can mix Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Changing it keeps every post the section already holds on its own platform.

posts.description: The coach's own posts, embedded on the page, in order: each a post's full link (instagram.com/p/... or /reel/..., tiktok.com/@name/video/..., youtube.com/shorts/...) or the id manage_page/read printed (a post on another platform than the section's prints as tiktok:<id> or youtube:<id>; send it back as printed). A TikTok short share link cannot be read; send the full address. A YouTube link must be the Short's own youtube.com/shorts/ address: youtu.be, watch?v= and embed links can be regular videos, which are refused and belong in a video section.

postSize.description: standard (the default, three across on a wide screen) or large (two across, bigger).

mobileLayout.description: stack (the default, one under another on a phone) or swipe (one sideways row a visitor swipes through on a phone).

socials.description: The social icons under the name, as a PATCH: each network's full http(s) profile link, "" to hide that icon, and a network left out keeps what it has. The avatar is a photo, added in the funnel editor; without one the page shows the name's initial.

url.description: A YouTube or Vimeo link (an unlisted one included), embedded on the page. "" takes it off. An uploaded video is added in the funnel editor, never here, and one the section holds is kept when its id comes back.

source.description: Which the section shows: embed (the link) or native (the video uploaded in the page editor). A section sent a url and no source shows the link. Switching a section that holds an uploaded video to embed would delete that upload, so it is refused here.

imageLayout.description: How wide the photo sits: contained (the default, the reading column), wide or fullBleed (edge to edge).

caption.description: A short line under the photo.

layout.description: grid (the default), carousel (a swipeable slider), masonry (a staggered collage) or strip (the photos drifting slowly across the page).

animation.description: A carousel's transition: slide (the default), fade, rotate3d or coverflow. Only on a carousel.

autoplay.description: true advances a carousel on its own. Only on a carousel.

columns.description: How many columns a grid or masonry uses: "auto" (the default, from the photo count), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a carousel.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: What the photo shows, for screen readers.

layout.description: grid (the default) or marquee, the logos drifting slowly across the page.

columns.description: "auto" (the default), "2", "3" or "4". Not on a marquee.

photo.description: Which of the photos this section holds this item keeps: the number manage_page/read printed beside it. Send this or imageKey, not both.

alt.description: The brand or publication the logo stands for.

style.description: slider (the default, a draggable split), sideBySide or toggle (tap to swap).

beforeLabel.description: The corner label on the first photo; "" hides it.

afterLabel.description: The corner label on the second photo; "" hides it.

layout.description: centered (the default) or bar, a compact strip that shows no subtext.

subtext.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

proof.description: A reassuring line under the form.

successBody.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

collectName.description: true adds a name field before the email.

nameRequired.description: true makes that name field required. Only with collectName.

redirectUrl.description: Where a visitor goes after signing up: a path on this site like "/p/thanks", or an https address. "" shows the success message instead.

welcomeEmailId.description: A saved email sent to each new signup, by id (manage_email/read lists them). "" sends nothing.

listId.description: A contact list each signup is added to, by id. "" adds them to none (they are still captured as a contact).

width.description: contained (the default, a centred column) or full (edge to edge).

grid.description: standard (the default: 24 columns of 24px rows on desktop and tablet, 8 on a phone) or fine (48 columns of 12px rows, 16 on a phone), and every place in this section is on it. Left out it keeps the section's grid. Switching moves every place the section keeps onto the new grid: to fine exactly (each number doubled), back to standard rounded to the nearest cell, and the answer says what rounded. Places sent in the same call are read on the new grid.

minRows.description: The section's least height in grid rows (default 12, at most 200 on the standard grid and 400 on the fine one); content taller than it grows it.

name.description: The element's name in the editor's layers list, for the coach only: it is never drawn on the page. "" takes it off, and the list names the element from what it shows.

groupId.description: Elements sharing a groupId (any short word, like "hero-copy") are one group in the editor: they select and move together. A group needs two or more elements. null takes this element out of its group.

text.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

preset.description: A text element's size and role: body (the default) renders the formatting `text` takes; h1, h2, h3 and eyebrow are plain text. An h1 takes the page's one main heading.

color.description: A text's, a line's or an icon's colour, and a BUTTON's label colour (also the line of an outline or ghost button). accent follows the section's accentColor.

ctaLink.description: Where the button goes. join (the default) is the community's join or checkout page. The others take one more field each: page takes `slug` (another funnel page), surface takes `surface` (library, community, audio, events), course takes `courseId`, paymentLink and offer take `token`, product takes `slug` and an optional `buyHere` (true opens the buy sheet on the published page, in a designed section too; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the product's page), anchor takes `sectionId` (a section on this page whose id manage_page/read printed), booking takes `typeSlug` ("" for the page listing every session type) and an optional `buyHere` (true opens that session's time picker in a sheet on the published page; refused with the "" listing; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the page), form takes `slug` (a published form, /f/<slug>), event takes `id` (an event whose public page is on, /e/<id>), guide takes `slug` (a public guide's share slug, /g/<slug>), store takes nothing else (the published store), blog takes nothing else (the blog's front page, /blog, which follows the blog's own address), blogPost takes `postId` (a published post's id from manage_blog/read; /blog/post/<id> forwards to the post's current link, so a renamed post or blog still lands), external takes an https `url`. Both blog kinds need the blog switched on. popup takes `popupId` (a LIVE popup from manage_site/popups; website pages only: the button opens the popup over the page). A destination this community does not have (or a single-use payment link, or this same page) is refused, and the refusal lists the ones it has; one the page already points at is kept as it is. On a section whose id you copied back, leaving this out keeps where the button goes now.

fill.description: A shape's colour, and a BUTTON's own colour: a solid button's background. Left out, a button is drawn in the page's ink (foreground), so the section's accentColor does not recolour it; send accent to follow the accent, or #rrggbb. A button's label colour is color.

size.description: Text only. A step on the scale (xs 12px, sm 14px, base 16px, lg 18px, xl 20px, 2xl 24px, 3xl 30px, 4xl 36px, 5xl 48px, 6xl 60px, 7xl 72px), which follows the site, or an exact size in px (10 to 160). A large size draws smaller on a phone.

lineHeight.description: Text only. Unitless, 0.8 to 2.5, stored in steps of 0.05.

letterSpacing.description: Text only. In em, -0.1 to 0.5, stored in steps of 0.01.

textCase.description: Text only. Left out, the letters are as typed.

fill.description: Text only: a box filled behind the words, which they are then checked against.

opacity.description: In percent. Left out, fully opaque.

border.description: Text, image and shape. Width in px.

style.description: solid (the default), dashed or dotted.

color.description: Left out, foreground.

radius.description: Text, image and shape: corner rounding in px, one number for all four or each corner (tl, tr, br, bl). It takes the place of the element's own radius.

shadow.description: Text, image and shape: the house elevations, lowest first.

padding.description: Text only: space inside the box, in px.

rotation.description: Turned by this many degrees, either way.

focus.description: Image only: the point kept in view when the photo is cropped, in percent. Left out, the centre.

edit.description: Image only: the photo's crop, turn, flip, adjust and filter, as a section photo's edit takes them. Left out, none.

mask.description: Image only: a shape the photo is cut to. It takes the place of the corners.

style.description: The element's own style. Left out, the element keeps the style it has; sent, it REPLACES that style whole; null puts it back to the site style. Each kind takes only some fields (named on each). Colour, alignment, a shape's fill and a photo's fit stay on the element itself, beside its style, not in it. A text colour that would not read on what it sits on (below 4.5 to 1) is drawn in a readable shade of it on the page, and manage_page/read says so.

enter.description: How it arrives as it scrolls into view: rise, fade, slideLeft (in from the left), slideRight (in from the right) or zoom. Left out, it is simply there. One already on screen when the page opens is never hidden, and a section whose elements arrive on their own takes no section entrance.

delay.description: With enter only: wait this many tenths of a second before it arrives.

scroll.description: An effect tied to scrolling: parallaxSlow or parallaxFast (it drifts against the page), fadeIn, riseIn or scaleIn (each done once it is fully on screen), or fadeOut (as it leaves the top). At most 12 elements in a section. A browser without scroll-driven animations shows it still.

hover.description: Under the pointer, on screens that have one: lift, grow, shadow, tint (the brand colour: over a photo or a shape, or as the ink of a text or an icon) or dim (it fades back). Each kind takes only some: text lift, grow, shadow, tint; image lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; button lift, grow, shadow; shape lift, grow, shadow, tint, dim; line lift, grow, dim; icon lift, grow, tint, dim. A text tint that would not read on what it sits on is left off the page, and manage_page/read says so.

pin.description: top: it stays in view below the header while the rest of its section scrolls past, on larger screens. On a phone it sits where it was placed.

motion.description: How the element moves. Left out, it keeps the motion it has; sent, it REPLACES that motion whole; null makes it still. A visitor who asks their device for less motion sees it still whatever is set.

editElements.description: INSTEAD OF elements, to change some elements and keep the rest: each entry names a stored element by id (with its kind) and carries only what changes; every element it does not name is kept exactly as it is, in its place. An id the section does not hold is refused (add a new element through elements). Sending elements replaces the list whole: an element left out of it is removed.
