tablet.description: The tablet layout (screens 768 to 1023px wide): a place for each element on the same grid as desktop (24 columns, 48 on the fine grid), keyed by element id like mobile. Left out it keeps what is stored; null (or never set) means tablets show the desktop layout. An element it does not place sits under the tablet layout.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: corner shape, button size, label size, label casing and depth. Every axis also takes "auto", which is the default and follows the page's own button style, which follows the community-wide one that manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS. The FILL is the exception: on these sections it is the section's own `ctaStyle` field (solid, outline or ghost) that the page renders from, so a `fill` here other than "auto" is REFUSED rather than stored, and the refusal says to send `ctaStyle` instead.

label.description: The block's name in the section list, for the coach only.

html.description: Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. With render inline (and no js) it can hold two NATIVE WIDGET slots that mount the real thing at that spot, inside the block's own layout: {{form:<key>}}, a form from the forms builder, and {{booking:<key>}}, a session type's booking picker. Which one: the slot's value in fields when set (a form id from list_catalog/forms, a session type's slug), else the key itself, so {{form:<form id>}} and {{booking:intro-call}} need no field. Each must sit in a <div>, a <section>, a list item or a table cell, never inside a paragraph, a heading or a link, and the form must be published for the page to publish. To put a real form beside a custom design otherwise, stack the sections: a custom block, then a form or booking section (style it with its customCss), then another custom block. Never build a form in the html: it submits nowhere, and the sanitizer removes it.

css.description: The block's own styles. Drawn inline, every rule is scoped to the block (html, body and :root mean the block itself; a rule reaching the block's siblings is dropped), and a sheet with a < character, a url() that is not https, or a script address is left out whole; an @import is removed (the page's own fonts apply). A native widget a slot mounts sits in a <div data-drry-widget="form"> or "booking" the styles can select.

js.description: Inline code only: the sandbox blocks external scripts and network calls. A block with any script always runs in its own frame, whatever render says.

render.description: How the block draws. "frame" (the default, and what a block left out of this field keeps) runs it sandboxed in its own frame, script included, where search does not read it. "inline" draws a block with NO script straight into the page so search engines read its words, after a strict sanitizer: no script, no event handler (onclick and every other on attribute), no javascript: or data: address, no data-* attribute, no frame, form, input, button, object, embed, base, meta, link or style tag; links must be https, a /path on this site, a #part, mailto: or tel:; pictures and videos https or a photo of this site; an inline style keeps only declarations that load nothing else. The write answer names what it removed. Only an inline block can hold a {{form:...}} or {{booking:...}} slot.

anyOf.description: Where the button goes. join (the default) is the community's join or checkout page. The others take one more field each: page takes `slug` (another funnel page), surface takes `surface` (library, community, audio, events), course takes `courseId`, paymentLink and offer take `token`, product takes `slug` and an optional `buyHere` (true opens the buy sheet on the published page, in a designed section too; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the product's page), anchor takes `sectionId` (a section on this page whose id manage_page/read printed), booking takes `typeSlug` ("" for the page listing every session type) and an optional `buyHere` (true opens that session's time picker in a sheet on the published page; refused with the "" listing; a freeform button or a custom code block's link field ignores buyHere and goes to the page), form takes `slug` (a published form, /f/<slug>), event takes `id` (an event whose public page is on, /e/<id>), guide takes `slug` (a public guide's share slug, /g/<slug>), store takes nothing else (the published store), blog takes nothing else (the blog's front page, /blog, which follows the blog's own address), blogPost takes `postId` (a published post's id from manage_blog/read; /blog/post/<id> forwards to the post's current link, so a renamed post or blog still lands), external takes an https `url`. Both blog kinds need the blog switched on. popup takes `popupId` (a LIVE popup from manage_site/popups; website pages only: the button opens the popup over the page). A destination this community does not have (or a single-use payment link, or this same page) is refused, and the refusal lists the ones it has; one the page already points at is kept as it is. On a section whose id you copied back, leaving this out keeps where the button goes now.

section.description: The section, whole: its type and its fields. Sections take an optional align (default, left, center, right; default keeps the section's own alignment) except these types: announcement, logos, profileHeader, form, stickyCta, linkList, marquee, custom, freeform; an optional spacing (normal, compact, roomy) except: announcement, stickyCta, custom; and an optional bgTone (default, tint, inverted, accent) except: announcement, ctaBanner, hero, stickyCta. The page does not render those there, so they are refused there. A sticky call to action is a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen and takes none of the three. manage_page/read prints each one that is set. Every section also takes hidden (true keeps it in the editor and off the live page) and three custom colours, bgColor, accentColor and textColor (each "#rrggbb", or "" to follow the theme). Every section but a sticky call to action and a saved layout takes a colour fade behind it, bgGradient ({from, to, angle}, the angle 0 to 360 with 180 pointing down; null removes it), a background photo, bgImageKey, and while it holds one, bgOverlay, the shade over that photo (dark, darker, light, none; dark is the default), and bgMotion, how it moves as the page scrolls (none, the default; parallax; slowZoom; a visitor who asks for less motion sees it still). A section the read prints with bgVideo true holds a looping background video the coach uploaded in the page editor (videos are never uploaded here): it covers any photo or fade, takes bgOverlay and bgMotion like a photo, is kept while bgVideo is left out or sent as true with the section's id, and bgVideo null takes it off (the page's history keeps it, so it can be restored). A PHOTO SLOT (bgImageKey, a hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageKey, a before-and-after's beforeKey and afterKey, a gallery or logo row item's imageKey, a saved layout's or a custom block's image slot) takes a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos, like "stock:cover-coastline", a photo this page already holds, one of the community's own uploaded page photos (manage_page/uploaded_photos; add a new one with manage_page/upload_photo or manage_page/photo_upload_link), or "" for none; never any other file. Videos are uploaded in the page editor, and every photo and video a section holds is kept when its id is copied back and the slot is left out (a gallery or logo row item's by the photo number manage_page/read printed beside it; a testimonial's while it keeps a name no other testimonial has). A profile header's avatar and a testimonial's photo are a person, so they are uploaded only. A hero's, an image-and-text block's and an image section's imageStyle, imageFinish, imageAspect and imageAlt, and an image section's imageLayout and caption, apply only while it holds an image, and so does a hero's or an image-and-text block's imageLayout ("bleed" runs a split photo to the screen edge). A hero and a cta banner take secondaryCta ({label, link, style}), a quieter second button beside the first, and an image-and-text block takes the hero's ctaLabel, ctaLink, ctaStyle and buttons for a button under its words. A form section's formId and a booking section's typeSlug are checked against what this community has. A custom code block (a plan with custom code) takes label, html, css and js, the code running sandboxed on the page, render (frame, the default, or inline: a block with no js drawn into the page through a sanitizer, so search reads its words), and fields, the values of the typed slots its html declares as {{type:key}} (text, markdown, link as a destination object, date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM, datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, image, and in an inline block form, a form id, and booking, a session type's slug, each mounting the real widget there), a patch where "" clears one; left out on a block whose id you copied back, each keeps what it has. THE COACH EDITS EVERY SLOT in the page editor's Content panel as a plain field, without touching code, and copy written straight into the html can only be changed in the code editor. So write each heading, paragraph, photo and button destination a coach would change as a slot ({{text:headline}}, , ) with its value in fields, and keep only structure and design in the html; a write's answer names any block whose copy or photos are fixed in the html. Search engines and AI answers do not read words inside custom code that runs in its own frame, so text that should be found belongs in an ordinary section or in a block with no script drawn into the page. Every section takes device (all, the default; desktop, hidden on phones; or phone, hidden on larger screens). Every section but a hero and a sticky call to action takes entrance, how it arrives as it scrolls into view: default (a quiet rise), none, fade, slideLeft, slideRight, zoom, or stagger (its items one after another, only on a section with items: value props, testimonials, stats, logos, steps, pricing, gallery, FAQ, link list and the four live sections). A FOCAL POINT, {x, y} in whole percentages from the left and the top (null is the centre), keeps the crop on what matters: imageFocus beside a hero's, an image-and-text block's, an image section's or a profile header's photo, bgImageFocus beside bgImageKey, a gallery item's focus, and a before-and-after's beforeFocus and afterFocus; each only while that photo is there, and a new photo starts centred. Beside each focal point the same photo takes an EDIT (imageEdit, bgImageEdit, a gallery item's edit, beforeEdit and afterEdit, and a freeform photo's style.edit): crop {x, y, w, h} in fractions of the turned photo (three decimals, w and h at least 0.1, inside the photo), turn 90, 180 or 270 clockwise, flip h or v (of the turned photo), adjust {brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth} each a whole number from -100 to 100, and filter (mono, sepia, fade, vivid, cool, warm); null removes it, left out it is kept while the photo stays, and a new photo starts unedited. A freeform photo's edit lives in its style, so it follows the style: a sent style replaces it whole (leave edit out of it to remove the edit), and a style left out keeps the edit while the photo stays. A built-in template photo (a stock key without "lib/") takes adjust and filter only: crop, turn and flip need an uploaded photo or a library photo. Every section but an announcement bar, a sticky call to action, a custom code block and a freeform layout takes exact space in whole pixels, padTop and padBottom (0 to 320), and maxWidth, the widest its content runs (360 to 1600); null clears one back to the section's own. Sent to one of those four, they are left out and the answer says so, rather than refusing the write. The same sections, and a freeform layout too, take dividers, a shape over the section's top and bottom edges, {top, bottom}, each {shape, height, flip, color} or null: shape one of wave, curve, tilt, triangle, zigzag, arch, cloud, drip; height sm, md (the default) or lg; flip true mirrors it; color a theme token (foreground, muted, accent, background) or "#rrggbb", left out to take the colour of the section next to it; dividers null removes both, and dividers left out keeps them. A section drawn as a photo beside words (an image-and-text block in its beside layout, or a hero in its split or splitLeft layout) also takes split, the left column's share of the row in whole percent (25 to 75), and phoneOrder, what a phone shows first where the columns stack: auto (as designed), photo, words, or hidePhoto. Every section but a sticky call to action takes customCss (a plan with custom code), the section's own CSS written as usual (h1 { letter-spacing: -0.02em; }): it applies to that section only, a url() must be https, and @import or a < is refused; "" clears it. Its rules WIN over the house styles inside the section, whatever their specificity (h2 { font-weight: 400; color: #333; } beats the bold headline and the Text colour). Every rule needs a selector: :scope (or &) is the section itself, and a declaration on it only inherits, so it never reaches a heading that sets the property itself. Stable hooks: the section's root carries data-section-type (its type), a headline is an h1, h2 or h3 with the class display, a small label above it is .eyebrow, body copy is p, and a button is an a. The screenshot (manage_page/preview) draws it as the page does.

position.description: Where it goes, 1 for the top. Omit to add it at the bottom.

to.description: Its new position, 1 for the top. Past the end means the bottom.

device.description: desktop (the default, 1280px wide), mobile (a phone, 390px wide), or both (desktop then phone in one answer; counts as two screenshots against the hourly limit).

fromScreen.description: The first screen to show, 1 for the top. The answer says how many there are.

versionId.description: Omit to list the versions; from that list to read one.

restorePointId.description: Or a website restore point holding the page, from manage_site/history.

fromPageId.description: Or another page of this community to copy from, as it stands now (manage_page/read with no pageId lists them). May be the page itself, which duplicates the section.

index.description: With fromPageId only: where it goes, 0 for the top. Absent puts it at the bottom.

savedSectionId.description: Omit to list them; from that list to read one in full.

name.description: What Add a section lists it under, up to 80 characters.

published.description: true to publish, false to take it back to a draft.

tools.name: manage_site
tools.title: Read and build the community website
tools.description:
The coach's own multi-page site: its pages, its menu, its footer, its chrome, the redirects that send a previous site's old addresses on to the new pages, its history (restore points of the whole site, and every menu, header and footer change), its languages (a version of each page in each language the site adds), its custom code (code that runs on every website page), and its popups (one section in a box over its pages). Every plan has the website, a beta: the Free plan holds up to five website pages (translations count). Popups, and languages beside the main one: Available on the Creator plan. Reading, taking down and removing work on every plan. To build a site, in order: manage_site/read, then a template (manage_site/apply_template) or pages (manage_site/create_page, then manage_page/update), the look (manage_site/set_look), the menu, footer and header (manage_site/set_menu, manage_site/set_footer, manage_site/set_chrome), search and sharing (each page's pageSettings on manage_page/update; manage_site/set_chrome for the whole site), a check of each page (manage_page/preview and manage_page/score), publishing each page (manage_page/publish), and the home page (manage_site/set_home).

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The whole site as it stands: what visitors see at the root of its address (a website page, a funnel page, the store, the blog or the join page) and how to change it, every page at its public address (/about; the home page at the root), how its header and footer are laid out and styled, the footer's social links in order, and how many popups, collections, custom code boxes and restore points it has. Start here.
- create_page: A new draft page on the coach's own website, added to the end of the menu (it shows there once published): empty, or filled in from a website page template (`pageTemplate`, a key from manage_site/page_templates).
- duplicate_page: Copy one website page, sections, look and settings, as a new draft at a new address, added to the end of the menu.
- set_home: Make a website page what visitors see at the root of the community's address, in place of whatever holds it now (another page, a funnel page, the store or the blog, each kept at its own address). Public at once for a published page.
- page_templates: The ready-made single website pages (About, Services, Contact, Team, Pricing, FAQ, Testimonials, Work with me, Start here, Class schedule, Free resource, Speaking, Press & media kit, Portfolio, Podcast, Retreat), each with its key, its suggested address and the sections it lays down; with `pageTemplate`, that page's full sections built for this community, to lay over an existing page with manage_page/update.
- templates: The website templates this community can start from: the designed ones first, then the starters, each with its key, the pages it makes, its look (palette, fonts, corners, buttons, header and footer) and its style (calm, bold, editorial or playful).
- apply_template: Lay a whole site down in one go from a template key (manage_site/templates): its new pages are drafts added to the end of the menu, but unless keepMyColours keeps the website's own look (kept by default once the website has pages), the template's look goes on every existing page, LIVE ones included, and on the header and footer at once, after a restore point manage_site/restore puts back. Its home page takes the root only when nothing holds it; the answer says when it did not, and manage_site/set_home moves it.
- set_menu: The site's navigation. Do this after the pages exist.
- set_footer: The links in the site's footer, each optionally under a column heading the columns footer groups them by (its tagline, social icons, layout and signup are manage_site/set_chrome's).
- set_chrome: The header (its layout: classic, transparent over the first section or centered; its style: standard, glass, pill or hideOnScroll, the last three always pinned; its button, announcement bar and stickiness), the footer's layout (simple or columns), its email signup (one of the community's forms), tagline and social icons (one ordered list of profile links, each shown as its platform's icon), and the website's search and sharing defaults: the description and social image (a stock photo) a page without its own uses, and whether the site belongs to a person or a business.
- redirects: Every old address the community sends on (a previous website's /about, /services-1) and the page each goes to.
- add_redirects: Send a previous website's addresses on to their new pages, up to 100 at a time, LIVE at once, so old links and the search ranking follow (a permanent 308). Each refused one says why.
- remove_redirects: Stop redirecting old addresses. Works on every plan.
- history: The website's restore points (the whole site at a moment: every website page plus the menu, header and footer; taken on a first publish, before a template, a restore or a delete, and on demand) and its menu, header and footer changes, newest first; with a restorePointId, the pages it holds and what restoring it (or one pageId of it) would change; with a frameVersionId, what undoing that change would put back.
- restore: Put the whole site back to a restorePointId (pages, menu, header and footer; a page deleted since comes back as a draft, a page made since is left alone), or one pageId of it, or undo one menu, header and footer change by frameVersionId. Never moves an address, the homepage or what is published, and saves the site as it is now first, so it can be undone.
- save_restore_point: Keep the whole website as it is now as a restore point, with an optional name. Changes nothing on the site.
- languages: The website's main language, the languages it adds (each with its address word, like /fr, and the coach's menu and footer words in it), and every website page's translation in each: its pageId, address (/fr/about), draft or published, and out of date when its main page was saved after it.
- set_languages: Set the main language, add languages (up to five beside it) or remove them (their pages are kept, off the site until the language is added again), and a language's words for the menu and footer labels.
- translate_page: Make a website page's version in an added language: a DRAFT copy of its sections to rewrite in that language with manage_page/update or manage_page/edit_section, then publish with manage_page/publish. It lives at the main page's address under the language (/fr/about).
- code: The website's custom code in full: the head, start-of-page and end-of-page boxes (each with its code, on or off, the pages it runs on and whether it waits for cookie consent), each page's own head code, the Google Tag Manager id, the custom section stylesheet and script every custom code section carries first, the versions it can go back to, and whether the community's ad tracking is connected.
- set_code: Put code on the website that RUNS ON EVERY PAGE (or chosen pages) and is live at once: any of the three boxes, a page's own head code, the Google Tag Manager id, the custom section stylesheet and script (`blockCss`, `blockJs`: written once, put into every custom code section ahead of its own code, so shared fonts and base styles are never repeated per section), or an earlier version back (`restoreVersionId`). Owner or admin only; every save is kept and the answer names the version that undoes it.
- look: The look the whole website wears (its colours, fonts, label font, corners and buttons) and every choice manage_site/set_look takes: the certified palettes, the tested font pairs, the label font, the corner and button steps.
- set_look: Change the whole website's look at once, on every page: a certified palette (or one brand colour built into one, refused when too pale to read), a tested font pair, a label font (eyebrows, buttons and the header navigation: any Google family, null takes it off), corners and buttons. Send only what changes: what is sent goes onto each page over its own look, and each one left out stays as each page has it. Saves a restore point first; on a live page it shows at once. The community's own Studio colours never change.
- restore_brand: Put the community's own Studio colours and fonts back on every website page (or the pages named), clearing what a template or a page's Design set. Words, corners and buttons are untouched; live pages show it at once.
- old_site: Moving from another site: read the old site's sitemap and match each old address to one of this website's pages (sure, a best guess to confirm, or none). Writes nothing.
- move_site: Save old addresses as redirects, each to a page named by its pageId, LIVE at once, so links to the old site keep working. Each refused pair is named.
- popups: Every popup, drafts included: its popupId, whether it is live, when it opens (only from a button, or by itself after a delay, a scroll or as the pointer leaves, on which pages and screens, and how often per visitor), which pages have a button to it, its last 30 days (shown, closed, clicked through, signed up), and its settings and section as JSON.
- save_popup: Make a popup (a draft, holding one freeform, form or offer section) or change one, only what is sent changing; on a live popup the change is seen at once. A website page's button opens it with the destination {"kind":"popup","popupId":"<id>"}.
- set_popup_live: Put a popup in front of visitors at once (live true: by itself as its settings say, and from every button that names it), or take it down (live false, on every plan).
- delete_popup: Delete a popup that was never live and that no live page's button opens. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

title.description: What the page is called in the console and, by default, in the menu. From a page template, its name is the usual choice.

slug.description: Its address: once published, the page answers at /<slug> on the community's own address ("about" is /about). 2 to 48 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Not a word the community already uses (/join, /library, /store and the like), nor the bio link's or the blog's own word. The two exceptions are terms and privacy: a PUBLIC website page published at /terms or /privacy replaces the community's own legal page at that address on the site, so a migrated site keeps its legal URLs. A missing address shows a not-found page in the site's own look, header and footer; there is nothing to build for it.

pageTemplate.description: Start the page from this website page template (manage_site/page_templates): a built-in key, or a designed one's lib- key. Omit for an empty page.

pageId.description: The website page to copy, from manage_site/read.

template.description: Which template to apply: a key from manage_site/templates.

keepMyColours.description: true keeps the website's own colours, fonts, buttons, header and footer; false brings the template's look to the whole website. Left out: false for a website with no pages yet, true for one that has some.

pageId.description: A site page's id, from manage_site/read or manage_page/read.

href.description: An https:// URL, or a path on the coach's own site starting with "/" ("/contact"). Nothing else is stored.

pageId.description: A site page's id, from manage_site/read or manage_page/read.

href.description: An https:// URL, or a path on the coach's own site starting with "/" ("/contact"). Nothing else is stored.

items.description: The dropdown's children. Pages or links, never another menu.

menu.description: The whole menu, left to right. At most 12 entries. Send [] to show no menu.

href.description: An https:// URL or a "/" path on the coach's own site.

group.description: The column heading this link sits under when the footer is "columns" (manage_site/set_chrome footerLayout), like "Help". Left out or "" = the "Links" column. The simple footer shows every link in one row.

links.description: The whole footer row, in order. At most 8. Send [] to clear it.

sticky.description: Keep the header pinned while the visitor scrolls. It changes nothing while headerStyle is glass, pill or hideOnScroll, which pin the header themselves.

buttonLabel.description: The header button's words. Send "" for the default, "Join".

buttonHref.description: Where the header button goes: an https:// URL or a "/" path. Send "" to send it to the community's own join/checkout flow.

announcement.description: The slim banner above the header, shown on every published website page. Send "" to remove it.

announcementHref.description: Where the banner links. Send "" to leave it as plain text.

announcementTone.description: How the banner looks: accent, soft or ink.

footerTagline.description: One line under the wordmark in the footer. Send "" to remove it.

socials.description: The footer's social icons, as ONE ordered list of profile links that REPLACES the whole row (send every link you want kept, in the order to show them; [] removes them all). Each link becomes its platform's icon from its address alone: Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, Pinterest, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Substack, Bluesky (X takes twitter.com too), and a globe for any other website. A link without https:// gets it; a bare "@handle" is refused (it names no platform). manage_site/read lists the row as it stands.

seoDescription.description: What search results and shared links say for a website page that has no description of its own. Send "" to clear it.

socialImage.description: The picture a shared link shows for a website page with none of its own: a stock photo's key from manage_page/stock_photos. Send "" for none (a card made from each page). The coach's own photo is chosen in the console.

siteEntity.description: Who the website belongs to: "person" (a coach under their own name) or "organization" (a studio, a brand). It is what search engines are told.

headerLayout.description: How the header is laid out: classic (the default, logo left, menu right), transparent (over each page's first section in a colour that reads on it, turning solid as the visitor scrolls; it stays solid where the first section gives it nothing certain to read on; it takes no style, so the header's style goes back to standard) or centered (logo in the middle).

headerStyle.description: How the header looks and behaves as the visitor scrolls, for the classic and centered layouts: standard (the default, a solid bar, pinned only when sticky is true), glass (a frosted, see-through bar pinned at the top that blurs the page behind it; its words are checked to read over anything, and it turns solid where they would not), pill (a rounded bar floating just below the top edge, pinned) or hideOnScroll (slides away while the visitor scrolls down, back as they scroll up; it stays put for visitors who ask for reduced motion). Glass, pill and hideOnScroll are always pinned. The transparent layout has its own behaviour and takes no style: a style other than standard on a transparent header takes it back to the layout it was laid over (classic unless it was centered), and sending one with headerLayout transparent is refused.

footerLayout.description: How the footer is laid out: simple (the default, centred, one row of links) or columns (the brand, the menu, each footer link group from manage_site/set_footer and an optional signup form, side by side).

footerFormId.description: The columns footer's email signup: the id of one of this community's forms (manage_form/list), shown once it is published. Send "" for none.

to.description: Where it goes now: "/p/about", "/", or an https:// address.

redirects.description: The redirects to add, one per old address.

fromPaths.description: The old addresses to stop redirecting, like "/about".

restorePointId.description: A restore point from this list, to read what it holds and what restoring it would change.

frameVersionId.description: A menu, header and footer change from this list, to read what undoing it would put back.

name.description: A name for it ("Before the spring redesign"), at most 80 characters.

mainLanguage.description: The site's main language, a code like en or fr. Its pages keep their addresses.

removeLanguages.description: Codes of added languages to remove (their pages are kept, hidden).

words.description: The coach's words for the menu and footer labels in each language. manage_site/languages lists the labels.
A menu or footer label as written in the main language, mapped to its words in this language. An empty value clears it.

language.description: An added language's code, like fr.

head.description: In the head: meta tags go in the page's head; scripts and styles load first.

code.description: The code, as the service gives it (HTML: <script>, <style>, <meta>, <noscript>...). At most 16,000 characters. "" empties the box.

enabled.description: Off keeps the code and runs nothing.

pages.description: "all" for every website page, or a list of website pageIds (from manage_site/code) to run on only those.

consent.description: true: added only once a visitor's cookie choice allows advertising and analytics tags.

bodyStart.description: At the start of the page, before its first section.

code.description: The code, as the service gives it (HTML: <script>, <style>, <meta>, <noscript>...). At most 16,000 characters. "" empties the box.

enabled.description: Off keeps the code and runs nothing.

pages.description: "all" for every website page, or a list of website pageIds (from manage_site/code) to run on only those.

consent.description: true: added only once a visitor's cookie choice allows advertising and analytics tags.

bodyEnd.description: At the end of the page, after everything on it.

code.description: The code, as the service gives it (HTML: <script>, <style>, <meta>, <noscript>...). At most 16,000 characters. "" empties the box.

enabled.description: Off keeps the code and runs nothing.

pages.description: "all" for every website page, or a list of website pageIds (from manage_site/code) to run on only those.

consent.description: true: added only once a visitor's cookie choice allows advertising and analytics tags.

pageHead.description: A website pageId mapped to that page's own head code (at most 4,000 characters); "" removes it.

gtm.description: A Google Tag Manager container id (GTM-ABC1234), or "" for none. It loads after cookie consent.

blockCss.description: CSS put into every custom code section on the website, before each section's own CSS. At most 20,000 characters. "" clears it; left out keeps it.

blockJs.description: JavaScript (no <script> tag) run in every custom code section on the website, before each section's own script. At most 20,000 characters. "" clears it; left out keeps it.

restoreVersionId.description: A version id from manage_site/code to put back whole. Send it alone.

palette.description: A palette key from manage_site/look. Left out keeps the colours.

brandColour.description: Instead of a palette: one colour, #rrggbb, built into a readable palette (refused when too pale to read).

fonts.description: A font pair key from manage_site/look. Left out keeps the fonts.

labelFont.description: The font of every page's eyebrows, buttons and header navigation: a Google Fonts family by its name (a mono suits it, e.g. "IBM Plex Mono"). null takes it off, so each keeps the face it was designed in. Left out keeps each page's.

corners.description: sharp, soft or round. Left out keeps the corners.

buttons.description: filled or outline. Left out keeps the buttons.

pageIds.description: The website pages to change, from manage_site/read. Left out: every website page.

popupId.description: The popup to change; leave out to make a new one.

section.description: The one section, required for a new popup: type freeform, form, offer, its id (send the popup's own back; one is made for a new popup) and its fields as manage_page/read prints them.

size.description: md (the default), sm, lg, or full (the whole screen).

placement.description: center (the default), bottom (a bar along the bottom) or corner (a card in the bottom corner).

backdrop.description: What covers the page behind it: dim (the default), blur or none (a corner or bottom card over no backdrop leaves the page usable).

closeOnBackdrop.description: Whether a click on the page around it closes it (true by default).

trigger.description: What opens it by itself. Any button whose destination is this popup opens it too, whatever is set here.

auto.description: none (only a button that links to it opens it), delay, scroll, or exit (the pointer leaving the page; on a computer only, never on phones).

delaySecs.description: delay only: seconds after the page loads (3 to 120).

scrollPercent.description: scroll only: how far down the page, in percent (10 to 90).

pages.description: Which website pages it opens by itself on: "all", or a list of website pageIds (from manage_site/read).

devices.description: Which screens it opens by itself on: all (the default), desktop or phone.

every.description: How often one visitor meets it by itself: week (the default), day, month, once or always.

stopAfterConvert.description: Never again once the visitor signs up through it (true by default).

window.description: When it may open by itself; null clears it.

from.description: An ISO date and time it may start opening from.

until.description: An ISO date and time it stops opening at.

live.description: true to put it live, false to take it down.

tools.name: manage_collection
tools.title: Read and build the website's collections
tools.description:
The coach's website collections: lists of like things they keep, such as their portfolio, team, testimonials, press, case studies or services. Each has fields (text, rich text, image, link, date, number, tags, yes or no, or a relation linking the community's own classes, courses or products) and items, each a draft or live. A collection is shown on a page by a collection section (manage_page), and when it has pages, at /<word> and /<word>/<item>. Building collections: Available on the Creator plan. Reading them, unpublishing an item and deleting a draft work on every plan.

Set `act` to one of:
- list: Every collection, each with its collectionId, preset, card style, address, preview address and how many items are live. Start here.
- read: One collection in full: its fields, its settings, its item page (built-in, or the designed layout as JSON with what each element is filled from) and every item in order, drafts included, with each item's itemId, address, preview address and values as JSON. Read before every edit.
- presets: The ready-made collections create starts from (portfolio, team, testimonials, press, caseStudies, services, custom), each with its fields, card style, word and whether items get pages.
- create: A new, empty collection from a preset, its name, address word, fields, card style, item pages and intro the preset's unless sent.
- update: Change a collection's name, address word, card style, intro, whether items get pages, or its whole field list (a field left out drops its values from every item). Live at once.
- set_item_layout: Design the page every item of a collection gets: freeform sections whose text, image and button elements may each be filled from the item's title or one of its fields (a bind), hidden on an item where that field is empty; live at once on every item's page. null puts the built-in item page back.
- add_item: Add 1 to 50 items with a title and values each, as drafts unless publish is true (then live at once).
- edit_item: Change one item's title, address or values; only the value keys sent change. Live at once on a published item.
- reorder_items: Put every item of a collection in a new order.
- publish_item: Put one item live on the website at once, with its own page when the collection has pages.
- unpublish_item: Make one item a draft again, off the website at once. Works on every plan.
- duplicate_item: Copy one item, values and all, as a new draft right after it.
- delete_item: Delete one item that has never been live. Cannot be undone.
- delete: Delete a collection none of whose items has ever been live. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

name.description: Its name, like Our work. The preset's label by default.

word.description: Its address word, like work for /work: 2 to 48 lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens.

fields.description: Fields in place of the preset's, in order.

key.description: The key item values are stored under: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, numbers and underscores (title and slug are taken).

label.description: What the console calls the field.

kind.description: text, richText, image, link, date, number, tags, toggle, or relation (links the item to the community's own classes and events, courses or products, drawn live on its page).

target.description: A relation field only, and required there: what it links, events, courses or products.

itemPages.description: Whether each item gets its own page and the collection a page listing them.

intro.description: The line under the title on the collection's own page.

sections.description: Freeform sections, as the layout manage_collection/read prints.

layout.description: The item page's layout, or null for the built-in item page.

slug.description: The item's address after /<word>/: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

tools.name: manage_studio
tools.title: Read and set the community's branding
tools.description:
How the member surface looks and reads: the wordmark, the colours, the page copy, the welcome flow, the home rails, the paywall, and which automatic emails members get and what they say.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: The whole theme as it stands, including what the automatic member emails say and the email footer's address and social links. Read before every edit.
- brand_look: Wordmark, colours and typography.
- read_website_brand: Read only: give it the coach's own website address and it reads that site's public HTML and CSS (running none of its scripts) and suggests a matching wordmark, background, text and accent colour as hex, and headline and body fonts matched to the curated menu, saying whether each is the same font or the nearest; plus any logo images it found, as addresses. Writes nothing: apply with manage_studio/brand_look.
- button_style: The community-wide default look for buttons: on the member home and join page, or on the funnel pages.
- page_copy: The words on the member home, library and community pages.
- member_onboarding: The welcome message (markdown-lite) and the profile questions a new member answers.
- member_emails: Switch the automatic member emails on or off: the new-content email, the welcome email, and session reminders (the reminders before a session and the gone-live email; invites, reschedules, cancellations, RSVP confirmations, tickets and booked sessions send either way). Also their wording: the subject and opening paragraph of the new-content and welcome emails, the receipt note, and the postal address in the footer of every email built in the email builder, and of new-content emails, digests and emailed posts. And the email signature of the coach: its words, where its saved pictures sit and how big, and whether it also signs the automatic emails (owner or admin only; a new picture is drawn, typed or uploaded in the console). Not the footer's social links (manage_marketing_org/assets).
- add_home_section: A new rail or block on the member home page, including an embedded page hosted elsewhere.
- update_home_section: Edit a home rail or message block (a coach's message can be signed by the owner and/or admins, and its body is markdown-lite; a Latest posts block takes which posts, how many and how they are laid out; an embedded page takes its address and height), restyle its button, or move it up the page.
- add_paywall_section: A new block on the join page. Staff only.
- update_paywall_section: Edit a join-page block, or restyle its button. Staff only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

wordmark.description: The community's name as members see it in the navigation, on the sign-in page and in the From line of its email. "" falls back to the community name.

background.description: Page canvas, e.g. #fbfaf6. Also moves an automatic card or soft fill with it, and one still holding the old default white or lavender that was never picked.

accent.description: The single brand colour: buttons, links, highlights.

card.description: The background of boxes and panels. "" makes it follow the background automatically (a raised shade of it), which is how a new community starts.

muted.description: Subtle fills for quieter areas. "" makes it follow the background automatically.

accentForeground.description: Text ON the accent colour. "" lets it be picked automatically by contrast, which is usually right.

profileHeader.description: The band behind a member profile photo. "" keeps the per-member colour gradient.

displayFont.description: Headline font. One of: Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Cormorant Garamond, Spectral, Bricolage Grotesque, Space Grotesk, Montserrat, Lato, System Sans, Libre Caslon Text, Young Serif, EB Garamond, Dancing Script, Marcellus, IBM Plex Serif, Bitter, Alegreya, Vollkorn, Petrona, Averia Serif Libre, Bodoni Moda, Italiana, Cinzel, Literata, Newsreader, Zilla Slab, Crimson Pro, Libre Bodoni, Besley, Gloock, Anton, Archivo Black, Sora, Space Mono, Fragment Mono, Oswald, Familjen Grotesk, Rubik, Gabarito, Unbounded, Schibsted Grotesk, Syne, Outfit, Jost, Red Hat Display, Albert Sans, Barlow, Figtree, Alegreya Sans.

bodyFont.description: Body font. One of: Hanken Grotesk, Inter, Work Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Nunito Sans, Lora, IBM Plex Sans, Montserrat, Lato, System Sans, Karla, Public Sans, Manrope, Mulish, Epilogue, Chivo, Assistant, Cabin, Raleway, Source Sans 3, Red Hat Text, Archivo, Barlow, Jost, Figtree, Albert Sans, Alegreya Sans, Schibsted Grotesk, Familjen Grotesk, Rubik, Outfit, Syne, EB Garamond, Literata, Newsreader, Crimson Pro, Vollkorn, Alegreya, Petrona, Averia Serif Libre, IBM Plex Serif, Libre Caslon Text, Spectral, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, Fragment Mono, Georgia, Palatino, System Mono.

url.description: The website's address, as a person would type it (https:// is added when missing).

surface.description: Which default to set: "home" (the member home and the join page, the default when omitted) or "funnels" (the funnel pages). The read prints both.

libraryHeadline.description: Heading on the courses page. "" falls back to the tab name.

communityHeadline.description: Heading on the community feed. "" falls back to the tab name.

notFoundHeadline.description: What a member sees when a link goes nowhere.

homeHeroHeadline.description: The greeting at the top of the Home tab. IGNORED once the home has its own arranged layout: edit the hero section instead.

homeCommunityCardTitle.description: The card on Home that links into the community feed.

welcomeMessage.description: The message under the welcome headline. Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

profileSubtext.description: The line under the profile headline. Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

doneMessage.description: The message on the you-are-in screen. Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.

enterCtaLabel.description: The button that drops them into the community.

questions.description: Only the questions you list are changed. Username and a photo are always asked and are not in this list.

shown.description: Ask it during the welcome flow.

required.description: Make an answer mandatory. Never allowed on a sensitive question. Defaults to leaving it as it is.

newContentEmail.description: Email members about newly published content.

welcomeEmail.description: Email a new member the moment they join.

sessionReminders.description: Remind members and invitees before a session, and email them when it goes live. Not plan-gated.

newContentSubject.description: The new-content email's subject, always. Empty builds one from what was published, like "New lesson: Morning Mobility Flow".

newContentIntro.description: The paragraph that opens the new-content email.

welcomeIntro.description: The paragraph that opens the welcome email.

receiptNote.description: A short thank-you above the details on the receipt a member gets after paying for a membership. {membership} is replaced by the level they bought (nothing, on a community with one membership) and {community} by the community's name.

footerAddress.description: The postal address in the footer of every email built in the email builder, and of new-content emails, digests and emailed posts, which anti-spam law (CAN-SPAM) requires to be a real address the coach receives mail at: a business address or a PO box both work. "" shows Drry's instead, marked "Sent via Drry". One line.

signature.description: The whole email signature, replacing the stored one. Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone. A PICTURE is a line of its own: ![what it shows](picture:a), optionally followed by {small} or {large} (medium otherwise). Only the slots manage_studio/read lists as saved can be placed, at most 2, and at most 400 characters of words. Send the stored value back edited to keep its pictures. "" takes the signature off.

signAutomaticEmails.description: Also put the signature on the automatic emails: new content, welcome, trial, cancellation, session emails, every receipt (membership, product, payment link, instalment, refund) and the copy of a signed agreement. Never reply notifications, failed-payment notices or sign-in codes.

type.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

position.description: Where in the order, counting from 0. Default: last.

body.description: The body copy. On a coachMessage or richText section it is markdown-lite (Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone.). On every other section it is plain text with line breaks kept, so do not write markdown marks into it.

buttons.description: How this section's button looks: shape, size, label size, label casing, fill and lift. Every axis also takes "auto", which inherits the community-wide default, which manage_studio/read prints under BUTTONS and manage_studio/button_style sets. A ctaBanner sets its fill through `ctaStyle` instead, and `fill` sent here is REFUSED on that type rather than stored, because the console shows only the one control there.

ctaStyle.description: The fill of a ctaBanner's button. Only that section type has it; every other section sets its fill through `buttons`.

variant.description: The section's layout style. Read the current one with manage_studio/read; a value the section does not offer is refused rather than ignored.

items.description: REPLACES the whole list on a list section. Send every row you want kept, in order.

hidden.description: Hide the section without deleting it. The reversible way to take something off the page; there is no delete here.

href.description: Where a button goes: a path inside the community like /library, or a full https:// URL. Anything else is refused.

limit.description: How many items a teaser rail shows.

showAuthor.description: Show who a coach's message is from (a photo and name) beside it, or who each post is by on a Latest posts section. false shows no byline.

mode.description: A Latest posts section's posts: latest (the newest), category (with categoryId), author (with authorId) or picked (postIds, in order). Only published posts show; a members-only post shows with a lock.

layout.description: A Latest posts section's layout: grid, list, carousel or featured.

count.description: How many posts a Latest posts section shows (not a picked one).

categoryId.description: A Latest posts section's category, by the categoryId manage_blog/read prints. "" clears it.

authorId.description: A Latest posts section's author, by the authorRef manage_blog/read prints. "" clears it.

postIds.description: A picked Latest posts section's posts, in order, by postId. REPLACES the list.

showCover.description: A Latest posts section's cover photos.

showExcerpt.description: A Latest posts section's card lines.

viewAll.description: A Latest posts section's View all button.

viewAllLabel.description: The View all button's words. "" means "View all posts".

height.description: How tall an embedded page's frame is, px (an embed section only).

authorIds.description: Who a coach's message is signed by: user ids of the community's owner or admins, in the order their names should read, up to 4. The ids and names are listed by manage_studio/read under the home sections. REPLACES the list; send an empty list to go back to the community owner, which is also what an unset list means. Anybody who is not an owner or admin here is refused. Only a coach's message takes it.

note.description: The reassurance line under the button, e.g. "Cancel anytime".

showLogo.description: Show the community logo at the top of the page.

tools.name: manage_settings
tools.title: Community settings, and see storage use and the sending domain
tools.description:
The switches a coach sets once: what the tabs are called, which surfaces members see, and the rules for discussions, events and messages. Also reads storage use against the plan and what extra storage costs, which only the owner can switch on, in the console, and whether email goes out from the community's own domain.

Set `act` to one of:
- labels: Rename the community feed and courses tabs, switch the audio and events surfaces on or off, switch the Resources tab on or off and rename it, AND show or hide the blog's tab in the member menu and rename the blog (blogInMemberMenu, blogLabel: owner or admin only). The other tabs and switches are console only. LIVE immediately; keep the previous values it returns.
- community: The community's name, its timezone, the country it is based in (which decides whether its forms, checkouts, bookings, event sign-ups, free downloads and join pages ask visitors about email updates, as they do in the EU/EEA, the UK and Canada, and which country-limited background collections its bio link offers), and which alerts the coach is emailed. No description: that belongs to a discussion category. The surface toggles live on manage_settings/labels. Staff only.
- discussion: The community feed's attachment rules and AI moderation (live chat's are manage_settings/events). Staff only.
- discussion_category: Add, rename or reorder a discussion category. Staff only.
- events_read: Read only: the calendar's standing defaults and what live chat allows: the standing meeting link, what an instant meeting starts with, whether chat carries pictures, files and link cards, whether a webinar attendee's link is held, and whether chat is screened. Staff only.
- events: The calendar's standing defaults and live-chat rules: a default join link, instant-meeting recording/notes/chat, whether live chat carries pictures, files and link cards, whether a webinar attendee's link is held for a host, and whether live chat is screened by AI (screening is Growth). To show or rename the tab use manage_settings/labels. Staff only.
- messages: Direct-message rules: photos and files, the membership needed, whether members may message each other or only the hosts, and AI screening (screening is owner only).
- domains: Read only: every domain Drry holds or is moving in for the community's owner, with its status, who pays (free with the plan, free from Drry, or a paid yearly add-on and its price), when it renews or that it won't, whether this community's website is on it, and how far a move in has got. DNS records, the website's address, name search and moving in are manage_domain; buying, renewal and moving out stay in the console. Staff only.
- sending_domain: Read only: whether email goes out from the community's own domain, its sender address, whether it is verified, pending or lapsed (falling back to Drry's senders), whether its DMARC record is in place, and whether the plan includes it. Connecting or removing one stays in the console. Staff only.
- storage: Read only: storage used against what the plan includes and how much is over, whether extra storage can be bought and is on sale this period (and from when), whether extra usage is on and its spend cap, what storage has cost this period (charged on the period's peak, the most held past the plan at any point), and how much of the shared cap live video, email and storage take. Staff only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

communityLabel.description: What the community feed tab is called, e.g. "The Lounge".

coursesLabel.description: What the courses tab is called, e.g. "Programs".

audioEnabled.description: Whether the audio surface is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages opening; nothing is deleted.

eventsEnabled.description: Whether the events surface is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages opening; nothing is deleted.

resourcesEnabled.description: Whether the Resources tab (member files) is shown to members. False hides its tab and stops its pages and downloads opening; nothing is deleted.

resourcesLabel.description: What the Resources tab is called, e.g. "Downloads".

blogInMemberMenu.description: Whether members get a Blog tab in their menu while the blog is on. It opens the blog itself. False takes the tab out; the blog and its posts stay public.

blogLabel.description: The blog's name, on its tab, its pages and its emails, e.g. "Journal". Empty goes back to "Blog".

name.description: Shape depends on `act`; the act that uses it validates it.

timezone.description: The community's clock, as an IANA zone name like Europe/London or America/Los_Angeles, never a display name like "Pacific Standard Time". Anything scheduled on a wall clock reads it.

country.description: Where the community is based, as a two-letter ISO country code like US, GB or CA; null clears it. It decides TWO things. First, MARKETING CONSENT: a community based in the EU, the EEA, the UK or Canada asks visitors whether they want email updates before their address joins the list (a box on its checkouts, bookings, event sign-ups, free downloads and join pages, and on every form whose Marketing consent step is on; its Instagram auto-DM email step cannot ask, so someone new it saves lands Not opted in); anywhere else, or with no country, nobody is asked. Changing it turns that on or off on every page at once, and a change that stops the asking pauses every live Instagram auto-reply with an email step (its consent line is sent from then on, so it must go live again to be checked), so confirm with the coach first. Second, which country-limited background collections the bio link Library offers. It is not the Stripe account's country and changes no price or currency.

newMemberEmail.description: Email the coach when somebody joins or pays to join.

memberLeftEmail.description: Email the coach when a paying member cancels.

productSaleEmail.description: Email the coach when somebody buys a digital product.

weeklyPulseEmail.description: The Monday-morning summary of what changed in this community.

drryNewsEmail.description: Drry's own product news and feature announcements.

allowImages.description: May members attach pictures to a post. Pictures use storage.

allowFiles.description: May members attach files to a post. Files use storage.

maxAttachmentsPerPost.description: How many attachments one post may carry, 1 to 10.

polls.description: May a post carry a poll.

reactions.description: Does a post show the reaction bar beyond a plain like.

screenPosts.description: Screen posts with AI before they go live. ON means a post that looks like a violation is HELD out of the feed until the coach approves it. OFF means nothing is held.

screenStrictness.description: How cautious the screen is. relaxed holds only clear violations, strict holds borderline posts too.

screenGuidance.description: What this community is about, in the coach's own words, so the screen can tell an off-topic post from an on-topic one. Plain text; it is read as context, never as instructions.

screenFor.description: The complete list of categories to screen for: HA (Hate and harassment), ME (Mean-spirited), SX (Sexual content), VI (Threats and violence), SH (Self-harm crisis), MI (Dangerous misinformation), SP (Spam and self-promotion), OT (Off-topic). Anything not listed is NOT screened for, so send the whole set, not just the change. Omit to leave the current set alone.

categoryId.description: The category to edit. Omit to create a new one, which returns its id. No read tool lists a community's existing categories yet, so if you do not already have the id, say so rather than guessing one.

description.description: One line saying what belongs in here. Empty clears it.

hue.description: The colour of its chip, as a hue angle 0-360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue). Defaults to 18 on a new category.

position.description: Where it sits in the list, zero-based, 0 being first. The other rooms shuffle around it; nothing else about them changes.

defaultJoinUrl.description: The coach's standing meeting link (a Zoom personal room, a standing Google Meet), prefilled into every new event. A booking type with no link of its own ALSO falls back to this one, so members really are sent here. http:// or https:// only. Empty string clears it.

instantMeetingRecording.description: Whether an instant meeting starts recording. Recordings use the community's storage.

instantMeetingNotes.description: Whether an instant meeting transcribes and writes a recap. Inert below Growth.

instantMeetingChat.description: Whether an instant meeting opens with live chat on.

chatImages.description: May a live-chat message carry a picture at all.

chatFiles.description: May a live-chat message carry a file (PDF, Office document, CSV or text) at all. A file is always a download. In a webinar only a host may share one either way.

chatLinkPreviews.description: Does a link in live chat render a preview card.

chatHoldLinks.description: Hold a guest's link in a webinar until a host releases it.

screenChat.description: Screen live-chat messages with AI before the room sees them. Independent of the community feed's screen: neither inherits from the other.

screenChatGuidance.description: Community context for the chat screen. Plain text.

screenChatFor.description: The complete list of categories the chat screen enforces: HA (Hate and harassment), ME (Mean-spirited), SX (Sexual content), VI (Threats and violence), SH (Self-harm crisis), MI (Dangerous misinformation), SP (Spam and self-promotion), OT (Off-topic). Anything not listed is not screened for.

minTierId.description: The membership tier needed to reach out, from list_catalog/membership_tiers. Pass null to open messaging to everyone. Omit to leave the current rule alone. Blocking, reporting, leaving and clearing a conversation are never gated.

lockedTabIsVisible.description: When a tier is required, whether members below it still SEE the tab locked (true, the default) or it disappears entirely (false).

screenMessages.description: Point an AI screen at direct messages. Owner only, Growth only. It never holds, edits or blocks a message.

hostsOnly.description: true = members may message the owner and admins but not each other; conversations between members become read-only, and a group stays open while a host is in it. false = members may message each other again, which reopens those conversations. The hosts can always message anyone.

tools.name: manage_domain
tools.title: Read and change domain names, DNS records, the website's address and moving a domain in
tools.description:
The domains Drry holds for a coach, done for them: check a name and what it would cost them, read and add DNS records, point the website at one of their domains, and walk a domain they own elsewhere through moving in. Changing or removing a live record, buying, renewal, moving a domain out and the transfer code are confirmed by the owner in the console, through the links these answers give. The list of domains is manage_settings/domains.

Set `act` to one of:
- search: Read only: whether a .com is free, ideas when it is not, and what the owner's next domain costs them bought new or moved in (free with the plan, free from Drry, or a paid yearly add-on). Buying is in the console; the answer links there. Owner only.
- dns: Read only: every DNS record on one of the owner's domains, the coach's own with their recordId and Drry's locked, and whether they can change now. Staff only.
- add_record: Add an MX, TXT or CNAME record, after the console's own checks (Drry's names and clashes refused). Live at once: show the coach the record first. Owner only.
- change_record: Changes nothing: checks an edit to, or the removal of, one of the coach's records and answers with a console link that opens it highlighted with the change filled in, for the coach to save. Owner only.
- connect_website: Point the community's website at a host on a domain Drry holds (yourname.com, www or a subdomain); Drry writes its records. Moving it off an address it already has needs replaceCurrent, after the coach agrees. Owner only, Creator and up.
- move_in_start: Start moving in a .com the coach owns elsewhere: claim it, make its zone and copy its records, at the price manage_domain/search quoted. Nothing is charged here. Owner only.
- move_in: Read only: the step a move in is at, the nameservers to set when that is the step, and the console link for the transfer code. Staff only.
- move_in_confirm_records: The copied records look right: on to the nameservers step, answered with the two nameservers to set. Owner only.
- move_in_check: Ask whether the nameservers have switched; once they have, the answer links to the transfer-code step in the console. Owner only.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

query.description: A name to check, like rootedwellness.com. Omit for ideas.

domain.description: A domain like yourname.com. For manage_domain/dns, manage_domain/add_record and manage_domain/change_record: one of the owner's domains from manage_settings/domains, omitted for the community's current one. For the move-in acts: the .com moving in, always required.

name.description: The host, relative to the domain: @ for the domain itself, or a name like mail2 or _dmarc. A full name under the domain is accepted too.

content.description: The value: the text for a TXT, the target host for a CNAME or MX.

priority.description: MX only: 0 to 65535, lower is preferred. Defaults to 10.

change.description: edit: change the record. delete: remove it.

replaceCurrent.description: True once the coach agreed to move the website off the address it has now.

expectedKind.description: The price quoted by manage_domain/search for moving one in.

tools.name: manage_email
tools.title: Read and write broadcast emails
tools.description:
The email a coach sends to members or leads. Drafted here with every block and design option the console's editor has, sent from the console, and referenced by automations and forms.

Set `act` to one of:
- read: One email in full (every block and style option in the form the update takes, sender name, tracking, header and design, schedule and send results: opens, clicks and, staff only, what it SOLD within 7 days of a click, net of refunds), and which blog post each blog post block shows, or every email when emailId is omitted. Says whether it is LIVE.
- create: A new draft, written block by block (photos from the stock library, a blog post block showing one published post or the newest few, custom code blocks on plans with custom code) or started from a template. Sends to nobody until a person presses send.
- update: Edit a draft: name, subject, preview, blocks (a photo may be a stock photo; a blog post block shows one published post or the newest few; a custom code block is written in full on plans with custom code), sender name, tracking, header and design. The coach's own uploads are carried, never chosen. A name alone may change on any email. Editing a LIVE one changes what automations and forms send from now on.
- templates: Read only: the template gallery, with the key a new draft or a template swap takes, and the fifteen stock photos the templates are made with.
- stock_photos: Read only: every stock photo a photo in an email body may use, the fifteen the templates are made with and the stock library's photos this community may pick now, each with its key, shape, mood, the kinds of coach it suits, whether it shows people, its search words and what it shows; narrowed by query, niche and shape, at most limit of them.
- apply_template: Replace a draft's blocks, subject, preview and design with a template's. Refused where it would delete uploaded photos or files; a custom block it replaces is removed and named.
- saved_blocks: Read only: the coach's saved blocks and saved emails, with the id a savedBlock body item takes.
- unschedule: Take a scheduled email back to a draft so it does not go out.
- test_send: Send a test of an email to your own account address, and nobody else. Says when a block was left out because the blog is off.
- delete: Delete a DRAFT email that was never sent or scheduled and that no automation, form, session type or product uses. Cannot be undone.

act.description: Which act to perform. See the list in the description.

emailId.description: Omit to list every email with its id.

name.description: The coach's private label for it in their list.

subject.description: The subject line. Required unless a template is named.

previewText.description: The line shown after the subject in an inbox.

color.description: This heading's own text colour. Leave out for the theme's.

body.description: Markdown-lite: **bold**, *italic*, [label](url) (a link may be bold: **[label](url)**), a line starting "- " is a bullet, a single newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph. Size words with {sm}...{/sm}, {lg}...{/lg}, {xl}...{/xl}, {2xl}...{/2xl} (relative to the surrounding text, smallest to largest). Start a paragraph with {left}, {center} or {right} to align that paragraph alone. Merge tags work in this copy and are filled in per recipient; the body parameter's description lists every one of them and the fallback syntax.

href.description: A full https:// address, a path starting with /, one of the link tags ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}), or {productLink:<id>} naming a product's id (see list_catalog/products); only a product currently FOR SALE resolves, a draft or archived one leaves the button out of the sent email with no warning at write time, or {formLink:<id>} naming a form's id (see list_catalog/forms); only a PUBLISHED form resolves, a draft one leaves the button out of the sent email with no warning at write time, ON ITS OWN. A link tag is substituted only when it is the ENTIRE value: one pasted inside a URL is either refused here or delivered to members as literal text inside a link that goes nowhere.

style.description: fill (accent), outline, ink (dark fill) or link (bare text).

shadow.description: none, raised (a soft lift, the console's Lift) or offset (a hard block, the console's Pop). A link-style button takes neither.

color.description: This button's own colour. Leave out for the brand accent.

spacing.description: The air above and below it.

color.description: The line's own colour. Leave out for the theme's.

part.description: A purchase insert, filled in per order on a product's receipt, download or refund email: delivery (the download button or a service's instructions), summary (the receipt table), refundPolicy, alsoFrom (what comes next) or refundDetails. A paid product's receipt must hold delivery and summary, a free product's download email delivery, a refund email refundDetails. An email holding one cannot be sent any other way, since there is no purchase to fill it.

options.description: The answers, 2 to 5, each a one-click link. A poll with fewer than 2 is not a question and is left out of the sent email.

endsAt.description: The deadline as an ISO-8601 instant, or "" while it is not set (the block is left out of the send).

timezone.description: The IANA timezone the deadline is written out in.

kinds.description: Which kinds it may show. Empty means all of them.

mode.description: post: one published blog post (postId). latest: the blog's newest published posts (limit). Each is drawn as its cover, title, card line and a Read more button; a members-only post shows its card line and a Members only marker, never its body. Resolved when the email sends; nothing shows while the blog is off.

postId.description: A published post's id (a uuid), from manage_blog/read. "" in latest mode.

limit.description: How many of the newest posts, 1 to 3. Latest mode.

refId.description: The id of a published course, lesson, audio track or event in this community.

ctaStyle.description: button, or link to make the whole card one link.

refId.description: The id of a published video or audio lesson in this community, drawn as a thumbnail that links to it.

refKind.description: product (a shop product), paymentLink, or checkout for the Their item card: the item each person left at checkout, filled in only on an email an automation sends when someone leaves checkout without paying.

refId.description: The id of an active shop product or payment link. Empty for checkout.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

fileKey.description: The file key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. A new one cannot be chosen here.

imageKey.description: A stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, or the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

imageKey.description: A stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, or the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

imageKey.description: The background photo: a stock:<name> key from manage_email/templates, the image key manage_email/read printed for this email, or "" for a solid band.

ctaHref.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

comp.description: The saved layout's design, as manage_email/read printed it.

fields.description: Its slots, as manage_email/read printed them: copy is written freely, a photo slot takes a stock:<name> key or a photo this email holds.

href.description: Where it links, or "" for no link. Same rules as a button link.

label.description: The block's name in the coach's editor. Members never see it.

html.description: Table-based email HTML: the fragment only, no html, head or body. Kept: table, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, div, span, p, h1 to h6, a, img, br, hr, ul, ol, li, strong, em, b, i, u, s, small, sup, sub, blockquote, center, font, pre and code, with style and the usual table attributes. Removed: scripts, style tags, iframes, svg, forms, comments, on* handlers, and a style holding url(), expression() or a comment. Editable slots are tokens: {{text:key}} for copy, {{image:key}} (the ONLY src an img may have, so every photo is a slot), {{link:key}} (or a full https:// address or mailto:) for an href, and {{color:key}}, {{size:key}} or {{align:key}} inside a style value. A text, link or image token inside a style drops that whole style attribute. A link tag ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}) is not a destination inside the html: put it in a link slot's field. Up to 24 slots; a key is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The markup is rebuilt by the sanitizer on save, so read it back.

css.description: Optional CSS for media queries and class rules, scoped to this block when sent. A <, @import, url(), expression() or an unclosed comment drops the whole stylesheet, so it is refused here.

fields.description: A value for each slot the html declares, by slot key: text is plain copy (merge tags work), image a stock:<name> key or a photo this email holds, link what a button link takes, color a hex, named colour, rgb(), hsl() or gradient, size one to four lengths such as 28px, 1.5rem or 100%, and align left, center or right.

tsx.description: Inert source an older designer left on some blocks; nothing reads or runs it. Send back what manage_email/read printed, or leave it out.

savedBlockId.description: From manage_email/saved_blocks. Arrives as the blocks it holds.

body.description: The blocks of the letter, in order. Required unless a template is named. Merge tags, filled in per recipient at send time: {firstName|there}, {community}, {eventTitle|the session}, {eventDate}, {eventTime}, {eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {eventLocation}, {offerLink}, {offerPrice}, {offerEnds}, {productTitle|your purchase}, {productPrice}, {checkoutLink}, {offerCode}. Type one exactly as listed, in a heading, text, quote or button label, or in the subject or preview. Do not hand-type a greeting, a date, a place or a price that a tag can fill. The text after "|" inside a tag is the fallback used when that recipient has no value, and the tags above already carry one wherever a default helps. The link tags ({eventLink}, {eventUrl}, {offerLink}, {checkoutLink}) take no fallback and must be the WHOLE href of a button, never part of one: only the exact tag is ever substituted, so a tag pasted inside a URL is either refused here or delivered to members as literal text inside a link that goes nowhere. Event and offer tags need an email that an automation sends for that event or offer; in a standalone broadcast one of them with no fallback blocks the send. The checkout tags ({productPrice}, {checkoutLink}, {offerCode}) and the Their item card fill in only on an email a checkout_abandoned journey sends, which also fills the product name tag with the item they left. PHOTOS: an image, image-and-text, hero, saved layout photo slot or custom block image slot takes either a stock photo from Drry's own library (a stock:<name> or stock:lib/<id> key, listed by manage_email/stock_photos) or a key manage_email/read printed for this email (or one a saved block brings in), sent back unchanged. The coach's own uploads are never chosen here, only carried: a new one is uploaded in the console. A download's fileKey is carried the same way. A body that leaves out an uploaded photo or file this email holds is refused, because dropping it deletes it; remove one in the console.
